body.input: The following is a conversation with Jed Buckwald, a professor of history and a philosopher of science at Caltech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Interested especially in the development of scientific concepts and the instruments used to create and explore new effects and ideas in science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast and here is my conversation with Jed Buckwald.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Does science progress via paradigm shifts and revolutions as philosopher Thomas Kuhn said, or does it progress gradually? What do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, I got into this field because I was Tom Kuhn's research assistant 50 years ago, 52 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He pulled me into it out of physics instead. So I know his work pretty well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And in the years when I was at MIT running an institute, he was then in the philosophy department, used to come over all the time to the talks we held and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So what would I say about that? He, of course, developed his ideas a lot over the years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The thing that he's famous for, the structure of scientific revolutions came out in 62.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And as you just said, it offered an outline for what he called a paradigmatic structure, namely the notion that you have to look at what scientists do as forming a community of investigators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And that they're trying to solve various puzzles, as he would put it, that crop up, figuring out how this works, how that works and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And of course, they don't do it out of the blue. They do it within a certain framework. The framework can be pretty vague.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He called it a paradigm. And his notion was that eventually they run into troubles or what he called anomalies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That kind of cracks things. Somebody new comes along with a different way of doing it, etc.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Do I think things work that way? No, not really. Tom and I used to have lengthy discussions about that over the years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I do think there is a common structure that formulates both theoretical and experimental practices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And historians nowadays of science like to refer to scientific work as what scientists practice. It's almost craftsman-like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They can usually adapt in various ways. And I can give you all kinds of examples of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I once wrote a book on the origins of wave theory of light. And that is one of the paradigmatic examples that Tom used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Only it didn't work that way exactly. Because he thought that what happened was that the wave theory ran into trouble with a certain phenomenon, which it couldn't crack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, it turned out that, in fact, historically that phenomenon was actually not relevant later on to the wave theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And when the wave theory came in, the alternative to it, which had prevailed, which was Newton's views of light as particles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that it seemed couldn't explain what the wave theory could explain. Again, not true. Not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Much more complex than that. The wave theory offered the opportunity to deploy novel experimental and mathematical structures,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: which gave younger scientists, mathematicians and others, the opportunity to effect, manufacture, make new sorts of devices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's not that the alternative couldn't sort of explain these things, but it never was able to generate them de novo as novelties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In other words, if you think of it as something scientists wanted to progress in the sense of finding new stuff to solve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: then I think what often happens is that it's not so much that the prevailing view can't crack something as that it doesn't give you the opportunity to do new stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: When you say new stuff, are we referring to experimental science here or new stuff in the space of new theories?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Could be both. Could be both, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So how does that, can you maybe elaborate a little bit on the story of the wave?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Sure. The prevailing view of light, at least in France, where the wave theory really first took off,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: although it had been introduced in England by Thomas Young, the prevailing theory dates back to Newton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that light is a stream of particles and that refraction and reflection involve sort of repulsive and attractive forces

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that deflect and bend the paths of these particles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton was not able successfully to deal with the phenomenon of what happens when light goes past a knife's edge or a sharp edge, what we now call diffraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He had cooked up something about it that no mathematical structure could be applied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Thomas Young first, but really this guy named Augustin Fresnel in France, deployed, in Fresnel's case,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: rather advanced calculus forms of mathematics which enabled computations to be done

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and observations to be melded with these computations in a way that you could not do or see how to do with Newton.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Did that mean that the Newtonian explanation of what goes on in diffraction fails?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Not really. You can actually make it work, but you can't generate anything new out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Whereas using the mathematics of wave optics in respect to a particular phenomenon called polarization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: which ironically was discovered by partisans of Newton's way of doing things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: you were able to generate devices which reflect light in crystals, do various things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that the Newtonian way could accommodate only after the fact. They couldn't generate it from the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And so if you want to be somebody who is working a novel vein, which increasingly becomes the case with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: people who become what we now call physicists in the 1820s, 30s, and 40s in particular,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: then that's the direction you're going to go. But there were holdouts until the 1850s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I want to try to elaborate on the nature of the disagreement you have with Thomas Kuhn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So do you still believe in paradigm shifts? Do you still see that there is ideas that really have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: transformational effect on science? The nature of the disagreement has to do with how those

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: paradigm shifts come to be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: How they come to be and how they change. I certainly think they exist. How strong they may be at any

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: given time is maybe not quite as powerful as Tom thought in general, although towards the end of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: his life, he was beginning to develop different modifications of his original way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But I don't think that the changes happen quite so neatly, if you will, in reaction to novel

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: experimental observations. They get much more complex than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In terms of neatness, how much of science progresses by individual lone geniuses and how much

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: by the messy collaboration of competing and cooperating humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I don't think you can cut that with a knife to say it's this percent and that percent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's almost always the case that there are one or two or maybe three individuals who are sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: central to what goes on when things begin to shift. Are they inevitably and solely responsible for

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: what then begins to happen in a major way? I think not. It depends. You can go very far back with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: this, even into antiquity to see what goes on. The major locus we always talk about from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: beginning is if you're talking about Galileo's work on motion, for example, were there ways of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: accommodating it that others could adapt to without buying into the whole scheme? Yes. Did it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: eventually evolve and start convincing people because you could also do other things with it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that you couldn't otherwise do? Also, yes. Let me give you an example. The great French mathematician

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: philosopher Descartes, who was a mechanical philosopher, he believed the world was matter

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in motion, he never thought much of what Galileo had done in respect to motion because he thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: well, at best it's some sort of approximative scheme or something like that. But one of his

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: initial, I wouldn't call him a disciple, but follower who then broke with him in a number of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: ways was a man named Christian Huygens, who was, along with Newton, one of the two greatest

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: scientists of the 17th century. Huygens is older than Newton. Huygens nicely deployed Galilean

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: relationships in respect to motion to develop all sorts of things, including the first pendulum

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: governed clock and even figured out how to build one, which keeps perfect time, except it didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: work, but he had the mathematical structure for it. How well known is Huygens? Oh, very well known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Should I know him well? Yes, you should. Interesting. You should definitely know him. No, no, no, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Can we define should here? Okay. Because I don't. Right. So is this should like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: yeah, can you define should? Should means this. If you had taken up to a second year of physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: courses, you should, you would have heard his name because one of the fundamental principles

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in optics is called Huygens principle. Okay. Okay. Yeah. So I have, and I have heard his name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There you go. No, but I don't remember. But you don't remember. So, I mean, there's a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: different thing between names attached to principles and laws and so on that you sometimes let go of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You just remember the equations of the principles themselves and the personalities of science. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: there's certain personalities, certain human beings that stand out. And that's why there's a sense to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: which the lone inventor, the lone scientists is the way I personally, I mean, I think a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: people think about the history of science is these lone geniuses without them. The sense is if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: remove Newton from the picture, if you remove Galileo from the picture, then science would,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: there's almost a feeling like it would just have stopped there. Or at the very least, there's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: feeling like it would take much longer to develop the things that were developed. Is that a silly

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: way to look at the history? That's not entirely incorrect, I suppose. I find it difficult to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: believe that had Galileo not existed, that eventually someone like Huygens, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: given the context of the time, what was floating around in the belief structure concerning the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: nature of the world and so on, the developments in mathematics and whatnot, that sooner or later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: whether it would have been exactly the same or not, I cannot say. But would things have evolved?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Evolved? Yes. If we look at the long arc of history of science, from back when we were in the caves

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: trying to knock two rocks together or maybe make a basic tool to a long time from now, many centuries

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: from now when human civilization finally destroys itself. If you look at that history and imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: you're a historian at the end, like with the fire of the apocalypse coming upon us, and you look back

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at this time in the 21st century, how far along are we on that arc? Do you sense? Have we invented

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and discovered everything that's to be discovered or are we at like below 1%? You're going to get a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: lot of absurd questions today. I apologize. It's a lugubrious picture you're painting there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I don't even know what the word lugubrious means, but I love it. Lugubrious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, let me try and separate the question of whether we're all going to die in an apocalypse

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in several hundred years or not from the question of where science may be sitting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Take this as an assumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Okay. I find that hard to say. I find it hard to say because in the deepest sense of the term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: as it's usually deployed by philosophers of science today, I'm not fundamentally a realist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That is to say, I think our access to the inner workings of nature is inevitably mediated

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: by what we can do with the materials and factors around us. We can probe things in various ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Does that mean that I don't think that the standard model in quantum electrodynamics is in...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Of course not. I wouldn't even dream of saying such a thing. It can do a lot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: especially when it comes to figuring out what's happening in very large expensive

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: particle accelerators and applying results in cosmology and so on as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Do I think that we have inevitably probed the depths of reality through this? I do not agree

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: with Steven Weinberg who thinks we have about such things. Do I, on the other hand, think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the way in which science has been moving for the last 100 years, physics in particular is what I

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: have in mind, will continue on the same course? In that sense, I don't because we're not going

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to be building bigger and bigger and more and more expensive machines to rip apart particles

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in various ways. In which case, what are physicists going to do? They'll turn their attention to other

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: aspects. There are all sorts of things we've never explained about the material world. We don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: theories that go beyond a certain point for all sorts of things. Can we, for example, start with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the standard model and work our way up all the way to chemical transformations? You can make an

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: argument about it and you can justify things, but in chemistry, that's not the way people work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They work with much higher level quantum mechanical relationships and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: This notion of the deep theory to explain everything is a long-standing belief

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: which goes back pretty far, although I think it only takes its fullest form sometime towards the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: end of the 19th century. Maybe we just speak to that. You're referring to a hope, a dream,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: a reality of coming up with a theory of everything that explains everything. There's a very specific

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: thing that currently means in physics, is the unification of the laws of physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I'm sure in antiquity or before it meant maybe something else or is it always about physics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I think as you've implied, in physics there's a sense once you get to the theory of everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: you've understood everything, but there's a very deep sense in which you've actually understood

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: not very much at all. You've understood at that particular level how things work, but you don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: understand how the abstractions on top of abstractions form. Or you don't understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: how the abstractions on top of abstractions form all the way to the chemistry, to the human mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and the human societies and all those kinds of things. Maybe you can speak to the theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of everything in its history and comment on what the heck does that even mean, the theory of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: everything. Well, I don't think you can go back that far with something like that, maybe to the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at best to the 17th century. If you go back all the way in antiquity, there are of course discussions

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: about the nature of the world. But first of all, you have to recognize that the manipulative

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: character of physics and chemistry, the probing of, let me put it this way, we assume and have

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: known for a long time, I'll come back to when in a moment, that if I take a little device,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: which is really complicatedly made out of all kinds of things, and I put a piece of some material

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in it, and I monkey around with it and do all kinds of unnatural things to it, things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: wouldn't happen naturally, and I find out how it behaves and whatnot. And then I try and make an

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: argument about how that really applies even in the natural world without any artificial structures

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and so on. That's not a belief that was widely held by pretty much anyone until sometime maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in the 1500s. And when it was first held, it was held by people we now call alchemists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So alchemy was the first, the early days of the theory of everything, of a dream of a theory of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: everything. I would put it a little differently. I think it's more along the way a dream that by

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: probing nature in artificially constructed ways, we can find out what's going on deep down there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So that was, that's distinct from science being an observing thing where you observe nature

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and you study nature. You're talking about probing, like messing with nature to understand it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Indeed I am, but that of course is the very essence of experimental science. You have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: manipulate nature to find out things about it, and then you have to convince others that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: haven't so manipulated it that what you've done is to produce what amounts to fake,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: artifactual behavior that doesn't really hold purely naturally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So where are we today in your sense to jump around a little bit with the theory of everything?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Maybe a quick kind of sense you have about the journey in the world of physics that we're taking

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: towards the theory of everything. Well, I'm of course not a practicing physicist. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I was trained in physics at Princeton a long time ago. Until Thomas Kuhn stole you away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: More or less. I was taking graduate courses in those days in general relativity. I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: an undergraduate, but I moved up and then I took a course with him. Well, you made the mistake of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: being compelled by charismatic philosophers and never looked back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I suppose so in a way. From what I understand, talking especially to my friends at Caltech,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: like Kip Thorne and others, the fundamental notion is that actually the laws that even at

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the deepest level we can sort of divine and work with in the universe that we inhabit

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: are perhaps quite unique to this particular universe as it formed at the Big Bang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The question is, how deep does it go? If you are very mathematically inclined, the prevailing

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: notion for several decades now has been what's called string theory, but that has not been able

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to figure a way to generate probative experimental evidence, although it's pretty good apparently

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at accommodating things. Then the question is, what's before the Big Bang? Actually,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the word before doesn't mean anything given the nature of time, but why do we have the laws

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that prevail in our universe? Well, there is a notion that those laws prevail in our universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: because if they didn't, we wouldn't be here. That's a bit of a cyclical but nevertheless,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: a compelling definition. There's all kinds of things like it seems like the unification

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of those laws could be discovered by looking inside of a black hole because you get both

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the general relativity and the quantum mechanics, quantum field theory in there. Experimentally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of course, there's a lot of interesting ideas. We can't really look close to the Big Bang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We can't look that far back. Caltech and MIT will lie go looking at gravitational waves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: perhaps allows us to march backwards and so on. It's a really exciting space. There's of course

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the theory of everything, like with a lot of things in science, captivates the dreams of those who are

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: perhaps completely outside of science. It's the dream of discovering the key to the nature of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: how everything works. That feels deeply human. That's perhaps the thing, the basic elements of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: what makes up a scientist in the end is that curiosity, that longing to understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Let me ask, you mentioned a disagreement with Weinberg on reality. Could you elaborate a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: bit? Obviously, I don't disagree with Steve Weinberg on physics itself. I wouldn't know

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: enough to even begin to do that. Clearly, he's one of the founders of the standard model and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It works to a level of accuracy that no physical theorist can ever understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: A level of accuracy that no physical theory has ever worked at before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I suppose the question in my mind is something that in one way could go back to the philosopher

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Immanuel Kant in the 18th century, namely, can we really ever convince ourselves that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: come to grips with something that is not in itself knowable to us by our senses or even except in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: most remote way through the complex instruments that we make as to what it is that underlies

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: everything? Can we corral it with mathematics and experimental structures? Yes. Do I think that a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: particular way of corralling nature will inevitably play itself out? I don't know. It always has.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I'll put it to you that way. The basic question is, can we know reality? Is that the con question? Is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that the Weinberg question? We humans, with our brains, can we comprehend reality? Sounds like a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: very trippy question because a lot of it rests on definitions of know and comprehend and reality, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: get to the bottom of it. Turtles on top of turtles. Can we get to the bottom turtle

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and say hello? Well, maybe I can put it to you this way in a way that I often begin discussions

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in a class on the history of science and so on and say, I'm looking at you. You are in fact a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: figment of my imagination. You have a messed up imagination, yes. Well, what do I mean by that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: If I were a dragonfly looking at you, whatever my nervous system would form by way of a perceptual

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: structure would clearly be utterly different from what my brain and perceptual system

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: altogether is forming when I look at you. Who's right? Is it me or the dragonfly?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, the dragonfly is certainly very impressive, so I don't know. But yes, the observer matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, what is that supposed to tell us about objective reality? Well, I think it means that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: it's very difficult to get beyond the constructs that our perceptual system is leading us to. When

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: we make apparatus and devices and so on, we're still making things, the results of which are

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the outputs of which we process perceptually in various ways. An analogy I like to use with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the students sometimes is this. All right, they all have their laptops open in front of them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of course. I've sent them something to read and I say, okay, click on it and open it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So PDF opens up. I said, what are you looking at? They said, well, I'm looking at the paper that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: sent me. I said, no, you're not. What you're looking at is a stream of light coming off

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: LEDs or LCDs coming off a screen. And I said, what happens when you use your mouse and move that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: fake piece of paper on the screen around? What are you doing? You're not moving a piece of paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: around, are you? You're moving a construct around, a construct that's being processed

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: so that our perceptual system can interact with it in the way we interact with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: pieces of paper. But it's not real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So are there things outside of the reach of science? Can you maybe, as an example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: talk about consciousness? I'm asking for a friend, trying to figure this thing out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, boy, I mean, I read a fair bit about that, but I certainly can't really say much about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I'm a materialist in the deepest sense of the term. I don't think there is anything out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: except material structures which interact in various ways. Do I have to say that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I think, for example, that this bottle of water is conscious? No, I do not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Although how would I know? I can't talk to it. It's a hypothesis you have. It's an opinion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: an educated opinion that may be very wrong. Well, I know that you're conscious because I

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: can interact directly with you. But am I? Well, unless you're a figment of my imagination,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Or I'm a robot that's able to generate the illusion of consciousness effectively enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to facilitate a good conversation, because we humans do want to pretend that we're talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to other conscious beings, because that's how we respect them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: If it's not conscious, we don't respect them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We're not good at talking to robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Of course, we generalize from our own inner sense, which is the kind of thing Descartes

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: said from the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We generalize from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But I do think that consciousness must be something, whatever it is, that occurs as

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: a result of some particular organizational structure of material elements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Does materialism mean that it's all within the reach of science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: My sense would be that especially as neuroscience progresses more and more, and at Caltech we

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: just built a whole neuroscience arena and so on, and as more knowledge is gained about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the ways in which animals, when they behave, what patterns show up at various parts of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the brain and nervous system, and perhaps extending it to humans eventually as well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: we'll get more of a handle on what brain activity is associated with experiences that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: as humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Can we move from the brain activity to the experiences in terms of our person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: No, you can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Brain is perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That's a hypothesis once again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Maybe consciousness is just one of the laws of physics that's yet to be discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Maybe it permeates all matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Maybe it's as simple as trying to plug it in and plug into the ability to generate and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: control that kind of law of physics that would crack open, or we would understand that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: bottled water is in fact conscious, just much less conscious than us humans, and then we

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: would be able to then generate beings that are more conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, that'll be unfortunate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I'd have to stop drinking the water after that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Every time you take a sip, there's a little bit of a suffering going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What do you think is the most interesting, beautiful moments in the history of science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What stands out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Then we can pull at that thread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, I like to think of events that have a major impact and involve both beautiful

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: conceptual, mathematical, if we're talking physical structures work, and are associated

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: as well with probing experimental situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Among my favorites is one of the most famous, which was the young Isaac Newton's work with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the colors produced when you pass sunlight through a prism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Why do I like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's not profoundly mathematical in one sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It doesn't need it initially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It needs the following though, which begins to show you, I think, a little bit about what

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: gets involved when you've got a smart individual who's trying to monkey around with stuff and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: finds new things about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: First let me say that the notion, the prevailing notion going back to antiquity was that colors

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: are produced in a sense by modifying or tinting white light, that they're modifications of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: white light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In other words, the colors are not in the sunlight in any way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now, what Newton did following experiments done by Descartes before him, who came to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: very different conclusions, he took a prism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You might ask, where do you get prisms in the 1660s?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That's the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: County fairs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They were very popular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They were pretty crude with bubbles in them and everything, but they produced colors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: so you could buy them at county fairs and things, very popular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They were modifying the white light to create colors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, they were creating colors from it, well known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What he did was the following.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was by this time, even though he's very young, a very good mathematician.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He could use the then known laws for how light behaves when it goes through glass to calculate

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: what should happen if you took light from the sun, passed it from a hole through a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: hole, then hit the prism, goes out of the prism, strikes a wall a long distance away

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and makes a splash of light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Never mind the colors for a moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Makes a splash of light there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was very smart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: First of all, he abstracts from the colors themselves, even though that's what everybody's

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214
