body.input: You know, you could go blind, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But if they're working properly, you get the actual qualities of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now that break, which is occurring towards the end of the 16th century and is most visible

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in Descartes is the break between conceiving that the qualities of the world are very different

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: from the qualities that we perceive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That in fact, the qualities of the world consist almost entirely in shapes of various kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and maybe hard particles or whatever, but not colors, not sounds, not smells, not softness

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and hardness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They're not in the world, they're in us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That break Newton is picking up as he reads Descartes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He's going to disagree with a lot in Descartes, but that break he is among other things picking

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: up very strongly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And that underlies a lot of the way he works later on when he becomes skeptical of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: evidence provided by the senses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Yeah, that's actually, I don't know, the way you're describing it is so powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It just makes me realize how liberating that is as a scientist, as somebody who's trying

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to understand reality, that our senses are not to be trusted, that reality is to be investigated

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: through tools that are beyond our senses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Yes, or that improve our senses in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That's pretty powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That is for a human being, that's like Einstein level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: For a human being to realize I can't trust my own senses at that time, that's pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: trippy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's coming in, it's coming in and I think it arises probably a fair number of decades

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: before that, perhaps in part with all chemical experimentation and manipulations, that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: have to go through elaborate structures to produce things and ways you think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But let me give you an example that I think you might find interesting because it involves

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that guy named Hook that Newton had an argument with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And he had lots of arguments with Hook, although Hook was a very clever guy and gave him some

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: things that stimulated him later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Anyway, Hook, who was argumentative and he really was convinced that the only way to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: gain real knowledge of nature is through carefully constructed devices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And he was an expert mechanic, if you will, at building such things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now there was a rather wealthy man in Danzig by the name of Hevelius, Latinized name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was a brewer in town and he had become fascinated with the telescope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: This is 30 years or so, 20 or 30 years after the telescope had moved out and become more

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: common.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He built a large observatory on the top of his brewery, actually, and working with his

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: wife, they used these very elaborately constructed grass and metal instruments to make observations

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of positions of the stars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And he published a whole new catalog of where the stars are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And he claimed it was incredibly accurate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He claimed it was so accurate that nothing had ever come close to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Hook reads this and he says, wait a minute, you didn't use a telescope here of any kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: because what's the point?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Unless you do something to the telescope, all you see are dots with stars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You just use your eye, your eyes can't be that good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So what did Hook do to prove this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He said, what you should have done is you should have put a little device in the telescope

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that lets you measure distances between these dots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You didn't do that and because you didn't, there's no way you could have been that good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: At two successive meetings of the Royal Society, he hauls the members out into the courtyard

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and he takes a card and he makes successive black and white stripes on the card and he

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: pastes the card up on a wall and he takes them one by one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He says, now move back looking at it, presumably with one eye until you can't tell the black

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: ones from the white stripes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He says, that I can then measure the distance, I can see the angles, I can give a number

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: then for what is the best possible, what we would call perceptual acuity of human vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And it turned out, he thought, to be something like 10 or more times worse than this guy

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Hevelius had claimed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So obviously says Hook Hevelius, well, years ago I calculated Hevelius's numbers and so

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: on using modern tables from NASA and so on and they are even more accurate than Hevelius

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: claimed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But worse than that, the Royal Society sent a young astronomer named Halley over to Danzig

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to work with him and Halley writes back and he says, I couldn't believe it, but he taught

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: me how to do it and I could get just as good as he, how is it possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well here, this shows you something very interesting about experiments, perception and everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Hook was right, but he was also wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was wrong for the right reasons and he was right for the wrong reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And what do I mean by that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What he actually found was the number for what we now call 20-20 vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You can't tell except a few people much better than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But he was observing the wrong thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What Hevelius was observing was a bright dot, a star moving past a pointer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Our eyes are rather similar to frogs' eyes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You know, I'm sure you've heard the story, if I hold a dead fly on a string in front

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of a frog and don't move it, the frog pays no attention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: As soon as I move the fly, the frog immediately tongue-lots out because the visual system

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of the frog responds to motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So does ours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And our acuity for distinguishing motion from statics, five or more times better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Damn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And of course, maybe you can comment on their understanding of the human perceptual system

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at the time was probably really terrible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I've recently been working with almost as a fun side thing with vision scientists and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: peripheral vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's a beautiful complex mess, that whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We still don't understand all the weird ways that human perception works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And they were probably terrible at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They probably didn't even have any conceptual peripheral vision or the fovea or basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They had some, I mean, because actually it was Newton himself who probed a lot of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: For instance, the young Newton trying to work his way around what's going on with colors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: wanted to try and distinguish colors that occur through natural processes out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and colors that are a result of our eyes not operating right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You know what he did?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's a famous thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He took a stick and he stuck that stick under his lower eyelid and pushed up on his eyeball.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And what that did was produced colored circles at diametrically opposite positions of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: stick in the eyeball.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And he moved it around to see how they moved, trying to distinguish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Legit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I always have to tell my students, don't do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Or do it if you want to be great and remembered by human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There's a lot of equivalent to sticking a stick into your eye in modern day that may

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: pay off in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: As a small aside, is the Newton and the Apple story true?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Was it a different fruit?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: As a colleague of mine named Simon Schaffer in England once said on a NOVA program that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: we were both on, the role of fruit in the history of science has been vastly exaggerated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So was there any, I mean, to zoom out, moments of epiphany?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Is there something to moments of epiphany?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Again, this is the paradigm shift versus the gradualism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There is a shift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's a much more complex one than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: As it happens, a colleague of mine and I are writing a paper right now on one of the aspects

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of these things based on the work that many of our colleagues have done over the last

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: 30 and 40 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Let me try and see if I could put it to you this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton, until the early 1670s and probably really until a fair time after that, first

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of all was not very interested in questions of motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He was working actually in all chemical relationships or what is called by historians, chemistry,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: a kind of early modern chemical structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Things of ours at Indiana have even reproduced the amalgams that...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Anyway, his way of thinking about motion involved a certain set of relationships which was not

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: conducive to any application that would yield computationally direct results for things

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: like planetary motions, which he wasn't terribly interested in anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He enters a correspondence with his original nemesis Robert Hooke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Hooke says, well, have you ever thought about...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Then Hooke tells him a certain way you might think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: When Newton hears that, he recognizes that there is a way to inject time that would enable

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: him to solve certain problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's not that there was anything he thought before that was contrary to that way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's just that that particular technical insight was not something that for a lot of reasons

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that are complex had never occurred to him at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That sent him a different way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But to answer your question about the Apple business, which is always about gravity and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the moon and all of that being...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The reason there is that the idea that what goes on here in the neighborhood of the earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and what goes on at the moon, let us say, remind the sun and the planet, can be due

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to a direct relationship between the earth, let's say, and the moon is contrary to fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: beliefs held by many of the mechanical philosophers, as they're called at the time, in which everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: has to involve at least a sequence of direct contacts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It has to be something between here and there that's involved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And Hooke, probably not thinking terribly deeply about it based on what he said, along

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: with others like the architect and mathematician Christopher Wren, hearken back to the notion

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that, well, maybe there is a kind of magnetic relationship between the moon and maybe the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: planets and the earth and gravity and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Vague, but establishing a direct connection somehow, however it's happening, forget about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton wouldn't have cared about that if that's all they said, but it was when Hooke mentioned

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: this different way of thinking about the motion, a way he could certainly have thought of because

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: it does not contradict anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton is a brilliant mathematician and he could see that you could suddenly start to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: do things with that that you otherwise wouldn't connect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: This led eventually to another controversy with Hooke in which Hooke said, well, after

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton published his great Principia, I gave him how to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And then Newton, of course, got ticked off about that and said, well, listen to this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I did everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And because he had a picayune little idea, he thinks he can take credit for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So his ability to play with his ideas mathematically is what solidified the initial intuition that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: you could have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Was that the first time he was born the idea that you have action at a distance, that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: can have forces without contact, which is another revolutionary idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I would say that in the sense of dealing with the mechanics of force-like effects considered

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to act at some distance, it is novel with both Hooke and Newton at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The notion that two things might interact at a distance with one another without direct

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: contact, that goes back to antiquity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Only there it would have thought of more as a sympathetic reaction to a magnet and a piece

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of iron.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They have a kind of mutual sympathy for one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Like what, love?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What are we talking about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, actually, they do sometimes talk like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That is love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: See, now I talk like that all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I think love is somehow in consciousness or forces of physics that yet to be discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now there is the other side of things, which is calculus that you began to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So Newton brought a lot of things to this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: One of them is calculus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What is calculus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: And what was Newton's role in bringing it to life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What was it like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What was the story of bringing calculus to this world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, since the publication starting many decades ago by Tom Whiteside, who is now deceased,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of Newton's mathematical papers, we know a lot about how he was pushing things and how

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: he was developing things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's a complex question to say what calculus is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Calculus is the set of mathematical techniques that enable you to investigate what we now

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: call functions, mathematical functions, which are continuous, that is, that are not formed

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: out of discrete sets like the counting numbers, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton, there were already procedures for solving problems involving such things as

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: finding areas under curves and tangents to curves by using geometrical structures, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: only for certain limited types of curves, if you will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton as a young man, we know this is what happened, is looking at a formula which involves

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: an expansion in separate terms, polynomial terms, as we say, for certain functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I know I don't want to get complicated here about this, and he realizes it could be generalized,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and he tries the generalization, and that leads him to an expansion formula called the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: binomial theorem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That enables him to move ahead with the notion that if I take something that has a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: value and I add a little bit to it, and I use this binomial theorem and expand things

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: out, I can begin to do new things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The new things that he begins to do leads him to a recognition that the calculations

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of areas and the calculations of tangents to curves are reciprocal to one another, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the procedures that he develops is a particular form of the calculus in which he considers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: small increments and then continuous flows and changes of curves and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We have relics of it in physics today, the notation in which you put a dot over a variable

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: indicating the rate of change of the variable, that's Newton's original type of notation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The dot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Yeah, the dot notation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Possibly independently of Newton because he didn't publish this thing, although he became

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: quite well known as quite a brilliant young man, in part because people heard about his

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: work and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: When another young man by the name of Gottfried Leibniz visited London and he heard about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: these things, it is said that he independently develops his form of the calculus, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: actually the form we use today, both in notation and perhaps in certain fundamental ways of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It has remained a controversial point as to where exactly and how much independently Leibniz

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: did it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Leibniz aficionados think and continue to maintain he did it completely independently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Newton, when he became president of the Royal Society, put together a group to go on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: attack saying, no, he must have taken everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: We don't know, but I will tell you this, about 25 or so years ago, a scholar who's a professor

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at Indiana now named Domenico Melli got his hands on a Leibniz manuscript called the 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Tammun, which was Leibniz's attempt to produce an alternative to Newton's mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It comes to some conclusions that you have in the Newton's mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, he published that, but Melli got the manuscript.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What Melli found out was that Leibniz reverse engineered the Principia and cooked it backwards

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: so that he could get the results he wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: That was for the mechanics, so that means his mind allows for that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Some people-

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You're breaking some news today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You're starting some old drama.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Some people think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I think most historians of mathematics do not agree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: A friend of mine, rather well-known physicist, unfortunately died a couple of years ago named

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Mike Nauenberg at UC Santa Cruz, had some evidence along those lines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Didn't pass mustard with many of my friends who are historians of math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In fact, I edit with a historian of math, a technical journal, and we were unable to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: publish it in there because we couldn't get it through any of our colleagues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But I remain suspicious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: What is it about those tense relationships and that kind of drama?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Einstein doesn't appear to have much of that drama.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Nobody claimed, I haven't heard claims that they've, perhaps because it's such crazy ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of any of his major inventions, major ideas being those that are basically, I came up

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: with it first or independently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There's not, as far as I'm aware, not many people talk about general relativity, especially

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: in those terms, but with Newton, that was the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Is that just a natural outgrowth of how science works?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There's going to be personalities that, I'm not saying this about Lenin, but maybe I am,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: that there's people who steal ideas for the, because of ego, because of all those kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I don't think it's all that common, frankly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The Newton hook, Leibniz, Contratombs, and so on, well, you're at the beginnings of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: lot of things there and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: These are difficult and complex times as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: These are times in which science as an activity pursued by other than, let us say, interested

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: aristocrats is becoming something somewhat different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's not a professional community of investigators in the same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's also a period in which procedures and rules of practice are being developed to avoid

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: attacking one another directly and pulling out a sword to cut off the other guy's head

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: if he disagrees with you and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So it's a very different period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Controversies happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: People get angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I can think of a number of others, including in the development of optics in the 19th century

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It can get hot under the collar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Sometimes one character who's worked an area extensively, whether they've come up with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: something terribly novel or not, and somebody else kind of moves in and does completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: different and novel things, the first guy gets upset about it because he's sort of muscled

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: into what I thought was my area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: You find that sort of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: But do you have examples of cases where it worked out well, like that competition is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: good for the progress of science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Yeah, it almost always is good in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Just painful for the individuals involved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Can be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It doesn't have to be nasty, although sometimes it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So on the space, for the example of optics, could you comment on that one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Well, yeah, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: I mean, there are several, but I could give you...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: All right, so I'll give you this example that probably is the most pertinent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: The first polytechnic school, like MIT or Caltech, was actually founded in France during

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It exists today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: It's the Ecole Polytechnique.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Two people who were there were two young men in the 90s, 1790s, named on the one hand Francois

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux and the other Jean-Baptiste Biot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: They both lived a long time, well into the 1850s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux became a major administrator of science, and Biot's career started to peter out after

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: about the late teens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now they are sent on an expedition, which was one of the expeditions involving measuring

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: things to start the metric system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: There's a lot more to that story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Anyway, they come back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux gets separated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He's captured by pirates, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Wounds up in Tangier, escapes, is captured again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Everybody thinks he's dead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He gets back to Paris and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He's greeted as a hero and whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In the meantime, Biot has pretty much published some of the stuff that he's done, and Aragaux

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: doesn't get much credit for it, and Aragaux starts to get very angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Biot is known for this kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So Aragaux, anyway, Biot starts investigating a new phenomenon in optics involving something

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: called polarization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He writes all kinds of stuff on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux looks into this and decides to write some things as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Actually, Biot gets mostly interested in it when he finds out that Aragaux is doing stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Now Biot is actually the better scientist in a lot of ways, but Aragaux is furious about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: this, so furious that he actually demands and forces the leader of French science, La

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Place, the Marquis de La Place, and cohorts to write a note in the published journal saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: oh, excuse us, actually, Aragaux, et cetera, et cetera, blah, blah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So Aragaux continues to just hold this antipathy and fear of Biot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: So what happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: In 1815, Napoleon is finished at Waterloo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: A young Frenchman by the name of Augustin Fresnel, who was in the army, is going back

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: to his home on the north coast of France in Normandy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He passes through Paris.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux is friends with Fresnel's uncle, who was the head of the École des Beaux-Arts

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Anyway, Fresnel is already interested in certain things in light, and he talks to Aragaux.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Aragaux tells him a few things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: Fresnel goes home, and Fresnel is a brilliant experimenter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He observes things, and he's a very good mathematician, calculates things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He writes something up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jed Buchwald: Isaac Newton and the Philosophy of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #214

body.input: He sends it to Aragaux.
