body.input: So in contrast to Tolstoy, let me ask you about Emma Goldman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: You wrote that if anarchism believed in rulers, then Emma Goldman would be the undisputed

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: queen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So what ideas define her flavor of anarchism would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Emma was really an old school radical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: She was a radical among radicals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I don't know what ideas, I mean, what would the ideas would find her was anarchism, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: There's the violence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I mean, she was more open to the idea of violent opposition versus somebody like Tolstoy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Oh, sure, for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So basically, Emma and Alexander Berkman, their mentor was someone named Johann Most.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And Johann Most was a very early free speech, not very early, but he was a free speech concern

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: because he published a pamphlet in Europe that was translated in the States about how

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: to build dynamite because his idea was, all right, you have this oppressive government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: this oppressive police force that use batons and bolts against us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: The only way for us as the working class to level the playing field is through dynamite

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: and here's how you build it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So the question is, all right, is this something that could be allowed to be legal now that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: you're allowing the layman in his own house build bombs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So Johann Most, basically they had a big parting of ways because when Alexander Berkman tried

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: to assassinate Frick, Johann said, no, no, no, this is not something I'm for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And in fact, they thought with this assassination, this failed assassination, this would be the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: thing that's fired off the revolution because you had this strike, the Pinkerton's involved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Pinkerton's getting killed, Strikers are getting killed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: This is what Marx predicted, they're going to light the spark and everything's going

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: to come falling down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He ends up going to jail for 13 years instead, Alexander Berkman does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And then Goldman and Berkman had a big issue because when Leon Solgaz killed McKinley in

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: 1901, it's kind of humorous in retrospect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He gets arrested and they're like, why'd you kill the president?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He goes, I was radicalized by Emma Goldman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And she's like, oh, damn it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So she's on the run.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: She's like, I don't even know this guy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And she made the point about like, why is it worse than the president being killed and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: somebody else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: We're all equal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And you would think if you're against capitalism against the ruling class, this would be your

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: first target.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: But Berkman, who went to jail, who tried to assassinate someone, he had said, McKinley,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: this is your villain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He's just a party hack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He's like a symptom of the times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: This is foolish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And Goldman disagreed with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He said it wasn't necessarily justified, but it may have done something that was defensible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So the three of them had their differences on the use of violence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And in fact, when she came back from Russia and was denouncing it in her book, My Dissolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: in Russia, My Fourth Dissolution in Russia, the last chapter, she goes, look, I'm not

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: saying I'm against violence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: When there's the revolution comes, we're going to have to use force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: She goes, but it's not the force of the state against the working class, against the masses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: This is exactly what we're opposed to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: This is a complete obscenity to our principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So that was interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: The fact that she was a her periodical mother earth was a clearinghouse for many prominent

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: ideas of the day that weren't anarchist, but were certainly radical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So she was a bit, and also she was like tiny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: She was like five one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So to have this little woman who was so feisty and talk back to Lenin, talk back to Lenin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: she took on Lenin, Woodrow Wilson, Jander Hoover was the one who deported her.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Someone who just, and the thing is you have to be careful because I think just like war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: it's very easy to glamorize violence and to regard it as something admirable or heroic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: like you're fighting for the cause.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: But if you take it out of the romanticism, you're like, you're killing someone who had

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: You are killing someone with a family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: If you're going to shoot someone, they're probably going to retaliate twice as hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: This sings its own song and this is a very dangerous road you're going down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So you really need to be careful about what you're preaching here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And she kind of had this mixed feelings about it, but that is certainly not Emma Goldman

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: and her best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Emma Goldman and her best was about the ultimate freedom of the individual, of caring about

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: people who are desperately poor, who despised the corporate idea that we all have to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: made cookie cutters and be interchangeable and all have to start work at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And basically our entire lives slave for corporation that have nothing to show for it while they

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: get wealthy and you have no opportunity for either productive work or creative work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So that I think the valorization of kind of the lowest of the low is something I find

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: very admirable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: There's a quote of hers, which I think even for those of us who are for property rights,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: left anarchism at its best, which she goes, go and ask for work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: If they don't give you work, ask for bread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: If they don't give you bread, take bread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So the idea that like, if you're that poor and you're honestly trying to work and work

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: isn't available and you steal food to keep alive that you shouldn't feel guilt about

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: it, I don't know that I would disagree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I think that there's something to be said at that point where it's just like, if property

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: rights come between that and mass starvation, it's going to be very hard for anyone to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: the case for property rights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Now, my argument is when you have free enterprise, food becomes so plentiful that now obesity

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: is an issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: But at the time she did not have, of course, have that data to access.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Is there somebody you left out from the book that you thought about leaving in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Like some interesting figures?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Yeah, there's a couple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So Chomsky would have been one, of course, because he's one of the biggest anarchist

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: thinkers in contemporary times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I was on the fence about Herbert Spencer because he's not an anarchist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Chris Williamson's reading the chapter for the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He coined the term survival of the fittest and the chapter is called The Right to Ignore

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: the State from his book Social Statics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: It was deleted from later editions, but people found it and reprinted it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And Randolph Bourne, he was an early progressive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: He was the only one or one of the very few fighting against entering the great war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And he had an essay called War is the Health of the State, which is basically about how

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: states love war because it gives them an excuse to increase their power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And it's very hard to argue against increasing state power in a time of war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: But since he was not himself an anarchist and there was plenty anti-war in there already,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I didn't include him, but those would be the ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Is there some people that you think the public would be surprised to learn that they are

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: at least in part anarchists?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I saw that Howard Zinn is supposed to be an anarchist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I mean, is there like just like Tolstoy is an anarchist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Is there some people like that that you think in our modern life that would be surprised

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: to learn they're anarchists?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I can't think of any off the top of my head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I mean, you could say Carl Hess, who was like Barry Goldwater's speechwriter from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: I mean, I think a lot of people would not ascribe to that term, but are certainly informed

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: with this complete distrust of all authority.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Murray Rothbard had an essay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: If I didn't include Anatomy of the State, I was going to include this one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: It's much, much shorter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And his question was who are our allies and who are our enemies?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And the point he made is there's lots of people who would call themselves anarchists who are

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: of little use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Whereas someone who is still like a minarchist or for government, but genuinely hates the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: question Rothbard had is if there's a button and you could press it, you would end the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Would you press it so fast your finger would get a blister?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: Those are allies, even if they're somewhat of a minarchist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: So I think that is kind of a better lens of looking at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: And I don't think anyone needs to really ascribe to anarchism as a whole ideology in so far

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: as you're seeing right now, many people in certain fringe elements are just essentially

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Jack Kerouac that perhaps begins to explain

body.input: the nature of and the reasons for my friendship with Mr. Michael Malus.

body.input: The only people for me are the mad ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: Totalitarianism and Anarchy | Lex Fridman Podcast #200

body.input: You've mentioned that in your childhood,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: you've developed a fascination with physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: especially the theory of relativity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and that Einstein was also a childhood hero to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: What aspect of Einstein's genius, the nature of his genius,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: do you think was essential

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: for discovering the theory of relativity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: You know, Einstein was a hero to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and I'm sure to many people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: because he was able to make, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: a major, major contribution to physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: with simplifying a bit just a Gedanken experiment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: a thought experiment, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: imagining communication with lights

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: between a stationary observer and somebody on a train.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And I thought, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: the fact that just with the force of his thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: of his thinking, of his mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: he could get to something so deep

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: in terms of physical reality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: how time depend on space and speed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: It was something absolutely fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: It was the power of intelligence, the power of the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Do you think the ability to imagine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to visualize as he did, as a lot of great physicists do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: do you think that's in all of us human beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: or is there something special

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to that one particular human being?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: I think, you know, all of us can learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and have in principle similar breakthroughs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: There are lessons to be learned from Einstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: the Eidgenossische Technische Hochschule in Zurich,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: in physics, and he was the worst of the five.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: The only one who did not get an academic position

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: when he graduated, when he finished his PhD,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and he went to work, as everybody knows,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: for the patent office.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And so it's not so much that he worked

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: for the patent office,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: but the fact that obviously he was smart,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: but he was not a top student,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: obviously he was the anti-conformist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: He was not thinking in the traditional way

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that probably his teachers

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and the other students were doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So there is a lot to be said about, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: trying to be, to do the opposite,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: or something quite different from what other people

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: are doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Never buy if everybody's buying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And also true for science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So you've also mentioned, staying on the theme of physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that you were excited at a young age

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: by the mysteries of the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that physics could uncover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Such, as I saw mentioned, the possibility of time travel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So the most out of the box question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: I think I'll get to ask today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: do you think time travel is possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Well, it would be nice if it were possible right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: You know, in science, you never say no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: But your understanding of the nature of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: It's very likely that it's not possible to travel in time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: We may be able to travel forward in time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: if we can, for instance, freeze ourselves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: or, you know, go on some spacecraft

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: traveling close to the speed of light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: But in terms of actively traveling, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: back in time, I find probably very unlikely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So do you still hold the underlying dream

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: of the engineering intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that we will build systems that are able

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to do such huge leaps, like discovering

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: the kind of mechanism that would be required

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to travel through time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Do you still hold that dream,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: or echoes of it from your childhood?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: You know, I don't think whether,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: there are certain problems that probably cannot be solved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: depending what you believe about the physical reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Like, you know, maybe totally impossible

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to create energy from nothing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: or to travel back in time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: But about making machines that can think

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: as well as we do, or better, or more likely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: especially in the short and midterm,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: help us think better, which is in a sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: is happening already with the computers we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And it will happen more and more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Well, that I certainly believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And I don't see in principle why computers at some point

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: could not become more intelligent than we are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: although the word intelligence is a tricky one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and one who should discuss what I mean with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And intelligence, consciousness, words like love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: is all these are very, need to be disentangled.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So you've mentioned also that you believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: the problem of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: is the greatest problem in science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: greater than the origin of life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: and the origin of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: You've also, in the talk I've listened to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: said that you're open to arguments against you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So what do you think is the most captivating aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: of this problem of understanding the nature of intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Why does it captivate you as it does?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Well, originally, I think one of the motivation

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that I had as, I guess, a teenager,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: when I was infatuated with theory of relativity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: was really that I found that there was the problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: of time and space and general relativity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: but there were so many other problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: of the same level of difficulty and importance

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that I could, even if I were Einstein,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: it was difficult to hope to solve all of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So what about solving a problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: whose solution allow me to solve all the problems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: And this was, what if we could find the key

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: to an intelligence 10 times better or faster than Einstein?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: So that's sort of seeing artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: as a tool to expand our capabilities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: but is there just an inherent curiosity in you

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: in just understanding what it is in here

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: that makes it all work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Tomaso Poggio: Brains, Minds, and Machines | Lex Fridman Podcast #13

body.input: Yes, absolutely, you're right.
