metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's a field defining textbook, as many people are aware, that you wrote with Stuart Russell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: How has the book changed and how have you changed in relation to it from the first edition to the second to the third and now fourth edition as you work on it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So it's been a lot of years, a lot of changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: One of the things changing from the first to maybe the second or third was just the rise of computing power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think in the first edition, we said, here's predicate logic, but that only goes so far because pretty soon you have millions of short little predicate expressions and they couldn't possibly fit in memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we're going to use first order logic that's more concise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then we quickly realized, oh, predicate logic is pretty nice because there are really fast SAT solvers and other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And look, there's only millions of expressions and that fits easily into memory or maybe even billions fit into memory now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that was a change of the type of technology we needed just because the hardware expanded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Even to the second edition, the resource constraints were loosened significantly for the second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that was early 2000s second edition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So 95 was the first and then 2000, 2001 or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then moving on from there, I think we're starting to see that again with the GPUs and then more specific type of machinery like the DPUs and you're seeing custom ASICs and so on for deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we're seeing another advance in terms of the hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Then I think another thing that we especially noticed this time around is in all three of the first editions, we kind of said, well, we're going to find AI as maximizing expected utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And you tell me your utility function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And now we've got 27 chapters where the cool techniques for how to optimize that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think in this edition, we're saying more, you know what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Maybe that optimization part is the easy part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And the hard part is deciding what is my utility function?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What do I want?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And if I'm a collection of agents or a society, what do we want as a whole?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You touch that topic in this edition, you get a little bit more into utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That's really interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: On a technical level, we're almost pushing the philosophical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I guess it is philosophical, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we've always had a philosophy chapter, which I was glad to that was a very interesting one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Glad that we were supporting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And now it's less kind of the Chinese room type argument and more of these ethical and societal type issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we get into the issues of fairness and bias and just the issue of aggregating utilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So how do you encode human values into a utility function?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Is this something that you can do purely through data in a learned way or is there some systematic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Obviously, there's no good answers yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: There's just beginnings to this, to even opening the doors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: There is no one answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yes, there are techniques to try to learn that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we talk about inverse reinforcement learning, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So reinforcement learning, you take some actions, you get some rewards and you figure out what actions you should take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: In inverse reinforcement learning, you observe somebody taking actions and you figure out, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: this must be what they were trying to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: If they did this action, it must be because they wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Of course, there's restrictions to that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So lots of people take actions that are self-destructive or they're suboptimal in certain ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you don't want to learn that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You want to somehow learn the perfect actions rather than the ones they actually take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that's a challenge for that field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Then another big part of it is just kind of theoretical of saying what can we accomplish?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so you look at this work on the programs to predict recidivism and decide who should get parole or who should get bail or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And how are you going to evaluate that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And one of the big issues is fairness across protected classes, protected classes being things like sex and race and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so two things you want is you want to say, well, if I get a score of say six out of 10,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: then I want that to mean the same whether no matter what race I'm on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I want to have a 60% chance of reoccurring regardless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And the makers of the one of the makers of a commercial program to do that says that's what we're trying to optimize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And look, we achieved that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We've reached that kind of balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then on the other side, you also want to say, well, if it makes mistakes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I want that to affect both sides of the protected class equally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And it turns out they don't do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So they're twice as likely to make a mistake that would harm a black person over a white person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that seems unfair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you'd like to say, well, I want to achieve both those goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then it turns out you do the analysis and it's theoretically impossible to achieve both those goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you have to trade them off one against the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that analysis is really helpful to know what you can aim for and how much you can get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You can't have everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But the analysis certainly can't tell you where should we make that tradeoff point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But nevertheless, then we can as humans deliberate where that tradeoff should be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So at least we now we're arguing in an informed way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We're not asking for something impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We're saying here's where we are and here's what we aim for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And this strategy is better than that strategy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that's I would argue is a really powerful and really important first step, but it's a doable one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So certainly they had part of that on the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Do you think deep learning will take its place as a chapter in this bigger is in this bigger view of AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, I think we don't know yet how it's all going to play out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So in the new edition, we have a chapter on deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We got Ian Goodfellow to be the guest author for that chapter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So he said he could condense his whole deep learning book into one chapter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think he did a great job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We were also encouraged that he's you know, we gave him the old neural net chapter and said, have fun with it, modernize that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And he said, you know, half of that was OK that certainly there's lots of new things that have been developed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But some of the core was still the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think we'll gain a better understanding of what you can do there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think we'll need to incorporate all the things we can do with the other technologies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So deep learning started out with convolutional networks and very close to perception and has since moved to be to be able to do more with actions and some degree of longer term planning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But we need to do a better job with representation and reasoning and one shot learning and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think we don't know yet how that's going to play out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Do you think looking at the some success, but certainly eventual demise, a partial demise of experts, the symbolic systems in the 80s, do you think there is kernels of wisdom in the work that was done there with logic and reasoning and so on that will rise again in your view?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So certainly I think the idea of representation and reasoning is crucial that sometimes you just don't have enough data about the world to learn de novo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you've got to have some idea of representation, whether that was programmed in or told or whatever, and then be able to take steps of reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think the problem with the good old fashioned AI was one, we tried to base everything on these symbols that were atomic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that's great if you're like trying to define the properties of a triangle, right, because they have necessary and sufficient conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But things in the real world don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: The real world is messy and doesn't have sharp edges and atomic symbols do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that was a poor match.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then the other aspect was that the reasoning was universal and applied anywhere, which in some sense is good, but it also means there's no guidance as to where to apply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so you started getting these paradoxes like, well, if I have a mountain and I remove one grain of sand, then it's still a mountain. But if I do that repeatedly, at some point it's not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And with logic, there's nothing to stop you from applying things repeatedly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But maybe with something like deep learning, and I don't really know what the right name for it is, we could separate out those ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So one, we could say, you know, a mountain isn't just an atomic notion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's some sort of something like word embedding that has a more complex representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And secondly, we could somehow learn, yeah, there's this rule that you can remove one grain of sand and you can do that a bunch of times, but you can't do it a near infinite amount of times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But on the other hand, when you're doing induction on the integer, sure, then it's fine to do it an infinite number of times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And if we could somehow we have to learn when these strategies are applicable rather than having the strategies be completely neutral and available everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Anytime you use neural networks, anytime you learn from data or form representation from data in an automated way, it's not very explainable as to or it's not introspective to us humans in terms of how this neural network sees the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Where why does it succeed so brilliantly on so many in so many cases and fail so miserably in surprising ways and small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So what do you think is this is the future there can simply more data, better data, more organized data solve that problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Or is there elements of symbolic systems that need to be brought in, which are a little bit more explainable?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So I prefer to talk about trust and validation and verification rather than just about explainability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then I think explanations are one tool that you use towards those goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think it is important issue that we don't want to use these systems unless we trust them and we want to understand where they work and where they don't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And in an explanation can be part of that. Right. So I apply for a loan and I get denied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I want some explanation of why and you have in Europe, we have the GDPR that says you're required to be able to get that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But on the other hand, the explanation alone is not enough. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So, you know, we are used to dealing with people and with organizations and corporations and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And they can give you an explanation and you have no guarantee that that explanation relates to reality. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So the bank can tell me, well, you didn't get the loan because you didn't have enough collateral.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that may be true or it may be true that they just didn't like my religion or something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I can't tell from the explanation. And that's true whether the decision was made by computer or by a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I want more. I do want to have the explanations and I want to be able to have a conversation to go back and forth and said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: well, you gave this explanation, but what about this? And what would have happened if this had happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And what would I need to change that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think a conversation is a better way to think about it than just an explanation as a single output.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think we need testing of various kinds. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So in order to know was the decision really based on my collateral or was it based on my religion or skin color or whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I can't tell if I'm only looking at my case. But if I look across all the cases, then I can detect the pattern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So you want to have that kind of capability. You want to have these adversarial testing. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we thought we were doing pretty good at object recognition and images.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We said, look, we're at sort of pretty close to human level performance on image net and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then you start seeing these adversarial images and you say, wait a minute, that part is nothing like human performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You can mess with it really easily. You can mess with it really easily. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And yeah, you can do that to humans too. Right. So in a different way, perhaps. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Humans don't know what color the dress was. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so they're vulnerable to certain attacks that are different than the attacks on the machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But the attacks on the machines are so striking, they really change the way you think about what we've done. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And the way I think about it is I think part of the problem is we're seduced by our low dimensional metaphors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So, you know, you look like that phrase, you look in a textbook and you say, OK, now we've mapped out the space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, cat is here and dog is here. And maybe there's a tiny little spot in the middle where you can't tell the difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But mostly we've got it all covered. And if you believe that metaphor, then you say, well, we're nearly there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, there's only going to be a couple adversarial images.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But I think that's the wrong metaphor. And what you should really say is it's not a 2D flat space that we've got mostly covered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's a million dimension space. And cat is this string that goes out in this crazy path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And if you step a little bit off the path in any direction, you're in no where's land and you don't know what's going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so I think that's where we are. And now we've got to deal with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So it wasn't so much an explanation, but it was an understanding of what the models are and what they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And now we can start exploring how do you fix that. Yeah. Validating the robustness of the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So on. But take it back to the this this word trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Do you think we're a little too hard on our robots in terms of the standards we apply?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So, you know, of there's a dance, there's a there's a there's a dance in nonverbal and verbal communication between humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, if we apply the same kind of standard in terms of humans, you know, we trust each other pretty quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, you and I haven't met before and there's some degree of trust, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That nothing's going to go crazy wrong. And yet to a eye, when we look at a systems where we seem to approach through skepticism, always, always.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And it's like they have to prove through a lot of hard work that they're even worthy of even inkling of our trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What do you what do you think about that? How do we break that barrier, close that gap?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think that's right. I think that's a big issue. Just listening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: My friend Mark Moffat is a naturalist and he says the most amazing thing about humans is that you can walk into a coffee shop or a busy street in a city.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And there's lots of people around you that you've never met before. And you don't kill each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. He says chimpanzees cannot do that. Yeah. Right. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: If a chimpanzee is in a situation where here's some that aren't from my tribe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Bad things happen, especially in a coffee shop. There's delicious food around, you know. Yeah. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But we humans have figured that out. Yeah. Right. And, you know, for the most part, for the most part, we still go to war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We still do terrible things. But for the most part, we've learned to trust each other and live together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So that's going to be important for our AI systems as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I also I think a lot of the emphasis is on AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But in many cases, AI is part of the technology, but isn't really the main thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So a lot of what we've seen is more due to communications technology than AI technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, you want to make these good decisions. But the reason we're able to have any kind of system at all is we've got the communications so that we're collecting the data and so that we can reach lots of people around the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think that's a bigger change that we're dealing with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Speaking of reaching a lot of people around the world, on the side of education, you've one of the many things in terms of education you've done, you've taught the intro to artificial intelligence course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That signed up 100,000 160,000 students is one of the first successful example of an massive of a MOOC massive open online course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What did you learn from that experience? What do you think is the future of MOOCs of education online?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, it was a great fun doing it, particularly being right at the start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Just because it was exciting and new, but it also meant that we had less competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So one of the things you hear about, well, the problem with MOOCs is the completion rates are so low, so there must be a failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I got to admit, I'm a prime contributor. I've probably started 50 different courses that I haven't finished, but I got exactly what I wanted out of them because I had never intended to finish them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I just wanted to dabble in a little bit, either to see the topic matter or just to see the pedagogy of how are they doing this class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I guess the main thing I learned is when I came in, I thought the challenge was information, saying if I'm just take the stuff I want you to know and I'm very clear and explain it well, then my job is done and good things are going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And in doing the course, I learned, well, yeah, you got to have the information, but really the motivation is the most important thing, that if students don't stick with it, it doesn't matter how good the content is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think being one of the first classes, we were helped by sort of exterior motivation. So we tried to do a good job of making it enticing and setting up ways for the community to work with each other to make it more motivating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But really a lot of it was, hey, this is a new thing and I'm really excited to be part of a new thing. And so the students brought their own motivation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so I think this is great because there's lots of people around the world who have never had this before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, would never have the opportunity to go to Stanford and take a class or go to MIT or go to one of the other schools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But now we can bring that to them. And if they bring their own motivation, they can be successful in a way they couldn't before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But that's really just the top tier of people that are ready to do that. The rest of the people just don't see or don't have the motivation and don't see how if they push through and we're able to do it, what advantage that would get them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think we got a long way to go before we're able to do that. And I think it'll be some of it is based on technology, but more of it's based on the idea of community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You got to actually get people together. Some of the getting together can be done online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think some of it really has to be done in person in order to build that type of community and trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, there's an intentional mechanism that we've developed a short attention span, especially younger people, because sort of shorter and shorter videos online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I mean, there's a whatever the way the brain is developing now with people that have grown up with the Internet, they have quite a short attention span.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So and I would say I had the same when I was growing up to probably for different reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I probably wouldn't have learned as much as I have if I wasn't forced to sit in a physical classroom, sort of bored, sometimes falling asleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But sort of forcing myself through that process to sometimes extremely difficult computer science courses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What's the difference in your view between in-person education experience, which you first of all yourself had and you yourself taught and online education?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And how do we close that gap if it's even possible? Yeah. So I think there's two issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: One is whether it's in person or online, so sort of the physical location, and then the other is kind of the affiliation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So you stuck with it in part because you were in the classroom and you saw everybody else was suffering the same way you were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But also because you were enrolled, you had paid tuition, sort of everybody was expecting you to stick with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Society, parents, peers. Right. And so those are two separate things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I mean, you could certainly imagine I pay a huge amount of tuition and everybody signed up and says, yes, you're doing this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But then I'm in my room and my classmates are in different rooms. Right. We could have things set up that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So it's not just the online versus offline. I think what's more important is the commitment that you've made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And certainly it is important to have that kind of informal, you know, I meet people outside of class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We talk together because we're all in it together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think that's really important, both in keeping your motivation and also that's where some of the most important learning goes on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you want to have that. Maybe, you know, especially now we start getting into higher bandwidths and augmented reality and virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You might be able to get that without being in the same physical place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Do you think it's possible we'll see a course at Stanford, for example, that for students enrolled students is only online in the near future or literally sort of it's part of the curriculum and there is no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So you're starting to see that. I know Georgia Tech has a master's that's done that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Oftentimes it's sort of they're creeping in in terms of a master's program or sort of further education considering the constraints of students and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But I mean, literally, is it possible that we, you know, Stanford, MIT, Berkeley, all these places go online only in in the next few decades?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, probably not, because, you know, they've got a big commitment to a physical campus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Sure. There's a momentum that's both financial and culturally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. And then there are certain things that just hard to do virtually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So, you know, we're in a field where if you have your own computer and your own paper and so on, you can do the work anywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But if you're in a biology lab or something, you know, you don't have all the right stuff at home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So our field, programming, you've also done a lot of you've done a lot of programming yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: In 2001, you wrote a great article about programming called Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years, sort of response to all the books that say teach yourself programming 21 days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So if you're giving advice to someone getting to programming today, this is a few years since you've written that article.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What's the best way to undertake that journey?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think there's lots of different ways and I think programming means more things now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I guess, you know, when I wrote that article, I was thinking more about becoming a professional software engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I thought that's a sort of a career long field of study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But I think there's lots of things now that people can do where programming is a part of solving what they want to solve without achieving that professional level status.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So I'm not going to be going and writing a million lines of code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But, you know, I'm a biologist or a physicist or something or even a historian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I've got some data and I want to ask a question of that data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think for that, you don't need ten years. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So there are many shortcuts to being able to answer those kinds of questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, you see today a lot of emphasis on learning to code, teaching kids how to code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think that's great. But I wish they would change the message a little bit. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think code isn't the main thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I don't really care if you know the syntax of JavaScript or if you can connect these blocks together in this visual language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But what I do care about is that you can analyze a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You can think of a solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You can carry out, you know, make a model, run that model, test the model, see the results, verify that they're reasonable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: ask questions and answer them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: All right. So it's more modeling and problem solving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And you use coding in order to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But it's not just learning coding for its own sake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That's really interesting. So it's actually almost in many cases, it's learning to work with data to extract something useful out of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So when you say problem solving, you really mean taking some kind of maybe collecting some kind of data set, cleaning it up and saying something interesting about it, which is useful in all kinds of domains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I see myself being stuck sometimes in kind of the old ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So, you know, I'll be working on a project maybe with a younger employee and we say, oh, well, here's this new package that could help solve this problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I'll go and I'll start reading the manuals and, you know, I'll be two hours into reading the manuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then my colleague comes back and says, I'm done. You know, I downloaded the package, I installed it, I tried calling some things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: The first one didn't work. The second one worked. Now I'm done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I say, but I have other questions about how does this work and how does that work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And they say, who cares? Right. I don't need to understand the whole thing. I answered my question. It's a big, complicated package.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I don't understand the rest of it, but I got the right answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I'm just it's hard for me to get into that mindset. I want to understand the whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, if they wrote a manual, I should probably read it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And but that's not necessarily the right way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think I have to get used to dealing with more being more comfortable with uncertainty and not knowing everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So I struggle with the same instead of the spectrum between Donald and Don Knuth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that's kind of the very, you know, before he can say anything about a problem, he really has to get down to the machine code assembly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. Versus exactly what you said of of several students in my group that, you know, 20 years old and they can solve almost any problem within a few hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That would take me probably weeks because I would try to, as you said, read the manual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So do you think the nature of masteries you're mentioning biology, sort of outside disciplines, applying programming, but computer scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So over time, there's higher and higher levels of abstraction available now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So with this week, there's the TensorFlow Summit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So if you're if you're not particularly into deep learning, but you still a computer scientist, you can accomplish an incredible amount with TensorFlow without really knowing any fundamental internals of machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Do you think the nature of mastery is changing even for computer scientists, like what it means to be an expert programmer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, I think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, we never really should have focused on programmers, right, because it's still it's the skill and what we really want to focus on is the result.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So we built this ecosystem where the way you can get stuff done is by programming it yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: At least when I started, you know, library functions meant you had square root and that was about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. Everything else you built from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then we built up an ecosystem where a lot of times you can download a lot of stuff that does a big part of what you need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so now it's more a question of assembly rather than manufacturing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that's a different way of looking at problems from another perspective in terms of mastery and looking at programmers or people that reason about problems in a computational way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So Google, you know, from the hiring perspective, from the perspective of hiring or building a team of programmers, how do you determine if someone's a good programmer or if somebody again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I want to deviate from I want to move away from the word programmer, but somebody who could solve problems of large scale data and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What's what's how do you build a team like that through the interviewing process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. And I and I think as a company grows, you get more expansive in the types of people you're looking for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. So I think, you know, in the early days, we'd interview people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And the question we were trying to ask is how close are they to Jeff Dean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And most people were pretty far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But we take the ones that were, you know, not that far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so we got kind of a homogeneous group of people who are really great programmers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Then as a company grows, you say, well, we don't want everybody to be the same, have the same skill set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so now we're hiring biologists in our health areas and we're hiring physicists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: We're hiring mechanical engineers, we're hiring social scientists and ethnographers and people with different backgrounds who bring different skills.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you mentioned that you still make partaking code reviews, given that you have a wealth of experience, as you've also mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: What errors do you often see and tend to highlight in the code of junior developers of people coming up now, given your background from Lisp to a couple of decades of programming?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, that's a great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, sometimes I try to look at the flexibility of the design of yes, you know, this API solves this problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But where is it going to go in the future? Who else is going to want to call this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, are you making it easier for them to do that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: That's a matter of design. Is it documentation? Is it sort of an amorphous thing? You can't really put it in words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's just how it feels. If you put yourself in the shoes of a developer, would you use this kind of thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think it is how you feel. Right. And so, yeah, documentation is good, but it's but it's more a design question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Right. If you get the design right, then people will figure it out whether the documentation is good or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And if the design is wrong, then it'll be harder to use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: How have you yourself changed as a programmer over the years?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: In a way, you already started to say sort of you want to read the manual, you want to understand the core of the syntax to the how the language is supposed to be used and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But what's the evolution been like from the 80s, 90s to today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I guess one thing is you don't have to worry about the small details of efficiency as much as you used to. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So, like, I remember I did my list book in the 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And one of the things I wanted to do was say, here's how you do an object system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And basically, we're going to make it so each object is a hash table and you look up the methods and here's how it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then I said, of course, the real common list object system is much more complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's got all these efficiency type issues. And this is just a toy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Nobody would do this in real life. And it turns out Python pretty much did exactly what I said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. And said objects are just dictionaries. And, yeah, they have a few little tricks as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But mostly, you know, the thing that would have been 100 times too slow in the 80s is now plenty fast for most everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you had to as a programmer let go of perhaps an obsession that I remember coming up with of trying to write efficient code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. That to say, you know, what really matters is the total time it takes to get the project done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And most of that's going to be the programmer time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So if you're a little bit less efficient, but it makes it easier to understand and modify, then that's the right trade off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you've written quite a bit about Lisp, your book on programming is in Lisp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You have a lot of code out there that's in Lisp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So myself and people who don't know what Lisp is should look it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: It's my favorite language for many researches. It is a favorite language, the favorite language they never use these days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So what part of Lisp do you find most beautiful and powerful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think the beautiful part is the simplicity that in half a page you can define the whole language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And other languages don't have that. So you feel like you can hold everything in your head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And then, you know, a lot of people say, well, then that's too simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, here's all these things I want to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And, you know, my Java or Python or whatever has 100 or 200 or 300 different syntax rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And don't I need all those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And Lisp's answer was, no, we're only going to give you eight or so syntax rules, but we're going to allow you to define your own.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so that was a very powerful idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think this idea of saying I can start with my problem and with my data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: and then I can build the language I want for that problem and for that data, and then I can make Lisp define that language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So you're sort of mixing levels and saying I'm simultaneously a programmer in a language and a language designer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And that allows a better match between your problem and your eventual code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I think Lisp had done that better than other languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, it's a very elegant implementation of functional programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But why do you think Lisp has not had the mass adoption and success of languages like Python?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Is it the parentheses? Is it all the parentheses?

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah. So I think a couple of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So one was I think it was designed for a single programmer or a small team

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: and a skilled programmer who had the good taste to say, well, I am doing language design and I have to make good choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And if you make good choices, that's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: If you make bad choices, you can hurt yourself and it can be hard for other people on the team to understand it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I think there was a limit to the scale of the size of a project in terms of number of people that Lisp was good for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And as an industry, we kind of grew beyond that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I think it is in part the parentheses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: You know, one of the jokes is the acronym for Lisp is lots of irritating, silly parentheses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: My acronym was Lisp is syntactically pure, saying all you need is parentheses and atoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But I remember, you know, as we had the AI textbook and because we did it in the 90s, we had pseudocode in the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: But then we said, well, we'll have Lisp online because that's the language of AI at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I remember some of the students complaining because they hadn't had Lisp before and they didn't quite understand what was going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I remember one student complained, I don't understand how this pseudocode corresponds to this Lisp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And there was a one to one correspondence between the symbols in the code and the pseudocode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And the only thing different was the parentheses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I said, it must be that for some people, a certain number of left parentheses shuts off their brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: Yeah, it's very, it's very possible in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And Python just goes the other way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And so that was the point at which I said, OK, can't have only Lisp as a language because I, you know, I don't want to, you know, you only got 10 or 12 or 15 weeks or whatever it is to teach AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And I don't want to waste two weeks of that teaching Lisp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So I say, I got to have another language. Java was the most popular language at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: I started doing that. And then I said, it's really hard to have a one to one correspondence between the pseudocode and the Java because Java is so verbose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: So then I said, I'm going to do a survey and find the language that's most like my pseudocode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42

body.input: And turned out Python basically was my pseudocode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Peter Norvig: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach | Lex Fridman Podcast #42
