body.input: And now here's my conversation with Ian Hutchinson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Maybe it'd be nice to draw a distinction between nuclear physics and plasma physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What is the distinction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Nuclear physics is about the physics of the nucleus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And my department, Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering at MIT, is very concerned about all the interactions and reactions and consequences of things that go on in the nucleus,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: including nuclear energy, fission energy, which is the nuclear energy that we have already, and fusion energy, which is the energy source of the sun and stars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: which we don't quite know how to turn into practical energy for humankind at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what my research has mostly been aimed at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But plasmas are essentially the fourth state of matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So if you think about solid, liquid, gas, plasma is the fourth of those states of matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's actually the state of matter which one reaches if one raises the temperature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So cold things, you know, like ice, are solid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Liquids are hotter water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if you heat water beyond 100 degrees Celsius, it becomes gas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, that's true of most substances. And plasma is a state of matter in which the electrons are unbound from the nuclei.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So they become separate from the nuclei and can move separately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So we have positively charged nuclei and we have negatively charged electrons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The net is still electrically neutral, but a plasma conducts electricity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: has all sorts of important properties that are associated with that separation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's what plasmas are all about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the reason why my department is interested in plasma physics very strongly is because most things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: well, for one thing, most things in the universe are plasma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The vast majority of matter in the universe is plasma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But most particularly, stars and the sun are plasmas because they're very hot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's only in very hot states that nuclear fusion reactions take place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we want to understand how to implement those kind of phenomena on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Maybe another distinction we want to try to get at is the difference between fission and fusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So you mentioned fusion is the kind of reaction happening in the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So what's fission and what's fusion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, fission is taking heavy elements like uranium and breaking them up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it turns out that that process of breaking up heavy elements releases energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does it mean to be a heavy element?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It means that there are many nuclear particles in the nucleus itself, neutrons and protons in the nucleus itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that in the case of uranium, there are 92 protons in each nucleus and even more neutrons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that the total number of nucleons in the nucleus, nucleons is short for either a proton or a neutron,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the total number might be 235, that's U-235, or it might be 238, that's U-238.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So those are heavy elements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Light elements, by contrast, have very few protons or neutrons in the nucleus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Hydrogen is the lightest nucleus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It has one proton.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They're actually slightly heavier forms of hydrogen isotopes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Deuterium has a proton and a neutron.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And tritium has a proton and two neutrons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So it has a total of three nucleons in the nucleus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, taking light elements like isotopes of hydrogen and not breaking them up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but actually fusing them together, reacting them together to produce heavier elements,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: typically helium, which is helium is a nucleus which has two protons and two neutrons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that also releases energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that, or reactions like that, making heavier elements from lighter elements, is what mostly powers the sun and stars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Both fusion and fission release approximately a million times more energy per unit mass than chemical reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So a chemical reaction means take hydrogen, take oxygen, react them together, let's say, and get water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That releases energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The energy released in a chemical reaction like that or the burning of coal or oil or whatever else

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is about a million times less per unit mass than what is released in nuclear reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So it's hard to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It requires very high energy of impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And actually it's very easy to understand why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that is that those two nuclei, if they're both, let's say, hydrogen nuclei,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: one is, let's say, deuterium and the other is, let's say, tritium, they're both electrically charged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And they're positively charged, so they like charges repel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Everyone knows that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So basically to get them close enough together to react, you have to overcome the repulsion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the electric repulsion of the two nuclei from one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And you have to get them extremely close to one another in order for the nuclear forces to overtake the electrical forces

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and actually form a new nucleus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so one requires very high energies of impact in order for reactions to take place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And those high energies of impact correspond to very high temperatures of random motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's why you can do stuff like that in the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So we can build the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's one way to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And on Earth, how do you create a fusion reaction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, nature's fusion reactors are indeed the stars, and they are very hot in the center.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And they reach the point where they release more energy from those reactions

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: than they lose by radiation and transport to the surface and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's a state of ignition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's what we have to achieve to give net energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's like lighting a fire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If you have a bundle of sticks and you hold a match up to it and you see smoke coming from the sticks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but you take the match away and the sticks just fizzle out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the reason they fizzled out is that, yes, they were burning, there was smoke coming from them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but they were not ignited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But if you are able to take the match away and they keep burning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and they are generating enough heat to keep themselves hot and hence keep the reactions going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that's chemical ignition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, what we need to do, what the stars do in order to generate nuclear fusion energy, is they are ignited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They are generated enough energy to keep themselves hot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's what we've got to do on Earth if we're going to make fusion work on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it's much harder to do on Earth than it is in a star,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: because we need temperatures of order tens of millions of degrees Celsius

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in order for the reactions to go fast enough to generate enough electricity to keep it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or enough energy to keep it going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so, if you've got something that's tens of millions of degrees Celsius,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and you want to keep it all together and keep the heat in long enough to have enough reactions taking place,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: you can't just put it in a bottle, plastic or glass, it would be gone in milliseconds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, you have to have some non-material mechanism of confining the plasma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In the case of stars, that non-material force is gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, gravity is what holds the star together, it holds the plasma in long enough for it to react

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and sustain itself by the fusion reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But on Earth, gravity is extremely weak.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't mean to say we don't fall, yes, we fall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But the mutual gravitational attraction of small objects is very weak compared with the electrical repulsion

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or any other force that you can think about on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so, we need a stronger force to keep the plasma together, to confine it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the predominant attempt at making fusion work on Earth is to use magnetic fields to confine the plasma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's what I've worked on for much, essentially most of my career,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is to understand how we can and how best we can confine these incredibly hot gases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: plasmas, using magnetic fields with the ultimate objective of releasing fusion energy on Earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and generating electricity with it and powering our society with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Dumb question. So, on top of the magnetic fields, do you also need the plastic water bottle walls

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or is it purely magnetic fields?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, actually, what we do need walls, those walls must be kept away from the plasma,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: because otherwise they'd be melted, or the plasma must be kept away from them inside of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But the main purpose of the walls is not to keep the plasma in, it's to keep the atmosphere out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, if we want to do it on Earth where there's air,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we want the plasma to consist of hydrogen isotopes or other things, the things we're trying to react.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And by the way, the density of those plasmas, at least in magnetic confinement fusion, is very low.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's maybe a million times less than the density of air in this room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, in order for a fusion reactor like that to work, you have to keep all of the air out and just keep the plasma in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, yes, there are other things, but those are things that are relatively easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, making a vacuum these days is technologically quite straightforward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We know how to do that, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What we don't quite know how to do is to make a confinement device that isolates the plasma well enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: so that it's able to keep itself burning with its own reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, maybe, can you talk about what a tokamak is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The Russian acronym from which the word tokamak is built just means toroidal magnetic chamber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, it's a toroidal chamber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: A torus is a geometric shape which is like a doughnut with a hole down the middle, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so, it's the meat of the doughnut, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's the torus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's got a magnetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, that's really all tokamak means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But the particular configuration that is very widespread and is the sort of best prospect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in the least in the near term, for making fusion energy work is one in which there's a very strong

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: magnetic field the long way around the doughnut, around the torus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, you've got to imagine that there's this doughnut shape with an embedded magnetic field

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: just going round and round the long way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The big advantage of that is that plasma particles, when they're in the presence of a magnetic field,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: feel strong forces from the magnetic field, and those forces make the particles gyrate

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: around the direction of the magnetic field line.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, basically, the particles follow helical orbits, following like a spring

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that's directed along the magnetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, if you make the magnetic field go inside this toroidal chamber and just simply go round

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and round the chamber, then because of this helical orbit, the particles can't move fast

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: across the magnetic field, but they can move very quickly along the magnetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if you have a magnetic field that doesn't leave the chamber, it doesn't matter if they move

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: along the magnetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It doesn't mean they're going to exit the chamber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But if you just had a straight magnetic field, for example, coming from a Helmholtz coil

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or a bar magnet, then you'd have to have ends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It would come to the ends of the chamber somewhere, and the particles would hit the ends,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and they would lose their energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, that's why it's toroidal, and that's why we have a strong magnetic field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's providing a confinement against motion in the direction that would lead the particles

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to leave the chamber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It turns out that...

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Here we're getting a little bit technical, but it turns out that a toroidal field alone

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is not enough, and so you need more fields to produce true confinement of plasma, and we get

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: those by passing a current as well through the plasma itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: To make sure it stays on track.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, what that does is makes the field lines themselves into much bigger helices, and that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for reasons that are too complicated to explain, that clinches the confinement of the particles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: at least in terms of their single particle orbit, so they don't leave the chamber.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, when the particles are flying along this donut, the inside of the donut, where's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: generation of the energy coming from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Are they smashing into each other?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, eventually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, in a fusion reactor, there will be deuterons and tritons, and they will be smashing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They will be very hot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They'll be 100 million degrees Celsius or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, they're moving thermally with very large thermal energies in random directions, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: they will collide with one another and have fusion reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: When those fusion reactions take place, energy is released, large amounts of energy is released

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in the form of particles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: One of the particles that's released is an alpha particle, which is also charged, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: it's also confined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That alpha particle stays in the donut and heats the other particles that are in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: donut.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, it transfers its energy to those, and it keeps them hot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's some leaking of heat all the time, a little bit of radiation, some transport,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's also a neutron released from that reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The neutron carries out four-fifths of the fusion energy, and that will have to be captured

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in a blanket that surrounds the chamber in which we take the energy, drive some kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of electrical generator from a thermal engine, gas turbine or something like that, and power

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And you've got energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, where do we stand?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: On getting this thing to be something that actually works, that generates energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, there have been experiments that have generated net nuclear energies or nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: powers in the vicinity of tens of megawatts for a few seconds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, that's 10 megajoules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's not much energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's a few donuts worth of energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Okay, literal donuts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Literal donuts, that's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But we have studied how well tokamaks can find plasmas, and so we now understand in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: rather great detail the way they work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we're able to predict what is going to be required in order to build a tokamak that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: becomes self-sustaining, that becomes essentially ignited or so close to ignited that it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And at the moment, at least if you use the modest magnetic field values, still very strong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but limited magnetic field values, you have to build a very big device.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so, we are at the moment, worldwide fusion research is at the moment in the process of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: building a very big experiment that's located in the south of France.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's called ITER, I-T-E-R, which means the way or just means the International Tokamak

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Experimental Reactor, if you like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that experiment is designed to reach this burning plasma state and to generate about

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: 500 megawatts of fusion power for hundreds of seconds at a time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It'll still only be an experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It won't put electricity on the grid or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's to figure out whether it works and what the remaining engineering challenges are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's a scientific experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It won't be engineered to run around the clock and so on and so forth, which ultimately one

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: needs to do in order to make something that's practical for generating electricity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it will be the first demonstration on earth of a controlled fusion reaction for

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a long time period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is that exciting to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's been an objective that has in many ways motivated my entire career and the career

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of many people like me in the field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I have to admit though that one of the problems with ITER is that it's an extremely big and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: expensive and long time to build experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so it won't even come into operation until about 2025, even though it's been being built

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for 10 years and it was designed for 30 years before that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so that's actually one of the big disappointments of my career in a certain sense, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that we won't get to a burning fusion reaction until well past the first operation of ITER.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And whether I'm alive or not, I don't know, but I certainly will be well and truly retired

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: by the time that happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so when I realized maybe some years ago that that was going to be the case, it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a discouragement to me, let's put it like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But if we can try to look maybe in a ridiculous kind of way, look into a hundred years from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: now, 200 years, 500 years from now, and there's folks like Elon Musk trying to travel outside

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, the amount of energy we need for some of the exciting things we want to do in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: world if we look again, a hundred years from now, seems to be a very large amount.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So do you think fusion energy will eventually, sometime into your retirement, will be basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: behind most of the things we do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Look, I absolutely think that fusion research is completely justified.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In fact, we should be spending more time and effort on it than we currently do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it isn't going to be a magic bullet that somehow solves all the problems of energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: By the way, that's a generic statement you can make about any energy source in my view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's a grave mistake to think that science of any sort is suddenly going to find

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a magic bullet for meeting all the energy needs of society or any of the other needs

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of society, by the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we can talk about that, I hope, later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But fusion is very worthwhile and we should be doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so my disappointment that I just expressed was, in a certain sense, a personal disappointment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I do think that fusion energy is a terrific challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's very difficult to bring the energy source of the sun and stars down to Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: This does contrast, in a certain sense, with fission energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: By contrast, fission energy, to build a fission reactor, proved to be amazingly easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We did it within a few years of discovering nuclear fission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: People had figured out how to build a reactor and did so during the Second World War.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Which is, by the way, fission is how the current nuclear power plants work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You have nuclear energy today because fission reactors are relatively easy to build.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What's hard is getting the materials, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's just as well because if everyone could get those materials, there would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: weapons, proliferation, and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it wasn't all that long after even the discovery of nuclear fission that fission

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: reactors were built.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Even fission reactors, of course, operated before we had weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think nuclear power is obviously important to meet the energy challenges of our age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It is completely, intrinsically completely CO2 emissions free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In fact, the wastes that come from nuclear power, whether it's fission or fusion for

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that matter, are so moderate in quantity that we shouldn't really be worried about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, yes, fission products are highly radioactive and we need to keep them away from people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but there's so little of them that keeping them away from people is not particularly

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: While people complain a lot about the drawbacks of fission energy, I think most of those complaints

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are ill-informed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We can talk about the challenges and the disasters, if you like, of fission reactors, but I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: fission in the near term offers a terrific opportunity for environmentally friendly energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: which in the world as a whole is rapidly being taken advantage of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: China and India and places like that are rapidly building fission plants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We're not rapidly building fission plants in the US, although we are actually building

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: two at the moment, two new ones, but we do still get 20% of our electricity from fission

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: energy and we could get a lot more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, it's clean energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So it's clean energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Now, again, the concern is there's a very popular HBO show, just came out on Chernobyl.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's the Three Mile Island, there's Fukushima, that's the most recent disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So there's a kind of a concern of nuclear disasters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is that, what do you make of that kind of concern, especially if we look into the future

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of fission energy-based reactors?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, first of all, let me say one or two words about the contrast between fission and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: fusion and then we'll come onto the question of the disasters and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Fission does have some drawbacks and they're largely to do with four main areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: One is, do we have enough uranium or other fissile fuels to supply our energy needs for

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a long time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The answer to that is we know we have enough uranium to support fission energy worldwide

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for thousands of years, but maybe not for millions of years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Secondly, there are issues to do with wastes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Fission wastes are highly radioactive and some of them are volatile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so, for example, in Fukushima, the problem was that some fraction of the fission wastes

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: were volatilized and went out as a cloud and polluted areas with cesium-137, astrontium-90,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's a challenge of fission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's a problem of safety beyond that and that is that in fission, it's hard to turn

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the reactor off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: When you stop the nuclear reactions, there is still a lot of heat being liberated from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the fission products.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that is actually what the problem was at Fukushima.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The Fukushima reactors were shut down the moment that the earthquake took place and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: they were shut down safely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What then happened after that at Fukushima was there was this enormous tidal wave, many

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: tens of meters high, that came through and destroyed the electricity grid feed to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Fukushima reactors and their cooling was then turned off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it was the after heat of the turned off reactors that eventually caused the problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that led to release.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's a safety concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And then finally, there's a problem of proliferation and that is that fission reactors need fissile

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: fuel and the technologies for producing and enriching and so forth the fuels can be used,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: can be by bad actors to generate the materials needed for a nuclear weapon and that's a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: serious concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So those are the four problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Fission has major advantages in respect of all of those problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It has more longer term fuel resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It has far more benign waste issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The radioactivity from fusion reactions is at least a hundred times less than it is from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: fission reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It has essentially none of this after heat problem because it doesn't produce fission

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: products that are highly radioactive and generating their own heat when it's turned off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In fact, the hard part of fusion is turning it on, not turning it off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And finally, you don't need the same fission technology to make fusion work and so it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: got terrific advantages from the point of view of proliferation control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So those are four main issues which make fusion seem attractive technologically because they

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: address some of the problems of fission energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't mean to say that fission energy is overwhelmingly problematic, but clearly there

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: have been catastrophes associated with fission reactors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Fukushima actually is, I think in many ways, often overstated as a disaster because after

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: all nobody was killed by the reactors, essentially zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's in the context of a disaster, a tsunami that killed between 15 and 20,000

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: people more or less instantaneously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So in the scale of risks, one should take the view that in my estimation that fission

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: energy came out of that looking pretty good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Of course, that's not the popular conception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: With a lot of things that threaten our wellbeing, we seem to be very bad users of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We seem to be very scared of shock attacks and not at all scared of car accidents and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: this kind of miscalculation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think from everything I understand, nuclear energy, fission-based energy goes into that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: category.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's one of the safest, one of the cleanest forms of energy and yet the PR, whoever does

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the PR for nuclear energy has a hard job ahead of them at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well I think part of that is their association with nuclear weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Because when you say the word nuclear, people don't instantly think about nuclear energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: they think about nuclear weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so there is perhaps a natural tendency to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But yes, I agree with you, people are very poor at estimating risks and they react emotionally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: not rationally in most of these situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Can we talk about nuclear weapons just for a little bit?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So fission is the kind of reaction that's central to the nuclear weapons we have today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what sets them off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what sets them off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So if we look at the hydrogen bomb, maybe you can say how these different weapons work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So the earliest nuclear weapons, the nuclear bombs that were dropped on Japan, etc., etc.,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: were pure fission weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They used enriched uranium or plutonium and their energy is essentially entirely derived

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: from fission reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it was early realized that more energy was available if one could somehow combine

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a fission bomb with fusion reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Because the fusion reactions give more energy per unit mass than fission reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And this was called the super.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You might have heard of the expression the super or more simply hydrogen bombs, bombs

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: which use isotopes of hydrogen and fusion reactions associated with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Like you said, it's hard to turn on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's hard to turn on because you need very high temperatures and you need confinement

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of that long enough for the reactions to take place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so a bomb, actually a thermonuclear bomb or a hydrogen bomb has essentially a chemical

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: implosion which then sets off a fission explosion which then sets off and compresses hydrogen

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: isotopes and other things, which I don't know because I've never had a security clearance

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: okay so I can't betray any secrets about weapons because I've never been party to them because

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I know a lot about this problem I can guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And sets off fusion reactions in the middle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's basically it's that sequence of things which produce these enormous multi-megaton

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: bombs that have very large yields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so fusion alone can't get you there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It is actually possible to set off or to try to set off little fusion bombs alone without

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the surrounding fission explosion and that is what is called laser fusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So another approach to fusion which actually is mostly researched in the weapons complex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the national labs and so forth because it's more associated with the technologies of weapons

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is inertial fusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So if you decide instead of trying to make your plasma just sit there in this torus in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the tokamak and be controlled steady state with a magnetic field, if you're willing to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: accept that I'll just set off an explosion okay and then I'll gather the energy from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that somehow I don't quite know how but let's not ask that question too much, then it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: possible to imagine generating fusion alone explosions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the way you do it is you take some small amount of deuterium tritium fuel, you bombard

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: it with energy from all sides and this is what the lasers are used for, extremely powerful

body.input: So that was the most important influence on me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That here were two people who were really smart, like me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm giving you my impressions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The way you felt at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The way I felt at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And they thought Christianity made sense and testified to its significance in their lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so that was a very important influence on me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And ultimately, I mean, the reason I didn't see Christianity as some kind of great evil,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the way it's sometimes portrayed by the radical atheists of this century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I think that's nonsense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I think there were certain attractive things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If you go to a university like Cambridge, you're surrounded by Western culture from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: about the 15th century onwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's saturated with Christian art and architecture and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so it's hard not to recognize that Christianity is, in fact, the foundation of Western society

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and Western culture, Western civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I mean, maybe I was in that sense favorably disposed towards Christianity as a religion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but as a personal faith, it didn't mean anything to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I became convinced really of two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: One is that the evidence for the resurrection of Jesus Christ is actually rather good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, it's not a proof.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's not some kind of scientific demonstrate or mathematical demonstration, but it's actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: extremely good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's not scientific evidence by and large.
