metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's historical evidence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Historical evidence, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that was one thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the other thing that came to me when I was at Cambridge, it became clear that Christianity

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: ultimately is not some kind of moral theory or philosophy or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It is, or at least it claims to be, a personal relationship with God, which is made possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: by what Jesus did on the cross and his life and his teaching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's a personal call to a relationship with God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I'd never really thought of it in those terms when I was younger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that thought became attractive to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I think most people find the person of Christ and his teachings compelling in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a certain sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What do you mean by personal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you mean personal for you, like a relationship like it's a meditative, like you specifically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: you Ian, have a connection with God?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And then the other side, you say personal with the actual body, the person of Jesus

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Christ.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So all of those things, what do you mean by personal connection and why that was meaningful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, so as a Christian-

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm sorry for the stupid questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: No, it's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: No problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: As a Christian, I believe that I have a relationship with God, which is best expressed by saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that it's personal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that comes about because Jesus through his acts has reconciled me with God, me a

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sinner, me someone full of sins, of failings, of ways in which I don't live up to even my

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: own ideals, let alone the ideals of a holy God, have been reconciled to the creator of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so Christians, myself included, believe that prayer is in a certain sense a connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: with God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And there are times when I have felt that God spoke to me, I don't mean necessarily

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: orally in words, but showed me things or enlightened me or inspired me in ways that I attribute

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I see it as a two-way relationship in a certain sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Of course, it's a very asymmetrical relationship, but nevertheless, Christians think that it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a two-way street.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We're not just talking into the air when we say we are going to pray for someone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In this two-way communication, is there a way that you could try to describe on a podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: what is God like in your view?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If you tried to describe, is it a force?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is it, for you, intellectually, is it a set of metaphors that you use to reason about

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is it a computer that does some computation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's an infinitely powerful computer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Or is it like Santa Claus, a guy with a beard on the cloud?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't mean what God actually is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, in your limited cognitive capacity as a human, what do you find helpful for thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of what God actually looks like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What is God?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, let me start by saying none of the above, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, clearly, God, the Christian God, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, et cetera,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is not any of those things, because all of those things you just mentioned are phenomena

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or entities in the created world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The most fundamental thing about monotheism as Abraham and Moses and so forth handed it

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: down is that God is not an entity within the creation, within the universe, that God is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the creator of it all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what Genesis, first two chapters of Genesis, is really about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's not about telling us how God created the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's about telling us and telling the early Hebrews that God created the world, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that therefore, he is not simply an entity within it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: On the other hand, our finite minds have a pretty hard time encompassing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So one has to, therefore, work in terms of metaphors and images and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think we would know very little about who God is if we were simply left to our own

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: devices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If we were just, here you are, you're in the universe, try to figure out who made it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, philosophers think they can do a little bit of that, maybe, and theologians think

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that they can do a little bit more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But Christians think that God has actually helped us along a lot by revealing himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we say that he's revealed himself supremely in the person of Jesus Christ.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so when Jesus says to his disciples, if you've seen me, you've seen the Father, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that is, in a certain sense, a watchword for answering this question for Christians.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It is that supremely, if we want to help ourselves understand who God really is, we look to Jesus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We look to what he did, we look to what he said, and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we believe that he is one with the Father, and that's why we believe in the Trinity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, it's basically because that revelation is extremely central to Christian belief and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: teaching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So in that sense, through Jesus, that's kind of a historical moment that's profound, that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: really powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you also think that God makes himself seen in less obvious ways in our world today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's certainly been the outlook of Jews and Christians throughout history that God is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: seen in the creation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: When we look at the creation, we see to some extent the wonder, the majesty, the might

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of the person, the entity, but the person who created it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's a way in which scientists particularly have over the ages, and certainly over most

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of the last five centuries since the Scientific Revolution, scientists have seen in a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sense the hand of God in creation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, this leads us perhaps to a different discussion, but I mean, it's remarkable to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: me how influential Christianity and religion in general has been in science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, most of the scientists through history, as you described, I mean, God has been a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: big part of their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, certainly up until the beginning of the 20th century, that was the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So maybe this is a good time to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Can you tell me what scientism is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, I mean, the short answer is that by scientism, we mean the belief that science

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is all the real knowledge there is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's a shorthand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There are lots of different facets of it and which one can explore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the book in which I explored it most thoroughly was actually an earlier book called Monopolizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the purpose of that title is to draw attention to the fact that in our society as a whole,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in particularly in the West today, we have grown so reliant on science that we tend to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: put aside other ways of getting to know things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so of course at MIT, we are focused on science and we do focus on it very much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But the truth is that there are many ways of getting to know things in our world, know

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: things reliably in our world, and a lot of them are not science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So scientism in my view is a terrible intellectual error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's the belief that somehow the methods of science as we develop them with experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and in the end, it relies particularly upon reproducibility in the world and on a kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of clarity that comes from measurements and mathematics and related types of skills.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Those powerful though they are for finding out about the world, do not give us all the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: knowledge we have and there's many other forms of knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the illustration that I usually use to try to help people to think about this is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to say, well, look, let's think about human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, to what extent can human history be discovered scientifically?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The answer is essentially it can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the reason is because human history is not reproducible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You can't do reproducible experiments or observations and go back and try it over again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's a one-off thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: History is full of unique events.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so you can't hope to do history using the methods of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, I mean, in some sense, history is a story of miracles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, they don't have to do with God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's just one-

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Uniqueness is anyway, unique events.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Unique events.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that science doesn't like that because it's unique events, by their very definition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are not reproducible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Can I ask sort of a tricky question?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't even know what atheist or atheism is, but is it possible for somebody to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: an atheist and avoid slipping into scientism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Oh yeah, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, these are two separate things, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm quite sure there are many people who don't believe in God and yet recognize that there

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are many different ways we get knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Some is history, some is sociology, economics, politics, philosophy, art history, language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: literature, et cetera, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There are many people who recognize those disciplines as having their own approaches

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to epistemology and to how we get knowledge and valuing them very highly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't mean to say that everyone who's an atheist automatically subscribes to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: scientistic viewpoint.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it's certainly the case that many of the arguments, in fact, most of the arguments

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of the aggressive atheists of this century, people are sometimes called new atheists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: although they're actually rather old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Most of their arguments are rather old, are drawing heavily on scientism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So when they say things like, there's no evidence to support Christianity, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What they are really focusing on is saying that Christianity isn't proved or the evidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for Christianity is not science, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Science doesn't prove it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if you read their books, that's what you find they really mean is science doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: lead you necessarily to believe in a creator God or in any particular religion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I accept that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But that's not a problem to me because I don't think that science is all the knowledge there

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is and I think there are other important ways of getting to know things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And one of them is historical, for example, and I mentioned earlier that I became persuaded

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and I still am persuaded that the historical evidence for the resurrection is very persuasive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Again, it's not proof or anything like that, but it's pretty good evidence, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, I've talked to Richard Dawkins on this podcast and I saw you debate with Sean Carroll.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I understand this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It makes me very curious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Maybe let me ask sort of another way, my own kind of worldview, maybe you can help by way

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of therapy understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You know, because you've kind of said that there's other ways of knowing, what about

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: if I kind of sit here and am cognizant of the fact that I almost don't know anything?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Sort of I'm sitting here almost paralyzed by the mystery of it all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's not even when you say there's other ways of knowing, it feels almost too confident

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And yeah, when I listen to beautiful music or see art, there's something there that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: beyond the reach of scientism, I would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So beyond the reach of the tools of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I don't even feel like that could be an actual tool of knowing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I just don't even know where to begin because it just feels like we know so little.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Like if we look even 100 years from now, when people look back to this time, humans look

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: back to this time, they'll probably laugh at how little we knew, even 100 years from

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if we look at a thousand years from now, hopefully we're still alive or some version

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of ourselves or AI version of ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You know, they'll certainly laugh at the absurdity of our beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So you don't seem to be as paralyzed by how little we know, you confidently push on forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But what do you make of that sense of just not knowing of the mystery?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We need to be modest or humble even about what we know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I accept that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I certainly think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Not simply because in the future we'll know more science and there will be more powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: ways of finding out about things, but simply because sometimes we're not right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We're wrong, okay, in what we think we know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's crucial, but it's also a very Christian outlook.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That kind of humility is what Jesus taught.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I don't know whether this was in the back of your mind when you were thinking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: this, but it's often the case that people of religious faith are accused of being dogmatists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And there is a sense in which dogma teaching, accepted teaching, is part of religions, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I don't think that necessarily that leads one to blind dogmatism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I certainly don't think that faith, we can talk about this later if you'd like, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I certainly don't think that faith means thinking you know something and not listening to counter

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: arguments, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I think that's crucial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does faith mean to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does it feel like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does it actually sort of, how do you carry your faith in terms of the way you see

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I think faith is very often misunderstood in our society at the moment because it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: often portrayed as being nothing other than believing things you know ain't true, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Or believing things that are not proven, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And faith does have a strand which is to do with basically believing in concepts or propositions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but actually the word faith is much broader than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Faith also means trusting in something, trusting in a person or trusting in a thing, the reliability

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of some technology, for example, that's equally part of the meaning of the word faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And there's a third strand to the meaning of the word as well, and that is loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So you know, I have faith in my wife and I try to act in faith towards her, and that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a kind of loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so those three strands are the most important strands of the meaning of faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Belief in propositions that we might not have full proof about or maybe we have very little

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: proof about, but it's also trust and loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And actually in terms of the Christian faith, Christians are far more called to trust and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: loyalty than they are to belief in things they don't have proof of, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The critics of religion generally tend to emphasize the first one and say, well, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: believe things for which you have no evidence, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what they think faith is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, yeah, there is a sense in which everybody has to live their lives believing or making

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: decisions in situations when they don't have all the proof or evidence or knowledge that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: enables you to make a completely rational or well-informed or prudent decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We do this all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: My drive down here, I nearly took a wrong turning and I thought, which way do I go?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do I keep going straight on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so my voice came out and I think, go straight, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So you have to make decisions and sometimes you don't have a navigation system telling

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: you what to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You just have to make that decision with insufficient evidence and you're doing it all the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as a human and that's part of being sentient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so that kind of action and belief on the basis of incomplete evidence is not something

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that I feel uncomfortable doing or that somehow my Christian commitments have forced me to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: do when I wouldn't have had to have done it otherwise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I would have had to do it anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so there's a sense in which I think it's important to see the breadth of meaning of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: faith and to recognize that, and certainly in the case of Christianity, it's trust and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: loyalty that are the key themes that we're called to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I mean, another interesting extension of that that you speak to is kind of loyalty

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is referring to a connection with something outside of yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I think you've spoken about like existentialism or even just atheism in general as leading

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: naturally to an individualism as a focus on the self and ideas that maybe the Christian

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: faith that can instill in you is allowing you to sort of look outside of yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So connection, I mean, loyalty fundamentally is about other beings and yeah, other beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I mean, I think, I don't know what it is in me, but I'm very much drawn to that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: idea and I think humans in general are drawn to that idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You can make all kinds of evolutionary arguments, all that kind of stuff, but people always

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: kind of tease me because I talk about love a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I mean, there's a lot of non-scientific things about love, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Like what the heck is that thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Why do we even need that thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It seems to be an annoying burden that we get so much joy in life from a connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: with other human beings, deep lasting connections with human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Same thing with loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Why do we get so much value and pleasure and strength and meaning from loyalty, from a

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: connection with somebody else, going through thick and thin with somebody else, going through

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: some hard times?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, some of the closest friends I have is going through some rough times together

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and that seems to make life deeply meaningful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, that resonates with me and obviously I would affirm it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think just to correct the implication that you made, I don't think it's necessarily the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: consequence of atheism that we lose track of those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I think that atheists can be loyal, okay, if you like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The question more often comes up in the context of where does morality come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And loyalty, I think, and duty are related to one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If we have loyalty to someone, then we have a duty to them, okay, as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think that insofar as we see ourselves as having some kinds, any kinds of duties

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or moral compulsions with respect to our relationships to other people, I think it's a question that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: always arises, well, where do these come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And there are various approaches that people have towards deciding what makes ethics or

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: morality moral, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I do think it's the case that it's very hard to ground morality in any kind of absolute

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: way or persuasive way in mere human relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so it's certainly the case that in Christianity, there is a sense in which morality and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: morality of morals comes from a transcendent place, from a transcendent deity, and that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we ground the compelling force of morals on God more than we do on individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Because after all, if you've got nothing but other people, why should you treat your neighbor

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: well?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Why shouldn't you defraud your neighbor if it's good for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, you can construct all kinds of arguments, and some of them are obviously arguments that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are commonplace in religion too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You should do as you would be done by and all this kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But none of that seems any more than mere pragmatism to most people, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so that's one of the things that Nietzsche amongst others really identified.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If God is dead, if the idea of God is grounding our moral behavior is no longer viable in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the West, which Nietzsche thought that it wasn't, okay, then what does ground it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And he had no good answer for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In fact, he claimed there was no answer, but then he couldn't live with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so he invented the idea of the ubermensch, this superior human being, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And this was a different way of trying to ground morality, not a very successful one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You could argue that it's a forerunner of the sort of racism of Hitler's regime and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: so forth that we've in the West thankfully shied away from in the past half or three

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: quarters of a century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think it is the case that Christianity gives me a basis for my moral beliefs that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is more than mere pragmatism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, but there is a, so stepping outside of all of that, there does seem to be a powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: stabilizing, like we humans are able to hold ideas together, like in a distributed way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: outside of whether God exists or not or any of that, just our ability to kind of converge

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: together towards a set of beliefs into sometimes into tribes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's kind of, I don't know if it's inherent to being human beings, I hope not, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: now if I look on Twitter and there's the red team and the blue team, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's almost like it's some kind of TV show that we're living in, that people get into

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: these tribes and they hold a set of beliefs that sometimes don't, I mean, they are beliefs

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for the sake of holding those beliefs and we get this intimate connection between each

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: other for sharing those beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And we spoke to the things about loyalty and love and that's the thing that people feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: inside the tribe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it seems very human that within that tribe, those beliefs don't necessarily always have

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to be connected to anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's just the fact that, you know, I've did sports my whole life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Whenever you're on a team, the bond you get with other people on the team is incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the actual sport is often the silliest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I don't play ball sports anymore, but the ball, when I played like soccer or

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: tennis, I mean, all those sports are silly, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You're playing with a little ball, but there's the bond you get is so deeply meaningful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I just, it's interesting to me on the sociological level that it's possible to be whatever the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: beliefs of religion is, whatever they're actually grounded in, they might have a power in themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think there is tribalism everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think tribalism in the US at the moment is rather difficult to bear from my point

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And it's, I think, fed by the internet and social media and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But historically, tribalism has been a trait and remains a trait in humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The genius of Christianity is that it supersedes tribalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, yes, when the Hebrews thought about Yahweh, initially they thought about him as

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: their tribal deity, just like the tribal deities round about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And yet from early on in Hebrew history, the crucial thing that Yahweh came to mean, or

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I would say revealed of himself to them was that he wasn't just a tribal deity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: He was the God that created the whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if he is the God of the whole thing, then he's not just the God of the Hebrews, or in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the case of Americans, God is not just the God of Americans, he's the God of everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that is in a way the most amazing transcending of tribal loyalties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And one of the crucial occasions in the New Testament, when the Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the apostles and the disciples speak in other tongues, and there are people from all the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: countries round about, hear them in their own languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so whether you take that as factual or not, that is a statement of the transcendent

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: aspects of Christianity, or the claimed transcendent aspects of Christianity, that it transcends

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's certainly something which I find appealing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: When I kind of touch on this topic in my own mind, one of the hardest questions is why

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is there suffering in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you have a good answer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I have some answers, but you're right that it is one of the toughest questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The problem of pain or the problem of suffering or the problem of theodicy, as theologians

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: call it, is probably one of the toughest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's important to say that there are certain types of answers to this question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: but there are aspects of this question to which there is no intellectual answer that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is going to satisfy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the fact of the matter is, when I'm speaking to an audience, let's say at some kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: lecture, I can be sure that there are people in that audience who are either personally

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: suffering, they've got illness, they've got pains, maybe they're facing death, or someone

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in their family is in similar sorts of situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So suffering is a reality, and there is nothing that I can say that is going to solve their

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: feeling of agony and angst and maybe despair in those types of situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There is really only one thing that I think humans can do for one another in those kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of situations, and that is simply to be there, to be there alongside your friend or your

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: colleague or family member or whoever it might be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that's the only really sense in which we can give comfort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If we try to give intellectual solutions to these problems, we're going to be like the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: comforters that were in the book of Job in the Bible, who brought no comfort to Job himself

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: with their intellectual answers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But if they had been there, and some of them were there, they sat alongside, that is some

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: level of comfort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And after all, that's the meaning of the word compassion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It means to suffer alongside of somebody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I would say first off, what does a Christian say about suffering?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The first thing a Christian should say is compassion is all that really counts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And what's more, we say that God has acted in compassion towards us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That is to say, he has suffered with us in the person of Jesus Christ.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And when we see the passion of Jesus, we recognize that God takes suffering deadly seriously,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: has taken it so seriously that he's been willing to come and be a part of his creation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in the person of Jesus Christ and suffer death, the most horrible death on the cross, for

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: our benefit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's one side of suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But the philosophical question remains, surely if God is good and God is omnipotent, benevolent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: why doesn't he take away all the suffering?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Why doesn't he cause miracles to occur that will take away all this suffering?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think there are some good answers to that question in the following sense, that we live

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in a world where the consistency of the world is an absolutely crucial part of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The fact that our world behaves reproducibly in the main is absolutely essential for the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: integrity of our lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Without it, we wouldn't exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so there is a sense in which the integrity of creation calls for there being consistent

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: behavior, which these days we think of as being the laws of nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so the consistent behavior of nature is very, very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's what enables us to be what we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if you're calling upon God in your critique of why isn't this benevolent creator fixing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: things, one answer is he's fixed things in a certain sense to have an integrity in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that integrity is the best thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's the way we have our existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's the way we live and move and have our being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And if you want something different, you've got to show that there is a way in which you

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: could invent a world that is better, that it has the integrity that we need to exist

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and to be able to think and love and be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But you are going to do it better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the atheists think that maybe they have got a better idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But if they thought about it a bit more carefully, they'd realize no one has put forward a better

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So another way to say that, I mean, is that suffering is an integral part of a consistent

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So in a philosophical sense, the full richness and the beauty of our experience would not

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: be as beautiful, would not be as rich if there was no suffering in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is that possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I think you said two different things that aren't exactly the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: One is that suffering is an integral part of our experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That might be considered a challenge to certain types of Christian theology or even Jewish

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: theology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Because Christians talk about the fall and talk about Adam and Eve in the garden and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: have a vision of there being some kind of perception or perfection from which we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: fallen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think there is a perfection from which we've fallen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I don't think that perfection is some kind of physical perfection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In other words, I don't subscribe personally to the view that some Christians do that there

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: was some state prior to the fall in which death did not occur.
