metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think that that's consistent with science as we know it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think that death, for example, has been part of the biological world and the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as a whole from billions of years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So just to be clear about that, on the other hand, if that's the case, then certainly in

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that sense at the very least, suffering or at least death is part of the biological existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that probably seems so completely obvious to somebody who is au fait with science, whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: they're a scientist or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So and I apologize if I'm interrupting, but it's the obvious reality of our life today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But there's a lot of people I think is currently in vogue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I talked to quite a few folks who kind of see as the goal of many of our pursuits as

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to extend life indefinitely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's sort of a dream for many people is to live forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But in the technological world, in the engineering world, in the scientific world, I mean, that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the big dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: To me, it feels like that's not a dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I certainly would like to live forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Like that's the initial feeling, the instinctual feeling, because life is so amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But then if you actually kind of like you've presented it, if you actually live that kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of life, you would realize that that's actually a step backwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's a step down from the experience of this life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In my sense, that death is an essential part of life, about essential part of this experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: death of all things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So the fact that things end somehow in a scarcity of things, somehow create the beauty of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: experience that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, transhumanism doesn't look very attractive to me either, but it also doesn't look very

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: feasible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's a whole big topic that I'm not exactly an expert, but I'm of a certain age where

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: my mortality is more pressing or more obvious to me than it once was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I don't dread that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't see that as, in a certain sense, even the enemy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You're not afraid of death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I'm afraid of lots of things in a conceptual way, but it doesn't keep me awake at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think like most people, I'm more afraid of pain than I am of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I don't want to put myself forward as some kind of hero that doesn't worry about these

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I do think, and maybe this is part of my Christian outlook, that there is life beyond

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the grave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I don't think that it's life in this universe or certainly not in this body and maybe not

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in a certain sense in this mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Christian belief in the afterlife is that we will be resurrected, we will in a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sense be with God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't know what that means, and I don't think anybody else really quite knows what

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But there are lots of ways that over history, people, artists, and writers and so forth

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: have pictured it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And these are all perhaps some of them helpful ways of thinking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you think it's possible to know what happens after we die?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think we find out by near-death experiences or those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think that we have sufficient, I feel I have sufficient information, if you like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in terms of God's revelation to be confident that I will go somewhere else, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it won't be here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: To me, the aspirations of transhumanism are horrific.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it would be a nightmare, not a dream, a nightmare to be somehow downloaded into

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a computer and live one's life like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Because it completely discounts the integrity of our bodies as well as our minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We aren't just disembodied minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It would not be me that was in the computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It would be something else if that kind of download were possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Of course, it isn't possible, and it's a very long way from being possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But you know, amazing things happen, so we shouldn't be too certain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So this is a place that, again, maybe taking a slight step outside wherever philosophizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Let me ask you about human level or superhuman level intelligence, the artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What do you make from almost a religious perspective that we've been talking about of the spiritual

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: special aspect of human nature, of us creating intelligence systems that exhibit some elements

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of that human nature?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is that something, again, like we were talking about with transhumanism, there's a feasibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: question of how hard is it to actually build machines that are human level intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: or have something like consciousness or have all those kinds of human qualities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And then there's the, do we want to do that kind of thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So in both of those directions, what do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So since your podcast is called AI, I don't want to offend too many of your listeners

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think one should be a little bit more modest about one's claims for AI than have

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: typically been the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think that actually a lot of people in AI are somewhat chastened, and so there are more

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: modest claims than are common with the transhumanists and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I used to play chess when I was a kid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I was pretty good at it, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Won competitions and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I'm talking about when I was in high school, I thought it was pretty unlikely that a computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: would be able to become good at chess, but I was dead wrong, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so-

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: How did that make you feel, by the way, when T-Blue-Big-Kid-Casparov?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I stopped playing chess seriously when I encountered computers that could beat me, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I still play with my grandchildren a little bit, but yeah, it seemed like in a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sense it became a solved problem when AI was able to do it better than I could.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So I think that there are ways in which today we've seen computers do things which historically

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: were regarded as being very characteristic of human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And in that sense, there is some success to AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I also think that there are certain things which one might think of as being AI, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are completely widespread in our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm thinking about the internet, search engines, and so forth, which are enormously influential

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and obviously do things more powerfully than any individual human or even any combination

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of humans could do, much faster, and accessing databases and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: All of this is outstripped human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm not sure the extent to which that is really intelligence in the way that was traditionally

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: meant, but it's certainly amazingly facile and it multiplies our ability to access human

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: knowledge and data and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So is that something, is that into the realm of something we should be concerned about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So in the realm of religion, you talk about what is good, what is evil, what is right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: what is wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You have a set of morals, set of beliefs, and when you have an entity come into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: picture that has quite a bit of power, if we potentially look into the future, and intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and capability, do you think there's something that religion can say about artificial intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Or is that something we shouldn't worry about until it arrives, you think, just like with

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the chess program?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Religious writers have thought about this for centuries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's been a long debate about what was historically called the plurality of worlds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It was actually more about whether there are places where other intelligent creatures live

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: than it was about us creating them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think it's largely the same question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's almost like aliens, like other intelligents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So if there is other intelligent life in the universe, what is its relationship to God?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That is, in a certain sense, the puzzle that religious thinkers and writers have thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: about for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And there's a whole range of different opinions about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, personally, I think it's an interesting question, but it's not a very pressing question

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think the same way about the question of what happens if we're able to build a sentient

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: robot, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's an interesting question, and we'll have to think about it when that happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think we're still quite a ways away from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And so I don't have a good answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think there's a literature that one could tap to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you want to start early on the question?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, let me ask you another impossible question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: From a religious or from a personal perspective, what do you think is consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: This subjective experience that we seem to be having.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Does the Christian religion have something to say about consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Does your own, when you look in the mirror, do you have a sense of what is consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think the Bible doesn't have much in the way of answers about that directly in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sense that you're perhaps asking it, which is more like I think you're asking for some

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: kind of quasi-scientific or maybe indeed scientific description of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's really looking for one, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think that it's an interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's actually a jump too far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think we don't even know the answer to the question, what is the mind, let alone consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So if you distinguish between those two things, I think the question that's being addressed

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: more directly scientifically as well as in other ways, it is what is the mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that is certainly a very topical question even in places like MIT, which is not his

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: historically involved with philosophical questions, the people doing neuroscience and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's a very important question and I think that we're going to find that we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: not computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In other words, I think the commonplace theory of what mind is, is generally speaking by

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: analogy that we are basically wetware, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That we're some computer-like entity and that the analogy to digital computers is a pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: decent one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, that's of course a viewpoint which drives the aspirations of the transhumanists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: They so much believe that our minds are nothing other than in a certain sense, some kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: implementation of software in biology that they say to themselves, well, of course we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: going to be able to download it into a digital computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think it's most likely that quantum mechanics is very important in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It seems most unlikely that it's not to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I know that that's contrary to the opinions of many people, but that's my view and it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: also a view, for example, of people like Roger Penrose and people like that who've written

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: about it rather extensively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If that's the case, then really my mind is not reducible to some kind of software which

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: can be considered to be portable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It is so connected to the hardware of my body that the two are inseparable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If that is in fact what we find, as I suspect will be the case, then the aspirations of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the transhumanists will be very long in coming, if at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think that actually physics and chemistry are in a sense involved with the brain and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: within the mind, but not in a very simple way like the computer analogy, in a much more

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: complicated way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I also think that it's philosophically ignorant to speak as if when and if the actions of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the brain are understood at the physical and chemical level, that the mind will vanish

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as a concept that will just say, we're nothing but brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Of course it won't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It may well be that our mind is an emergent phenomenon that comes out of the physics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: chemistry and biology, but it's also something that we have to encounter and take seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's not the case that the mind is reducible to nothing but physics and chemistry, even

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: if it's embedded continuously into physics and chemistry, as I rather suspect it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's my own view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Another way of putting it is that the mind or the soul is not something added into humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as might have been the viewpoint historically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I do think there is something added to humans, but it's not the mind, it's the spirit, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that takes us beyond the physical, it takes us beyond this universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I don't think that consciousness, the mind, et cetera, et cetera, is that thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: which is necessarily added in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It could be emergent in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm not a substance dualist in that sense, if you want to put it philosophically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The mind and the intelligence and consciousness can be these emergent things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you have a hope, a sense that science could help us get pretty far down the road of understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: all this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Oh, we will get much further than we have, and it'll be interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Right now, our methods of diagnosing the human brain are extremely primitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The resolution that we have that comes out of NMR and brain scans and so forth is miserable

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: compared with what we need in order to understand the brain at the cellular level, let alone

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: at the atomic level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But we're making progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's relatively slow progress, but it's progress, and people are working on it, and we're going

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to get better at it, and we will find out very interesting things as we do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The time resolution is also completely hopeless compared with what we need to understand the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's a long way to go, and we will get better at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I'm not at all worried, as some people are, and some people speak as if it's a good

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: thing, that somehow the concepts of humanity and the mind and religion and consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: are going to vanish because we're going to have complete physicochemical description

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of the brain in the near future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We're not going to have that, and secondly, even if we had it, the mind and all these

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: other things aren't going to vanish because of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I find kind of compelling the notion that whoever created this universe and us

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: did so to understand itself, himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, there's a powerful self-reflection notion to this whole experiment that we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a part of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I certainly think that God takes delight in His creation and that it was created for

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that delight as much as it was for any other reason, and that therefore, there's reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to be hopeful and awestruck by the creation, whether it's on the very small or on the very

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: large.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I'm not sure if you're familiar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's something called the simulation hypothesis that's been fun to talk about with computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: scientists and so on, which is a kind of thought experiment that proposes that the entirety

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of the world around us is a kind of computer program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's a simulation, and then we're living inside it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think from a certain perspective, that could be consistent with a religious view of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, you could just use different terms, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It feels like a more modern, updated version of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What's your sense of the simulation hypothesis?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you find it interesting, useful to think about it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you find it ridiculous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you find it fun?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What are your thoughts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's fun, and it's been, of course, the subject of various movies, some of which are very

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: well known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think it makes sense to think of it as a simulation hypothesis in the sense that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we're really lying on banks of beds, having our energy drained away from us, and the simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is going on in our individual brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That makes no sense to me at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think that's what's meant by the simulation hypothesis as you're using it now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There is very little distinction between saying that an intelligent creator has set up the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: universe according to his will and his plan and set it in motion and is allowing it to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: run out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Maybe, as Christians say, he's sustaining it, actually, by his word of power, it says

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in the book, the letter to Hebrews, in this amazingly consistent and integrated way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think there's very much difference between saying that and saying that it's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I think it's almost the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think it's important to recognize that the simulation in that concept, the simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and the creation of the universe are the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In other words, it's a simulation that is billions of light years across.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: There's a sense in which it helps one understand, especially if you're not religious, that there

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is something outside of the world that we live in, that there is something bigger than

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: the world we live in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, that's just another perspective that humbles you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So, in that sense, it's a powerful thought experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: One shortcoming of that is the following of the analogy, is this, that we think of a simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as something taking place in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's taking place in my computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think that's the right analogy for a Christian view of creation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think it's taking place in some other universe that God has made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think maybe it's taking place in the mind of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Christians might hypothesize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I think that it's important to recognize that Christian theology at any rate is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: God is not one of the entities in the universe and presumably therefore is very different

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: from a simulation that we might run on a computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Let me ask you, Adam and Eve, even Adam ate of the fruit of the tree of knowledge of good

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Is this story meaningful to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does this story mean to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, it is meaningful to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I take the writings of the Bible very seriously and I think that most Christians regard them

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: as having some kind of authoritative role in their faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What do I get from it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean, I think the most important thing that Christians get from the story of Adam and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Eve and eating the apple and so forth is that the relationship between humans and God is

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: broken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Has been broken by man's disobedience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That's what the story of Adam and Eve and the apple is all about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That broken relationship is for Christians what Jesus came to redeem, came to overcome

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that brokenness and restore that relationship with God to some extent at any rate on earth

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: and ultimately in eternity to restore it fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So that's really what Christians mean and gain from the story of Adam and Eve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Of course, lots of people ask the questions about how literally should we take these stories

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of particularly the first few chapters of Genesis, which is an important question, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we tend to get bogged down with it a bit too much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think we should take away the message and I think what actually we would have seen if

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we'd been there is something which is a matter of speculation and it's certainly not terribly

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: important from the point of view of Christian theology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But it seems like a very important moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: As a man of faith, do you wish that, I think it was Eve first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Yeah, it was Eve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you wish that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It was an apple by the way, it was just a fruit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It was a fruit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You said it very carefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It was the fruit of the tree, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Do you wish they wouldn't have eaten of the tree?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: This is back to our discussion of suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Was that an essential thing that needed to happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: You're going to have to read Paradise Lost to get your answer to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Beautifully put.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, let me ask the biggest question, one that you also touch in your book, but one

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that I ask every once in a while is what is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: The meaning of my life is many different things, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But they are all kind of centered around relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I mean for a Christian, one's relationship with God is a crucial part of the meaning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of life, but one's relationship with one's family, wife, parents, children, grandchildren

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: in my case, and so forth, those are crucially important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: These are all the places where people, whether they're religious or not, find meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But ultimately, I think a person who has faith in a creator who we think has an intention,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: many intentions, but a will in respect of the world as a whole, that's a crucial part

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And the idea that my life might have some small significance in the plan of that creator

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: is an amazingly powerful idea that brings meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I tell a story in my book that when I was a student before I became a Christian, I read

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: a philosophy book whose approximate title was What is the Meaning of Life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: That book basically said there is no meaning to life, you have to make up the meaning as

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: you go along.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think that's probably the predominant secular view these days, that there is no

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: real meaning, but you can make up a meaning and that will give you meaning into your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't subscribe to that view anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I think there is more meaning than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: But I do think that those things which give meaning to our life are very important and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: we should emphasize them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And you have said that as the part of that meaning, as the part of your faith, love and

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: loyalty are key parts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: So can you try to say what is love and loyalty?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does it mean to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: What does it look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: If you were to give advice to your children, grandchildren of what to look for in looking

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: for loyalty and love, what would you try to say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Well, I think it's something like yielding your will or desire to another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: It's valuing others more highly or at least as highly as yourself, but that's just the

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: start of it because true love, you reach a point where you feel compelled by the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And that I think to some people sounds very scary, but actually, it's terrifically liberating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think that love then brings you into service towards another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I'm reminded of the phrase from the Anglican prayer book where it talks about Jesus whose

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: service is perfect freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: In other words, for us Christians to serve God is what perfects our freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And I think there is an amazing love is in part captivity, but in a kind of paradoxical

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: sense it's also an amazing freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Love is freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: I don't think there's a better way to end it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: We started with fusion energy and ending on love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Ian, it was a huge honor to talk to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Thank you so much for your time today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Thanks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Arthur C. Clarke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Finally I would like to assure my many Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, Jewish, and Muslim friends

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: that I am sincerely happy that the religion which chance has given you has contributed

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: to your peace of mind and often as Western medical science now reluctantly admits to

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: your physical well-being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Perhaps it is better to be unsane and happy than sane and unhappy, but it is the best

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: of all to be sane and happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

body.input: Whether our descendants can achieve that goal will be the greatest challenge of the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Hutchinson: Nuclear Fusion, Plasma Physics, and Religion | Lex Fridman Podcast #112

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: maybe the most important question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: What is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: What gives your life fulfillment, purpose, happiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: and meaning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Why do you think we're here on this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Given all the big bang and the infinities of photons

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that we've talked about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: All I would say, I think it's not a stupid question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: I mean, there are some people, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: many of my colleagues who are scientists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: and they say, well, that's a stupid question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Meaning, yeah, well, we're just here

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: because things came together and produced life and so what.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: I think there's more to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: But what there is that's more to it, I have really much idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And it might be somehow connected to the mechanisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: of consciousness that we've been talking about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: the mystery there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: It's connected with all sorts of, yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: I think these things are tied up in ways which are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: you see, I tend to think the mystery of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: is tied up with the mystery of quantum mechanics

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: and how it fits in with the classical world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And that's all to do with the mystery of quantum mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: With the mystery of complex numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And there are mysteries there

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: which look like mathematical mysteries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: but they seem to have a bearing

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: on the way the physical world operates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: We're scratching the surface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: We have a long, huge way to go

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: before we really understand that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And it's a beautiful idea that the depth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: the mathematical depth could be discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And then there's tragedies of ghettos and completeness

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: along the way that we'll have to somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: figure our ways around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: So, Roger, it was a huge honor to talk to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Thank you so much for your time today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: It's been my pleasure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation

body.input: with Roger Penrose.
