body.input: or simply connect with me on Twitter at LexFreedman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words of wisdom

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that Roger Penrose wrote in his book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: The Emperor's New Mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Beneath all this technicality is the feeling

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that it is indeed quote unquote obvious

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that the conscious mind cannot work like a computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: even though much of what is involved

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: in mental activity might do so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: This is the kind of obviousness that a child can see,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: though the child may later in life become brow-beaten

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: into believing that the obvious problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: are quote unquote non-problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: to be argued into nonexistence by careful reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: and clever choices of definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Children sometimes see things clearly

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that are obscured in later life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: We often forget the wonder that we felt as children

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: when the cares of the quote unquote real world

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: have begun to settle on our shoulders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Children are not afraid to pose basic questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: that may embarrass us as adults to ask,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: what happens to each of our streams of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: after we die?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Where was it before we were born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Might we become or have been someone else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Why do we perceive it all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Why are we here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Why is there a universe here at all

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: in which we can actually be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: These are puzzles that tend to come

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: with the awakenings of awareness in any of us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: and no doubt with the awakening of self-awareness

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: within whichever creature or other entity it first came.

metadata.title: Podcast: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85

body.input: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

body.input: The following is a conversation with Rodney Brooks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: one of the greatest roboticists in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He led the Computer Science

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at MIT,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: then co-founded iRobot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which is one of the most successful robotics companies ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Then he co-founded Rethink Robotics

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that created some amazing collaborative robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: like Baxter and Sawyer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Finally, he co-founded Robust.ai,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: whose mission is to teach robots common sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which is a lot harder than it sounds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: To support this podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: As a side note, let me say that Rodney

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: is someone I've looked up to for many years

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: in my now over two-decade journey in robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because, one, he's a legit great engineer

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: of real-world systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and two, he's not afraid to state controversial opinions

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that challenge the way we see the AI world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But, of course, while I agree with him

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: on some of his critical views of AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I don't agree with some others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and he's fully supportive of such disagreement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Nobody ever built anything great by being fully agreeable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's always respect and love behind our interactions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and when a conversation is recorded

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: like it was for this podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I think a little bit of disagreement is fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and here is my conversation with Rodney Brooks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What is the most amazing or beautiful robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that you've ever had the chance to work with?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I think it was Domo,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which was made by one of my grad students,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Aaron Edsinger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It now sits in Daniela Rus' office, director of CSAIL,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and it was just a beautiful robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and Aaron was really clever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He didn't give me a budget ahead of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He didn't tell me what he was going to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He just started spending money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He spent a lot of money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He and Jeff Weber, who is a mechanical engineer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: who Aaron insisted he bring with him

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: when he became a grad student,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: built this beautiful, gorgeous robot, Domo,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which is an upper torso humanoid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: two arms, three-fingered hands,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and face eyeballs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: not the eyeballs, but everything else,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: series elastic actuators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You can interact with it, cable-driven.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: All the motors are inside, and it's just gorgeous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The eyeballs are actuated too or no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh yeah, the eyeballs are actuated with cameras.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It had a visual attention mechanism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: looking when people came in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and looking at their face and talking with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Wow, was it amazing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The beauty of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You said what was the most beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What is the most beautiful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's just mechanically gorgeous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: As everything Aaron builds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: it's always been mechanically gorgeous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's just exquisite in the detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We're talking about mechanically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: literally the amount of actuators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The actuators, the cables.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He anodizes different parts, different colors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and it just looks like a work of art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What about the face?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you find the face beautiful in robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: When you make a robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: it's making a promise for how well it will be able to interact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I always encourage my students not to over-promise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Even with its essence, the thing it presents,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: it should not over-promise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, so the joke I make, which I think you'll get,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: is if your robot looks like Albert Einstein,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: it should be as smart as Albert Einstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The only thing in Domo's face is the eyeballs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because that's all it can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It can look at you and pay attention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's not like one of those Japanese robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that looks exactly like a person at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But see, the thing is, us humans and dogs too,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: don't just use eyes as attentional mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They also use it to communicate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's part of the communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Like a dog can look at you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: look at another thing and look back at you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that designates that we're going to be looking at that thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, or intent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You know, on both Baxter and Sawyer at Rethink Robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: they had a screen with graphic eyes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: so it wasn't actually where the cameras were pointing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But the eyes would look in the direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: it was about to move its arm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So people in the factory nearby

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: were not surprised by its motions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because it gave that intent away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Before we talk about Baxter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which I think is a beautiful robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And so he had to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Otherwise, the other drivers would just beat them all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So you co-founded I robot, as we mentioned, one of the most successful robotics companies ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What are you most proud of with that company and the approach you took to robotics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, there's something I'm quite proud of there, which may be a surprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I was still on the board when this happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was March 2011.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And we sent robots to Japan and they were used to shut help shut down the Fukushima Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant, which was everything was well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I've been there since I was there in 2014 to the robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Some of the robots were still there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I was I was proud that we were able to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Why were we able to do that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And and, you know, people have said, well, you know, Japan is so good at robotics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was because we had had about sixty five hundred robots deployed in Iraq and Afghanistan teleopped,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: but with intelligence dealing with roadside bombs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We had it was at that time nine years of infield experience with the robots in harsh conditions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: whereas the Japanese robots, which were, you know, getting, you know, this goes back to what annoys me so much, getting all the hype.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Look at that. Look at that Honda robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It can walk well, the features here couldn't do a thing because they weren't deployed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But we had deployed in really harsh conditions for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We were able to to do something very positive in a very bad situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What about just the simple and for people who don't know, one of the things that I robot is great is the Roomba vacuum cleaner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What about the simple robot that that is the Roomba quote unquote simple that's deployed in tens of millions of tens of millions of homes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What do you think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, I make the joke that I started out life as a pure mathematician and turned into vacuum cleaner salesman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So if you're going to be an entrepreneur, be ready for that, be ready to do anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I was, you know, there was a there was a wacky lawsuit that I got the post for not too many years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I was the only one who had e-mail from the 1990s and no one in the company had it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I went and went through my e-mail and and it reminded me of, you know, the joy of what we were doing and what was I doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What was I doing at the time we were building building the Roomba?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: One of the things was we had this incredibly tight budget because we wanted to put it on the shelves at two hundred dollars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There was another home cleaning robot at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was the Electrolux Trilobite, which sold for two thousand euros.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And to us, that was not going to be a consumer product.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So we had reason to believe that two hundred dollars was a was a thing that people would buy at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That was our aim. But that meant we had, you know, that's that's on the shelf making profit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That means the cost of goods has to be minimal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I find all these e-mails of me going, you know, I'd be in Taipei for a MIT meeting and I'd stay a few extra days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'd go down to Shenzhou and talk to these little tiny companies, lots of little tiny companies outside of TSMC, Taiwan Semiconductor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation, which let all these little companies be fabulous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They didn't have to have their own fab so they could innovate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And they were they were building their innovations were to build stripped down sixty eight oh twos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Sixty eight or two is what was in an Apple one. Get rid of half the silicon and still have it be viable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I previously got some of those for some earlier failed products of a robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And then that was in Hong Kong going to all these companies that, you know, they weren't gaming in the current sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There were these hand-held games that you would play or birthday cards because we had about a 50 cent budget for computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I'm tracking from place to place, looking at their chips, looking at what they'd removed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh, the interrupt. The interrupt handling is too weak for a general purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I was doing deep technical detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And then I found this one from a company called Windbond, which had and I'd forgotten it had this much RAM.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It had five hundred and twelve bytes of RAM and it was in our budget and it had all the capabilities we needed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yes. You excited. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I was reading all these emails. Colin, I found this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So did you think did you ever think that you guys could be so successful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Like eventually this company would be so successful. Did you could you possibly have imagined?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: No, we never did think that we'd had 14 failed business models up to 2002 and then we had two winners same year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: No. And then, you know, we I remember the board because by this time we had some venture capital in the board went along with us building

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: some robots for aiming at the Christmas 2002 market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And we went three times over what they authorized and built 70,000 of them and sold them all in that first because we released on September 18th.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And they were all sold by Christmas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So it was so we were gutsy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But but yeah, you didn't think this will take over the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, this is so a lot of amazing robotics companies have gone under over the past few decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Why do you think it's so damn hard to run a successful robotics company?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's a few things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: One is expectations of capabilities by the founders that are off base.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The founders, not the consumer, the founders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The expectations of what can be delivered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Mispricing and what a customer thinks is a valid price is not rational, necessarily. Yeah. And expectations of customers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And just the sheer hardness of getting people to adopt a new technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I've suffered from all three of these. You know, I've had more failures and successes in terms of companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I've suffered from all three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So do you think one day there will be a robotics company and by robotics company, I mean, where your primary source of income is from robots,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that will be a trillion plus dollar company. And so what would that company do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I can't, you know, because I'm still starting robot companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm not making any such predictions in my own mind. I'm not thinking about a trillion dollar company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And by the way, I don't think, you know, in the 90s, anyone was thinking that Apple would ever be a trillion dollar company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So these are very hard to predict.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But sorry to interrupt. But don't you, because I kind of have a vision in a small way and a big vision in a small way that I see that there will be robots in the home at scale, like Roomba, but more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that's trillion dollar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Right. And I think there's a real market pull for them because of the demographic inversion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You know, who's going to do all the stuff for the older people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's too many. You know, I'm leading here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's going to be too many of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But we don't have capable enough robots to make that economic argument at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do I expect that that will happen? Yes, I expect it will happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I got to tell you, we introduced the Roomba in 2002 and I stayed another nine years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We were always trying to find what the next home robot would be in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Still today, the primary product of 20 years late, almost 20 years later, 19 years later, the primary product is still the Roomba.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I robot hasn't found the next one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you think it's possible for one person in the garage to build it versus like Google launching Google self-driving car that turns into Waymo?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you think this is almost like what it takes to build a successful robotics company?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you think it's possible to go from the ground up or is it just too much capital investment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. So it's very hard to get there without a lot of capital.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And we're starting to see, you know, fair chunks of capital for some robotics companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You know, Series Bs, I just saw one yesterday for $80 million, I think it was, for covariant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But it can take real money to get into these things and you may fail along the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I certainly failed at Rethink Robotics and we lost $150 million in capital there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So, OK, so Rethink Robotics is another amazing robotics company you co-founded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So what was the vision there? What was the dream?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And what are you most proud of with Rethink Robotics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm most proud of the fact that we got robots out of the cage in factories that was safe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: absolutely safe for people and robots to be next to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So these are robotic arms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Robotics arms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They're able to pick up stuff and interact with humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, and that humans could retask them without writing code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And now that's sort of become an expectation for a lot of other little companies

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and big companies are advertising they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's both an interface problem and also a safety problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. So I'm most proud of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I let myself be talked out of what I wanted to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And you know, I can't replay the tape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I can't replay it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Maybe if I'd been stronger on...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I remember the day. I remember the exact meeting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Can you take me through that meeting?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. So I'd said that I'd set as a target for the company that we were going to build $3,000 robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: with force feedback that was safe for people to be around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Wow. That was my goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And we built... So we started in 2008 and we had prototypes built of plastic, plastic gearboxes

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and at a $3,000 lifetime or $3,000, I was saying we're going to go after

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: not the people who already have robot arms in factories, the people who would never have a robot arm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We're going to go after a different market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So we don't have to meet their expectations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And so we're going to build it out of plastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It doesn't have to have a 35,000 hour lifetime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's going to be so cheap that it's OPEX, not CAPEX.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And so we had a prototype that worked reasonably well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: but the control engineers were complaining about these plastic gearboxes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: the beautiful little planetary gearbox,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: but we could use something called serious elastic actuators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We embedded them in there. We can measure forces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We knew when we hit something, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The control engineers were saying, yeah, but this is torque ripple

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because these plastic gears, they're not great gears.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And this ripple and trying to do force control around this ripple is so hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I'm not going to name names, but I remember one of the mechanical engineers saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: we'll just build a metal gearbox with spur gears and it'll take six weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We'll be done. Problem solved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Two years later, we got the spur gearbox working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We cost reduced it every possible way we could, but now the price went up to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and then the CEO at the time said, well, we have to have two arms, not one arm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So our first robot product, Baxter, now cost $25,000.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And the only people who were going to look at that were people who had arms in factories

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because that was somewhat cheaper for two arms than arms in factories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But they were used to 0.1 millimeter reproducibility of motion and certain velocities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I kept thinking, but that's not what we're giving you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You don't need position repeatability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You use force control like a human does. No, but we want that repeatability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: All the other robots have that repeatability. Why don't you have that repeatability?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So can you clarify, force control is you can grab the arm and you can move it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, you can move it around. But suppose you... Can you see that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Suppose you want to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Suppose this thing is a precise thing that's got to fit here in this right angle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Under position control, you have fixtured where this is, you know where this is precisely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and you just move it, and it goes there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: If force control, you would do something like, slidle over here till we feel that and slide it in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that's how a human gets precision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They use force feedback and get the things to mate rather than just go straight to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Couldn't convince our customers who were in factories and were used to thinking about things a certain way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And they wondered, wondered, wondered. So then we said, okay, we're going to build an arm that gives you that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So now we ended up building a $35,000 robot with one arm with... Oh, what are they called?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: A certain sort of gearbox made by a company whose name I can't remember right now, but it's the name of the gearbox.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But it's got torque ripple in it. So now there was an extra two years of solving the problem of doing the force with the torque ripple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So we had to do the thing we had avoided for the plastic gearboxes. We ended up having to do... The robot was now overpriced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that was during tuition from the very beginning. You're opening a door to solve a lot of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You're eventually going to have to solve this problem anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. And also I was aiming at a low price to go into a different market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Low price. $3,000 would be amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. I think we could have done it for five. But you talked about setting the goal a little too far for the engineers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So why would you say that company not failed, but went under?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We had buyers and there's this thing called the Committee on Foreign Investment in the US, CFIUS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that had previously been invoked twice around where the government could stop foreign money coming into a US company based on defense requirements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We went through judge's elegance multiple times. We were going to get acquired.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But every consortium had Chinese money in it. And all the bankers would say at the last minute, you know, this isn't going to get past CFIUS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And the investors would go away. And then we had two buyers. We were about to run out of money. Two buyers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And one used heavy-handed legal stuff with the other one. Said they were going to take it and pay more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Dropped out when we were out of cash and then bought the assets at one thirtieth of the price they had offered a week before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was a tough week.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Does it hurt to think about an amazing company that didn't, like iRobot, didn't find a way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, it was tough. I said I was never going to start another company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I was pleased that everyone liked what we did so much that the team was hired by three companies within a week.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Everyone had a job in one of these three companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Some stayed in their same desks because another company came in and rented the space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I felt good about people not being out on the street.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So Baxter has a screen with a face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's a revolutionary idea for a robotic arm. How much opposition did you get?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, first, the screen was also used during codeless programming where you taught by demonstration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It showed you what its understanding of the task was. So it had two roles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Some customers hated it. And so we made it so that when the robot was running, it could be showing graphs of what was happening and not show the eyes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Other people, and some of them surprised me who they were, saying, well, this one doesn't look as human as the old one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We like the human looking. So there was a mixed bag.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But do you think that's a I don't know. I'm kind of disappointed whenever I talk to roboticists, like the best robotics people in the world, they seem to not want to do the eyes type of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They seem to see it as a machine as opposed to a machine that can also have a human connection. I'm not sure what to do with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It seems like a lost opportunity. I think the trillion dollar company will have to do the human connection very well, no matter what it does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, I agree. Can I ask you a ridiculous question? Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I might give a ridiculous answer. Do you think, well, maybe by way of asking the question, let me first mention that you're kind of critical of the idea of the Turing test as a test of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Let me first ask this question. Do you think we'll be able to build an AI system that humans fall in love with and it falls in love with the human? Like romantic love?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, we've had that with humans falling in love with cars, even back in the 50s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's a different love, right? Well, I think there's a lifelong partnership where you can communicate and grow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I think we're a long way from that. I think Blade Runner had the time scale totally wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. To me, honestly, the most difficult part is the thing that you said with the Marv X paradox is to create a human form that interacts and perceives the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But if we just look at a voice like the movie Her, or just like an Alexa type voice, I tend to think we're not that far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, for some people, maybe not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: As humans, as we think about the future, we always try to, and this is the premise of most science fiction movies, you've got the world just as it is today and you change one thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But that's the same with a self-driving car. You change one thing. No, everything changes. Everything grows together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So, surprisingly, it might be surprising to you or might not, I think the best movie about this stuff was Bicentennial Man. And what was happening there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was schmaltzy and you know, but what was happening there? As the robot was trying to become more human, the humans were adopting the technology of the robot and changing their bodies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So there was a convergence happening in a sense. So we will not be the same. We're already talking about genetically modifying our babies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's more and more stuff happening around that. We will want to modify ourselves even more for all sorts of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We put all sorts of technology in our bodies to improve it. I've got things in my ears so that I can sort of hear you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So we're always modifying our bodies. So I think it's hard to imagine exactly what it will be like in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But on the touring test side, do you think, forget about love for a second. Let's talk about just like the Alexa Prize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Actually, I was invited to be an interviewer for the Alexa Prize or whatever. That's in two days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Their idea is success looks like a person wanting to talk to an AI system for a prolonged period of time, like 20 minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: How far away are we? And why is it difficult to build an AI system with which you'd want to have a beer and talk for an hour or two hours?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Not for to check the weather or to check music, but just to talk as friends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. Well, we saw Weissenbaum back in the 60s with his program, Eliza, being shocked at how much people would talk to Eliza.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I remember in the 70s typing stuff to Eliza to see what it would come back with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I think right now, and this is a thing that Amazon's been trying to improve with Alexa, there is no continuity of topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You can't refer to what we talked about yesterday.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's not the same as talking to a person where this seems to be an ongoing existence, which changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We share moments together and they last in our memory together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah. There's none of that. And there's no sort of intention of these systems that they have any goal in life, even if it's to be happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They don't even have a semblance of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Now, I'm not saying this can't be done. I'm just saying I think this is why we don't feel that way about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's a sort of a minimal requirement. If you want the sort of interaction you're talking about, it's a minimal requirement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Whether it's going to be sufficient, I don't know. We haven't seen it yet. We don't know what it feels like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I tend to think it's not as difficult as solving intelligence, for example, and I think it's achievable in the near term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But on the Turing test, why don't you think the Turing test is a good test of intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh, because, you know, again, Turing, if you read the paper, Turing wasn't saying this is a good test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He was using a rhetorical device to argue that if you can't tell the difference between a computer and a person,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: you must say that the computer is thinking because you can't tell the difference when it's thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You can't say something different. What it has become is this sort of weird game of fooling people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So back at the AI lab in the late 80s, we had this thing that still goes on called the AI Olympics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And one of the events we had one year was the original imitation game as Turing talked about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because he starts by saying, can you tell whether it's a man or a woman? So we did that at the lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You'd go and type, and the thing would come back, and you had to tell whether it was a man or a woman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And one man came up with a question that he could ask, which was always a dead giveaway

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: of whether the other person was really a man or a woman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He would ask them, did you have green plastic toy soldiers as a kid? Yeah. What do you do with them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And a woman trying to be a man would say, oh, I lined them up. We had wars, we had battles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And the man just being a man said, I stomped on them. I burned them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So that's what the Turing test with computers has become. What's the trick question? That's why I say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's sort of devolved into this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Nevertheless, conversation not formulated as a test is a fascinatingly challenging dance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's a really hard problem. To me, conversation when non-posed as a test is a more intuitive illustration

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: how far away we are from solving intelligence than computer vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Computer vision is harder for me to pull apart. But with language, with conversation, you could see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Because language is so human. We don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's so human. We can so clearly see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Shit, you mentioned something I was going to go off on. Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, I have to ask you because you were the head of CSAIL, AI lab for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I don't know. To me, when I came to MIT, you're like one of the greats at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So what was that time like? And plus you're friends with, but you knew Minsky and all the folks there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: all the legendary AI people of which you're one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So what was that time like? What are memories that stand out to you from that time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: From your time at MIT, from the AI lab, from the dreams that the AI lab represented, to the actual revolutionary work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Let me tell you first a disappointment in myself. As I've been researching this book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and so many of the players were active in the 50s and 60s, I knew many of them when they were older.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I didn't ask them all the questions now I wish I had asked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'd sit with them on Thursday lunches, which we had a faculty lunch, and I didn't ask them so many questions that now I wish I had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Can I ask you that question? Because you wrote that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You wrote that you were fortunate to know and rub shoulders with many of the greats,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: those who founded AI robotics and computer science and the World Wide Web.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And you wrote that your big regret nowadays is that often I have questions for those who have passed on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I didn't think to ask them any of these questions, even as I saw them and said hello to them on a daily basis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So maybe also another question I want to ask, if you could talk to them today, what question would you ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, Rick Leiter, I would ask him. He had the vision for humans and computers working together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and he really founded that at DARPA, and he gave the money to MIT, which started Project MAC in 1963.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I would have talked to him about what the successes were, what the failures were, what he saw as progress, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I would have asked him more questions about that because now I could use it in my book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I think it's lost. It's lost forever. A lot of the motivations are lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I should have asked Marvin why he and Seymour Pappitt came down so hard on neural networks in 1968 in their book Perceptrons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because Marvin's PhD thesis was on neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: How do you make sense of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That book destroyed the field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you think he knew the effect that book would have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: All the theorems and negative theorems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's just the way of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But still, it's kind of tragic that he was both the proponent and the destroyer of neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Is there other memories stand out from the robotics and the AI work at MIT?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, but you've got to be more specific.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, I mean, it's such a magical place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: To me, it's a little bit also heartbreaking that with Google and Facebook, like DeepMind and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: so much of the talent doesn't stay necessarily for prolonged periods of time in these universities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh, yeah. Some of the companies are more guilty than others of paying fabulous salaries to some of the highest producers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And then just you never hear from them again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They're not allowed to give public talks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They're sort of locked away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And it's sort of like collecting Hollywood stars or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And they're not allowed to make movies anymore. I own them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, that's tragic because there's an openness to the university setting where you do research,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: both in the space of ideas and space like publication, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, and there's the publication and all that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And often, although these places say they publish, there's pressure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I think, for instance, NetNet, I think Google buying those eight or nine robotics company was bad for the field

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: because it locked those people away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They didn't have to make the company succeed anymore, locked them away for years and then sort of all fretted away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So do you have hope for MIT?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: For MIT?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, why shouldn't I?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, I could be harsh and say that I'm not sure I would say MIT is leading the world in AI or even Stanford or Berkeley.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I would say DeepMind, Google AI, Facebook AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I would take a slightly different approach, a different answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'll come back to Facebook in a minute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I think there's other places following a dream of one of the founders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I'm not sure that it's well founded, the dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I'm not sure that it's going to have the impact that he believes it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You talk about Facebook and Google and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm talking about Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But the thing is those research labs aren't, there's the big dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I'm usually a fan of no matter what the dream is, a big dream is a unifier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Because what happens is you have a lot of bright minds working together on a dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What results is a lot of adjacent ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So much progress is made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I'm not saying they're actually leading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm not saying that the universities are leading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I don't think those companies are leading in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We saw this incredible spike in attendees at NeurIPS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: As I said in my January 1st review this year for 2020, 2020 will not be remembered as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: watershed year for machine learning or AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There was nothing surprising happened anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Unlike when deep learning hit ImageNet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That was a shake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And there's a lot more people writing papers, but the papers are fundamentally boring and

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: uninteresting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Incremental work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Is there particular memories you have with Minsky or somebody else at MIT that stand

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Funny stories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, unfortunately, he's another one that's passed away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You've known some of the biggest minds in AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And they did amazing things and sometimes they were grumpy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, he was interesting because he was very grumpy, but I remember him saying in an interview

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that the key to success or to keep being productive is to hate everything you've ever done in

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Maybe that explains the Perceptron book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There it was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He told you exactly what.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But meaning like just like, I mean, maybe that's the way to not treat yourself too seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Just always be moving forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That was his idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, that crankiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, there's a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, so let me tell you what really the joy memories are about having access to technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: before anyone else has seen it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So I got to Stanford in 1977 and we had terminals that could show live video on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Digital sound system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We had Xerox graphics printer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We could print...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217
