body.input: It wasn't like a typewriter ball hitting characters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It could print arbitrary things only in one bit, black or white, arbitrary pictures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: This was science fiction sort of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: At MIT, the list machines, which they were the first personal computers and they were

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: cost $100,000 each and I got there early enough in the day, I got one for the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Couldn't stand up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Had to keep working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So having that like direct glimpse into the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I've had email every day since 1977.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The host field was only eight bits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I thought that many places, but I could send email to other people at a few places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So that was pretty exciting to be in that world so different from what the rest of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: world knew.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Let me ask you, I'll probably edit this out, but just in case you have a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm hanging out with Don Knuth for a while tomorrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Did you ever get a chance to such a different world than yours?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He's very kind of theoretical computer science, the puzzle of computer science and mathematics

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and you're so much about the magic of robotics, like the practice of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You mentioned him earlier for like not about computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Did your worlds cross?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: They did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I know him now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We talked, but let me tell you my Donald Knuth story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So besides analysis of algorithms, he's well known for writing tech, which is in LaTeX,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: which is the academic publishing system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So he did that at the AI lab and he would work overnight at the AI lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: One night, the mainframe computer went down and a guy named Robert Paul was there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: He only did his PhD at the media lab at MIT and he was an engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And so he and I tracked down what the problem was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was one of this big refrigerator size or washing machine size disk drives had failed

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: and that's what brought the whole system down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So we've got panels pulled off and we're pulling circuit cards out and Donald Knuth, who's

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: a really tall guy, walks in and he's looking down and says, when will it be fixed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Because he wanted to get back to writing his tech system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We figured out it was a particular chip, 7400 series chip, which was socketed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We popped it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: We put a replacement in, put it back in, smoke comes out because we put it in backwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Because we were so nervous that Donald Knuth was standing over us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Anyway, we eventually got it fixed and got the mainframe running again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So that was your little, when was that again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, that must have been before October 79 because we moved out of that building then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So probably 78, sometime early 79.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, all those figures are just fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: All the people who have passed through MIT is really fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Let me ask you to put on your big wise man hat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Is there advice that you can give to young people today, whether in high school or college

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: who are thinking about their career or thinking about life, how to live a life they're proud

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: of, a successful life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So many people ask me for advice and have asked for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I talk to a lot of people all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And there is no one way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: There's a lot of pressure to produce papers that will be acceptable and be published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Maybe I come from an age where I could be a rebel against that and still succeed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Maybe it's harder today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I think it's important not to get too caught up with what everyone else is doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And well, it depends on what you want of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: If you want to have real impact, you have to be ready to fail a lot of times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So you have to make a lot of unsafe decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And the only way to make that work is to keep doing it for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And then one of them will be work out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And so that will make something successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's the whole point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Or you just may end up not having a lousy career.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's certainly possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Taking the risk is the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But there's no way to make all safe decisions and actually really contribute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you think about your death, about your mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I got to say when COVID hit, I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Because in the early days, we didn't know how bad it was going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That made me work on my book harder for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But then I'd started this company and now I'm doing more than full-time at the company,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: so the book's on hold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But I do want to finish this book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: When you think about it, are you afraid of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm afraid of dribbling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I'm losing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The details of, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But the fact that the ride ends?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I've known that for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, but there's knowing and knowing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's such a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, and it really sucks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It feels a lot closer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: So in my blog with my predictions, my pushback against that was I said, I'm going to review

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: these every year for 32 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That puts me into my mid-90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Every time you write the blog posts, you're getting closer and closer to your own prediction

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: of your death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What do you hope your legacy is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: You're one of the greatest roboticists, AI researchers of all time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What I hope is that I actually finish writing this book and that there's one person who

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: reads it and sees something about changing the way they're thinking, and that leads to

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: the next big...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And then there'll be on a podcast 100 years from now saying, I once read that book, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: that changed everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: What do you think is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: This whole thing, the existence, all the hurried things we do on this planet, what do you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: is the meaning of it all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, I think we're all really bad at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Life or finding meaning or both?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's easier to do the stuff that's immediate and not do the stuff that's not immediate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: The big picture we're bad at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Do you have a sense of what that big picture is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Why you ever look up to the stars and ask, why the hell are we here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: My atheism tells me it's just random, but I want to understand the way random...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And that's what I talk about in this book, how order comes from disorder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: But it kind of sprung up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Most of the whole thing is random, but this little pocket of complexity they would call

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Earth, why the hell does that happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And what we don't know is how common those pockets of complexity are or how often, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: they may not last forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Which is more exciting slash sad to you, if we're alone or if there's infinite number

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh, I think it's impossible for me to believe that we're alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That was just too horrible, too cruel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It could be like the sad thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It could be like a graveyard of intelligent civilizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Oh, everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That may be the most likely outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And for us too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And all of this will be forgotten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Including all the robots you build, everything forgotten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, on average, everyone has been forgotten in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Most people are not remembered beyond the generation or two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, yeah, well, not just on average, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Very close to 100% of people who have ever lived are forgotten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I mean, in a long arc of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I don't know anyone alive who remembers my great grandparents because we didn't meet

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Still, this life is pretty fun somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Even the immense absurdity and at times, meaninglessness of it all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It's pretty fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And for me, one of the most fun things is robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And I've looked up to your work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I've looked up to you for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: That's very kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Rod, it's an honor that you would spend your valuable time with me today talking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: It was an amazing conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Thank you so much for being here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Well, thanks for talking with me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I enjoyed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Rodney Brooks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And now, let me leave you with the three laws of robotics from Isaac Asimov.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: One, a robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: to come to harm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Two, a robot must obey the orders given to it by human beings except when such orders

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: would conflict with the first law.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: And three, a robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: with the first or the second laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: Thank you for listening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rodney Brooks: Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #217

body.input: I hope to see you next time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: States, let me say a few words about what this country, my country, the United States of America

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: means to me. First, by way of background, I was born and raised in the Soviet Union, just long

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: enough to get a bit of the Russian soul. An appreciation of Soviet history, music, culture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: of wrestling and mathematics, of engineering and philosophy, stoicism and humor, tragedies and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: triumphs of war and revolutions, all in ways that are uniquely Russian. I do happen to at times

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: mention that I'm Russian. This is what I mean, that I got a bit of that Russian soul. But of

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: course, who I really am is an American. This country gave me the opportunity, the freedom to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: become and to be who I am, to stand as an individual. This seemingly simple freedom to be a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: sovereign human being in the face of all the beauty and cruelty of life is why I love this country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Much of life can be unfair, unjust, even tragic. But this is the country where if I'm clever enough,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: work hard enough, and just get lucky enough, I have a chance to dream big and make my dream a reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: The United States welcomed me, my family and millions of immigrants throughout its history

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: so that we can make something meaningful of ourselves, to love, to dream, to create,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: to find joy and meaning. It lets me be the weird kid I am, who wears a suit, talks about love

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and has a fascination with robots. I know some people these days have an aversion to pride and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: love for their country. I don't. I love America. I also love humanity. I believe these two, patriotism

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and humanism, are not in conflict. Much like loving your family and loving your country are

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: not in conflict. They are all manifestations of the human spirit, longing to strive for a better

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: world. I was born a Russian, but I believe I will die an American, a proud American. Hopefully not

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: too soon, but life is short. I already had one hell of a fun journey, so I'm ready to go when it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: time. This is the Lex Friedman Podcast, and here is my conversation with Jaco Willink.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Is it tragic or beautiful to you that some of the closest bonds that have formed

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: between people are through war often? I think it's both tragic and beautiful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and for the obvious reasons. What are the obvious reasons? Why is it so obvious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Well, it's tragic because a lot of people die, and it's beautiful because you form bonds with

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: people that are very difficult to break once you've been through them. What is it about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: the trauma of war that makes bonds difficult to break? Because what you realize when you're in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: war is that the people that are next to you, you rely on them, and they're relying on you to survive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and without them, you will not survive. And when you realize that you need to work together as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: team to live, that forms a very strong bond. And there's nothing like that team outside of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: realm of war? I don't know because there's a lot of things that I haven't experienced in my life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: but I think the pressure and the consequences of war, there could be similar situations in

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: survival scenarios, in various atrocities where people need to work together in order to survive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and I think you could probably get something that was similar. There's a very particular nature to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: the kind of war that World War II was, especially for the Soviet Union, where it didn't just

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: influence the lives of people, it created culture, the music, the poetry, the literature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: It's in the way people think, it's in the way people see the world, it's in the way they talk,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: even still to this day. And of course, I was talking about the directly relationship between

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: two soldiers, but there's something about the depth of human connection that results from the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: almost like reverberations of war. Generations later, you're still close to other humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: There's a coldness towards other humans in Russia, but once you open up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: it's depth, you seek depth of connection versus breadth of career kind of thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: how can I make friends with this so I can move into this direction? What can this person be

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: friends with this so I can move into this direction? What can this person benefit me?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Instead, you seek a depth of human connection and appreciation that brings a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And maybe I'm romanticizing war here, but it feels like that's inextricably connected to World War II

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: for Russians. Does that resonate at all? So if you look at military training,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: what they do is they take people in the military from the civilian world, they bring them into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: military and they put them through boot camp, which is the stereotypical thing that you see on TV.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: You're going to get yelled at, you're going to get screamed at, you're going to get put in the mud

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and you're going to be made to do hard things together. And what does that do with those

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: civilians? Well, it gives them a common background. It gives them a common suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: that they've been through together and they form some sort of connection, some sort of bond. Now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: to make that bond a little bit stronger, after you get done with boot camp, they send you to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: advanced infantry school and you suffer some more together. And when you suffer more together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: now you're in a smaller group too, because now it's infantry, it's not supply people anymore,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: or logisticians, it's strictly people that are going to fight their infantrymen. So they go

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: through a school together and now they get a little bit tighter, get done with that. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: maybe you go to an airborne division. So you go to airborne school and now you all overcome this

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: fear of jumping out of an airplane together and you celebrate surviving that. Then maybe you get

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: done with that. And now you go at an airborne division. Now you're an even tighter group

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: because you've suffered together. What comes next is special forces training or ranger training.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And what they do is they put you in these situations where you're going to suffer

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: together and you're going to build these bonds. Because as I said earlier, you have to rely on

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: each other to survive. And by the way, not everyone does, not everyone makes it through

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: this training. So you sort of have these memories of people that didn't make it. You share that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: connection as well. And you can keep going down this road until you go into combat with a military

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: unit and military units that go through combat have an even tighter bond. And the harder the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: combat that they go through, the tighter the bond is going to be. So I think when you talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: what the Soviet Union went through in World War II, there was a shared suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: to survive. And so the entire nation has that common thread. And that's probably the thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: you sense or feel when you refer back to the bond that resonates all the way back to World War II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: So on your podcast and your writing, you talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: some of the most fascinating things I listened to you talk about in terms of military conflict

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: is tactics and sort of the details of combat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: But allow me to stick on World War II for a second. There's a particular aspect to that war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: I don't know if you can speak to it, where twice the number of civilians died and military personnel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: So the Soviet Union, especially. My grandfather was a machine gunner

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: in Ukraine as the Germans were marching towards Moscow. There's this main, there's this important

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: push in 1941 where they were trying to get before the winter to Moscow. And what Stalin was doing is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: he was basically throwing bodies at, to slow the attack. And what that meant is everybody understood

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: that your job was, you have this heavy machine guns, it's very, it's almost unreasonable to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: able to be mobile in any kind of way with them. So you're thrown at the front and you're just

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: nonstop shooting and 95 plus percent of people are just dead. Other soldiers are just dead. And then

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: you just go back and back and you're trying to protect as many civilians as you can through

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: out this whole process, but you don't. And so you have millions of civilians that die along the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: into this march. Is there something you could say about this complete, perhaps it's naive of me to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: say, but a war that lacks tactics, that lacks strategy and is purely about just,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: no consideration of human life and just throwing bodies and bullets

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: into a mix together where millions die. And that in particular felt much less like conflict

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and much more like torture or suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: It didn't come off as torture only that interestingly enough, as you probably know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: my grandfather, including everybody else, volunteered. They were proud to do this. They

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: were proud to march to their death for country, for love of country. But the question on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: civilian side, when you're in a war, you're not going to be able to do that. You're not going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: be able to do that. And so I think that's the question on the civilian side. When, when more

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: civilians die, the military personnel, what do you make of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: It's awful. It's awful when a soldier dies. It's awful when a civilian dies. It's awful when

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: 10 civilians or 10 soldiers. And it's even more awful when millions and millions of soldiers and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: it's awful when a soldier dies. And you have to say that the Soviet Union was facing an existential

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: threat to their existence against the Nazis. So to not fight would be to die as well. Maybe die a

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: death a few years later, maybe die a different way, but the choice was die now trying or die later

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: I think the choice was pretty clear as far as the tactics go. I mean, there is, this is attrition

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: warfare. That's what that is. We are going to keep, you know, you said throwing bodies at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: problem. That's attrition warfare. And the Soviet Union had a lot of bodies more than the Germans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And when you fight with attrition warfare, whoever has more men and material will eventually win.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: It's an awful, it's an awful way, but that's the, that's, that's what the strategy was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: You often talk about leadership. Let's put the evils of Hitler aside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: The boldness of Hitler in making some of the strategic decisions he did was considered by

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: many military historians quite brilliant early in the war or insane and brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Stalin, on the other hand, I think universally is seen as somebody who is terrible military

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: strategist, especially early in the war. He did not see all the possible trajectories that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: war could take. Is there something you could say about failure of leadership, Stalin, also the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Kingdom before Churchill and also FDR on the United States side, who basically was trying to

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: turn a blind eye to everything that was happening over there with a perspective of who we just want

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: to make. We want to keep America's interest as the primary interest and everything else, let other

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: countries work out their problems. You know, I think one of the things with Hitler was in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: beginning of the war, he listened to his advisors, he listened to his generals and therefore they did

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: pretty well with that. I think as the war went on, he believed that he was smarter than he was and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: made decisions that were bad that cost him dearly. You know, I mean, case in point, as everyone knows

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: going and attacking the Soviet Union while you're still fighting a war on the other front is not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: not a good move. There's an example of, yeah, bad leadership, letting your ego get in the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: believing that you can do things that are beyond your capabilities. But, you know, as you mentioned

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: in the beginning with Blitzkrieg, those were really dynamic and bold moves and they worked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And that, what does that do? That fuels your ego and makes you think that you can win.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Many people consider that war a just war. What do you think makes a just war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: I think you have the Nazis and the Imperial Japanese trying to impose their will on other

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: nations and other peoples. And when that happens, I think on a grand scale, people look at that and

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: believe it's just to step in and do something about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: But is there some gray area here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: There's, there's nothing but gray area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: The United States has been involved in a lot of military conflicts since then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: How do you draw the line to the gray area? What, what war should we engage in and not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: I know you don't get into politics much, but what the decision to go to war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: you have to look at the situation that you're going into and you have to make sure that you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: the will to go to war. And the will to go to war means that you are willing to kill people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And when I say people, I don't just mean enemy because in war, civilians are going to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Women and children are going to die. Every, a lot of people are going to die. And so you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: and you are going to kill them. It doesn't matter what kind of smart munitions you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: Doesn't matter how disciplined your soldiers are. When you go into a war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: civilians are going to die and you have to understand that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jocko Willink: War, Leadership, and Discipline | Lex Fridman Podcast #197

body.input: And the other thing that you have to understand is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: You get a bunch of gas, large enough, it becomes a star.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: I mean, you don't even have to do anything to it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: and it becomes a star.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Why is fusion so difficult to put on the Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Because in outer space, stars are monopoles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: They are poles, single poles, that are spherically symmetric.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: And it's very easy to get spherically symmetric

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: configurations of gas to compress into a star.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: It just happens naturally all by itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: The problem is magnetism is bipolar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: You have a North Pole and a South Pole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: And it's like trying to squeeze a long balloon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Take a long balloon and try to squeeze it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: You squeeze one side, it bulges out the other side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Well, that's the problem with fusion machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: We use magnetism with a North Pole and a South Pole

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: to squeeze gas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: And all sorts of anomalies and horrible configurations

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: can take place because we're not squeezing something

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: uniformly like in a star.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Stars, in some sense, are for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Fusion on the Earth is very difficult.

body.input: But I think it's inevitable, and it'll eventually

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: give us unlimited power from seawater.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: So seawater will be the ultimate source of energy

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: for the planet Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: Why?

body.input: What's the intuition there?

body.input: Because we'll extract hydrogen from seawater,

body.input: to give us unlimited energy without the meltdown,

body.input: without the nuclear waste.

body.input: Why do we have meltdowns?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: We have meltdowns because in the fusion reactors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

metadata.title: Podcast: Michio Kaku: Future of Humans, Aliens, Space Travel & Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #45

body.input: And now, here's my conversation with Scott Aronson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I sometimes get criticism from a listener here and there

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: that while having a conversation

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: with a world-class mathematician, physicist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: neurobiologist, aerospace engineer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: or a theoretical computer scientist like yourself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I waste time by asking philosophical questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: about free will, consciousness, mortality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: love, nature of truth, super intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: whether time travel is possible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: whether space-time is emergent or fundamental,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: even the crazier questions like whether aliens exist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: what their language might look like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: what their math might look like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: whether math is invented or discovered,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and of course, whether we live in a simulation or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: So I try-

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Out with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Out with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I try to dance back and forth from the deep technical

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to the philosophical, so I've done that quite a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: So you're a world-class computer scientist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and yet you've written about this very point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: the philosophy is important for experts

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: in any technical discipline,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: though they somehow seem to avoid this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: So I thought it'd be really interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to talk to you about this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Why should we computer scientists, mathematicians,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: physicists care about philosophy, do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Well, I would reframe the question a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I mean, philosophy almost by definition

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: is the subject that's concerned with the biggest questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: that you could possibly ask, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: So, the ones you mentioned, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Are we living in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Are we alone in the universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: How should we even think about such questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Is the future determined?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And what do we even mean by it being determined?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Why are we alive at the time we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and not at some other time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: When you sort of contemplate the enormity

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: of those questions, I think you could ask,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: well then why be concerned with anything else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Why not spend your whole life on those questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I think in some sense, that is the right way

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to phrase the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And actually, what we learned throughout history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: but really starting with the scientific revolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: with Galileo and so on, is that there is a good reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to focus on narrower questions, more technical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: mathematical or empirical questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And that is that you can actually make progress on them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and you can actually often answer them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And sometimes they actually tell you something

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: about the philosophical questions that sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: maybe motivated your curiosity as a child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: They don't necessarily resolve the philosophical questions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: but sometimes they reframe your whole understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: of them, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And so for me, philosophy is just the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: that you have in the background from the very beginning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: that you want to, these are sort of the reasons

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: why you went into intellectual life in the first place,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: at least the reasons why I did, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: But math and science are tools that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: for actually making progress, and hopefully,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: even changing our understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: of these philosophical questions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: sometimes even more than philosophy itself does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Why do you think computer scientists avoid these questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: We'll run away from them a little bit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: at least in technical scientific discourse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Well, I'm not sure if they do so

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: more than any other scientists do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I mean, Alan Turing was famously interested,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and his most famous, one of his two most famous papers

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: was in a philosophy journal, Mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: It was the one where he proposed the Turing test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: He took a Wittgenstein's course at Cambridge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: argued with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I just recently learned that little bit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: and it's actually fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I was trying to look for resources in trying to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: where the sources of disagreement and debates

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: between Wittgenstein and Turing were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: That's interesting that these two minds

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: have somehow met in the arc of history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Yeah, well, the transcript of the course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: which was in 1939, right, is one of the more fascinating

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: documents that I've ever read, because Wittgenstein

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: is trying to say, well, all of these formal systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: are just complete irrelevancies, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: If a formal system is irrelevant, who cares?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: Why does that matter in real life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And Turing is saying, well, look,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: if you use an inconsistent formal system

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to design a bridge, the bridge may collapse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: And so Turing, in some sense, is thinking decades ahead,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: I think, of where Wittgenstein is, to where formal systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: are actually going to be used in computers, right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: to actually do things in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: in the physical world, right?

body.input: And if I were trying to explain it to a theologian,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Quantum Computing | Lex Fridman Podcast #72

body.input: maybe I would say, you know, we are studying,
