metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the bar, the bar needs to remain high, but focusing on what matters rather than on the detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So you don't, you know, I've been reading quite a bit about history. You don't worry about

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: human nature and corruption that can seep in. You're saying institutionally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: there's protections against this. I think there is always the fear

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: of corruption, particularly when you speak about public servants, but clearly the risk

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is very different country by country. And speaking about agencies by agencies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think the regulatory agencies have a very good track record and history of the US,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: of Europe, of England, of very, very good track record of integrity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's something I think about. So I grew up in the Soviet Union and I need to perhaps

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: introspect this a little bit, but when I was growing up ethically, there was a sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that bribery is the only way you can get stuff done. That was the system of the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Like you get pulled over by a police officer, like obviously you need to bribe them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It was like the way of life. And then so coming to this country, it was beautiful to see that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the rule of law has so much power. And ultimately the rule of law, when enacted, when it holds up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: it gives people freedom to do the best work of their lives, but there's still human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And that worries me a lot here. And again, it goes back to the perception, the communication,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: when there's people that have worked at Pfizer and an FDA at the CDC, you look at their resume,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: they have those things on their resume, it worries people. Are these great leaders

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that we are supposed to see as authorities, are they playing a game on us?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I would say that I recognize what you said about what happened in, or what I'm sure that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: what you describe in the country that you're coming from, it was how you experienced it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And I know that there are other countries that you need to do these things to do your job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I don't think it's the case in this country, particularly when it comes to those agencies

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that you mentioned. I think they have a very high track record. And also I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that there are a lot of people that they are worried about it or don't think that they are

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: a lot of people that they are worried about it or doubt it. I'm sure like everywhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: there will be a minority, but the vast majority of the Americans, the vast majority of the Europeans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the vast majority of the Brits, the vast majority of the Israelis, they trust what FDA or EMA or CDC

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: or NHRA will say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Still, there's currently a distrust of Big Pharma in the public. Maybe this is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I'd love to hear your comment on. There's distrust of science when it's tangled up with

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: corporations and government institutions like we've talked about. But they have to be entangled

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: to achieve scale, oversight and to achieve the kind of scale that Pfizer has been able to accomplish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: How can Pfizer regain the public trust? How can you regain the public trust, do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Not regain, but sort of take steps to increase the public trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Reputation is something that you can lose in buckets, but you can earn it back in drops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And once you lost it, you are going to take a lot of effort to bring it back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And the pharmaceutical industry lost it. It's clear that the reputation of the industry

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in the last decade was on the lowest that we have seen ever. And there are many reasons for that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but clearly there are reasons that are related also with the behavior of the industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: That needed to change and I'm hopeful that very few will disagree that the industry is a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: different industry right now. That being said, I truly believe that if there is one lesson that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: stands out from the main lessons that we learned during COVID is the power of science in the hands

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: of the private sector. I think it was the private sector that came with solutions with diagnostic

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: tests when we didn't have, solutions with respirators when we didn't have, solutions

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: with treatments, solutions with vaccines. And I think that demonstrated very clearly to the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the value of a thriving private life sciences sector to society. That also affected very positively

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the reputation, both of the sector and of Pfizer. I'm not going to make the mistake to consider

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: given. I'm not to make the mistake that because our reputation is high, that will remain so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: We need to earn it every day. Every day with everything we do, with everything we say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: with the way we behave. And I hope that we'll rise to this occasion and we will do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: You've been at Pfizer for 28 years. Time flies when you're having fun and you've become CEO

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in 2019. It is a company you love, a company you believe in. It's a company that has developed

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: drugs that has helped millions of people. So let me ask you yet another hard question

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: on this topic of reputation. In 2009, Pfizer pleaded guilty to the illegal marketing of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: arthritis drug Bextra and agreed to a $2.3 billion settlement. How do you make sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: of the fact that this happened to a company you love and that you believe in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yes. The Bextra case in 2009 was related to things that happened in 2003.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And the things that happened in 2003 were things that basically several of our reps did off-label

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: promotion. So they spoke with the physicians about off-label use of the product and they shouldn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Can you clarify? So off-label are things that the FDA didn't approve, extra stuff. You basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: say this drug does extra stuff that the FDA never approved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Correct. And this is something that it is allowed when physicians are speaking to physicians,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but it is not allowed for the pharmaceutical companies to refer to these studies because

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: usually there are studies that are happening off-label. And apparently several of our reps

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in 2003, they did it. And we had to settle in 2009 and we paid a very big fine, as you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: The fine was related not to the severity of the conduct, but the size of the revenues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So the fines are – if Bextra was a small product, we would get a small fine. Bextra was a very big

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: product and we got a very large fine. Very bad. What happened in 2003? I don't think that these

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: things happened since then. We have a stellar record from 2009 until now of complying with every

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: single regulation and rule. We have internal processes to make sure that these are not happening

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: by individuals that may have an interest. For example, to get a promotion, they may try to

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: think that they are not the right things. And we have, more importantly, a culture in this company

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that really sets aside people that they think differently. So I didn't like what happened in

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: 2003, but I believe a lot has changed in the 20 years that followed, or almost 20 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So you're developing drugs, you're developing solutions to help millions of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but there's risk involved. And so there will be lawsuits heading back your way

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: because there's a lot of lawyers in the world, partially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: How do you put that into the calculation of how you try to do good in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: That some of the cost is the lawsuits. How do you

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: not fall victim to thinking that it's just the cost of doing business,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: and that some of the lawsuits might actually represent real pain that people are going through?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think that we try always to do the right thing. And that's, as I said, very well embedded into

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: our culture. If you don't do the right thing, sooner or later you will pay for it, one way or another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And right now, for us doing the right thing, it is being able to find innovations to do the right

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: innovations to issues that are real, diseases that they do not have good coverage, good treatments

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: right now. We try to find treatments that significantly surpass the current standards of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: care. And we try not only to comply with what regulators are asking us to do, this is what you

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: need to do to prove the safety or the efficacy, but exceed them. No matter what we do on that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I'm sure that people will find opportunity because, as you said, there are a lot of lawyers

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: to sue us. But we believe in the justice system. And we believe that eventually,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: if you are doing the right thing, you will be on the right side of the history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I'm really glad you say that because focusing on doing the right thing, no matter the money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I believe is the best way to make money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's exactly what I said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's exactly what I said. And also, in another way, in other realms, creating a product that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people love is the best way to make money. So focusing on the core of the thing that makes

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people feel good, that brings value to people's lives. So I'm now in Austin, Texas. My good friend,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Joe Rogan, he's been highlighting to me this aggressive marketing on mainstream media channels

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: by Pfizer. So let me ask a general marketing question. Do you see this as a conflict of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: interest? Is it my bias, the reporting of news, that a lot of people, me included, look to these

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: mainstream channels of news for kind of authority of like, what the heck's going on in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And if Pfizer is sponsoring many of these shows, there's a worry, it may be a perception thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but there's also a natural worry that it would influence what they're talking about because

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: they're afraid of losing the sponsorship. It's subtle, but at scale, it might have a serious

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: impact. Do you worry about this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think people could go one way or another because of multiple reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: From our perspective, I don't think we have aggressive marketing. What we do, we go on TV

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: and we are having ads about our products and they are highly regulated. I think it is the right of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people to know, to learn that if there is a product like that, it's very clearly that we cannot say

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: things that they are off label, that have not been approved. We need to have, every time we go on TV,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: as you know, FDA is forcing us to say also the bad things that can happen for a medicine. Sometimes

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that takes more time than the good things. I don't think that we are doing aggressive marketing. Now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people could be influenced and can be biased in the podcasts or in the other type of media

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: activities that they have for multiple different reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yeah, I know, but it's still, it's pressure, it's human nature. I mean, one of it is perception,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but I worry about too. I have a ton of sponsors for this podcast, for example, and none of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: ever asked me to do anything. They're just, I think likely that kind of pressure is not happening for

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Pfizer, but there's implied pressure sometimes. And I worry about that a lot because, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I look at academia, like I look for the good in people. I tend to believe most people are good or

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: have the capacity to be good and desire to be good. When I came to MIT, I was a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: disappointed, maybe heartbroken. How much pressure, I think unjustified pressure people felt from

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: financial constraints, especially at MIT, when there's, I think a lot of money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people still felt constraints and they weren't, it wasn't bringing out the best in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: They weren't supporting each other. They weren't loving each other, like celebrating each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Successes. I don't want to blame money on everything, money constraints, but when you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: sponsors, it just, I personally worry that doesn't bring the best out of people. And so I feel like I

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: want to put some responsibility on sponsors and great big companies like Pfizer to kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: not get in the way of the best of human nature, whether it's sponsoring podcasts, mainstream media,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: like, I don't know, athletes, whatever. You need to know that we are so, so careful

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: with sponsorships. First of all, we have very few, very, very few. You have a team that for

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: every single one could be $2,000. They will try to sell you a team that's going to be $2,000.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: They will try to see if there is a conflict of interest in the way we do it. And also what is

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the reputation of the persons or the programs that we are sponsoring. So I don't think our friend,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think was from Texas. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yeah. I don't- Joe Rogan, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yes. I don't think he got it right that we do those type of things. We don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Oh, in terms of like having a negative effect on-

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Not even having aggressive sponsorships. We have very few.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yeah. When you clip them all together- And most of the sponsorships that we have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: it is more on patient related organizations. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Rather than, we are very careful not to sponsor other things that can be perceived, not even

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: influenced, but perceived that we may influence. So we are very, very careful on that. This is not

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the case with us. So with the incredibly fast development of the vaccine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: could you tell me the story from the engineering to the science to the human story of how you could

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: do it so fast? By November, you even had the ambition to do it by October. It was in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: initial days. How do you- Eight days later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: In that time, how do you show that the vaccine is safe and effective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Given that I think previous vaccines have taken years to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yeah. The vaccines take years to do that. The time that it takes, it is basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the vast majority of the time to conduct the final phase three study, what is the confirmatory study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: You do that because the phase three study cost a lot of money. In our case, it cost almost a billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So you don't want to go and risk a billion in blinded data normally before you do a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: experiments to make sure that the product that you're putting in the phase three is the right one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: We didn't have that time. So we risk all the money. So we condensed all the time towards this phase

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: three. But the phase three study had to follow all the rules that any study follows when you do this

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: trial. Could you just briefly describe the basics of what is phase three?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Describe the basics of what is phase one, what is phase two, what is phase three?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Let's say that there are so many phases when you try first of all to find what is the right vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: We tried from 20 different vaccines, we nailed down to four. And for those four,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we selected eventually two and then eventually one. Once you have those selections, what is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: dose you're going to use? And then we tried multiple different doses to see which one we

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: think is the best. What does trying entail in those early days?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: You go first of all with smaller doses in humans. And then after you have done a lot of experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in animals so that you can feel that it is safe enough to go to humans and then go with very low

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: dose. And then you gradually increase the dose and then you monitor those humans to make sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that there are not any, let's say, reactogenicity to what you are giving them. At the same time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: you start to measure what is doing in terms of immune responses. So you do that with multiple

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: vaccines and you do that with multiple doses and you do that with multiple ages of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: young people, old people. And eventually from the 20 vaccines to multiple doses to multiple

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: schedules, is it after three weeks the second dose or is it after four weeks or after six months?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: All of that will inform you that I think this is the vaccine, this is the dose, this is the scheme

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that I believe will give me the best results. And when you have that, then you go to do what

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we call the phase three. This is a very big study with thousands of people where you use the vaccine

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that you think is the right one and a placebo. The placebo and the vaccine, they look identical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Nobody knows if he's injected a placebo or a vaccine. The physician that makes the injection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the doctor doesn't know if he's injecting placebo or vaccine. He knows a barcode. Only the computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: knows. In order to go into this computer, there are keys and there are at least two people that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: needs to put their keys so that someone can see the data. And those people, they have legal

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: obligations never to do that. So before a certain point. So all of that is blind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: The idea is that when you go into this study, you need to make sure that you are going with the right

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: one. That's why it takes so much time. But the study is the study. You need to have a significant

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: number of people that will give the two and then you let them live their lives and then you see how

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: many of them will get the disease and then you see if there are differences in percentage

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: of infections for the vaccinated compared to the non-vaccinated. At the same time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: you're monitoring all of them to see if there are differences in the safety profile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: If those that got the placebo have the same, let's say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: heart attacks with those that they didn't. They got the vaccine because heart attacks will happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: if you have 50,000 people because it's part of life. All these processes are very well established

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: and since years. What we did the last one was exactly the same as we did always. We just didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: lose time. We were not careful with money. Instead of recruiting 50,000 people over a year, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we had, let's say, 30 hospitals doing the recruitment, we went with 150 hospitals doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the recruitment. That cost a lot of money. But instead of recruiting them in a year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we recruited them in three, four months. So I did this type of things by taking return on investment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: taking cost out of the equation, and we were able to achieve this result. But it's not the process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: believe me. It is the heart of the people. People don't know what they can and what they cannot do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And if anything, they have a serious tendency to underestimate what they can do. And always,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: when you ask them something that is seemingly impossible, they will think out of the box to

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: be able to deliver. We discussed about the timing. Instead of eight years, we then asked them to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: it in six. We asked them to do it in eight months. Our normal manufacturing, yearly production of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Pfizer was 200 million doses of vaccines every year. That was what we were doing in the last 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: years. We didn't ask them to make 300 million doses for a new vaccine. We asked them to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: 3 billion doses for a new vaccine. The discovery phase of a new molecule, like the treatment that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we have now, the pill against COVID, takes four years. We didn't ask them to do it in three. We

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: asked them to do it in four months, which is what they did. When you are setting this type of goals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: they know immediately. They cannot just think within the box. And immediately, this is where

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the human ingenuity in the heart comes. And this is how they surprised all of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So there's incredible science and engineering going on here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: This is what's bothering me that the conversation in public is often not about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's about politics, unfortunately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Politics. So I spent the day with Elon Musk yesterday. He works with rockets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Similar situation as with Pfizer in the sense that there's NASA and then there's this private

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: company. And that's a source of incredible inspiration to people. No politics, very little

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: politics. So this is part of the thing I'm trying to, I'm hoping to do our little part in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: conversation to help untangle a little bit, just reveal the beauty and the power of the thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: was done here, especially with the vaccine, but other things that are being done with the antiviral

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: drug. Let me just kind of linger on the safety. What can you say? There's a lot of people that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: are concerned that the Pfizer vaccine, by the way, of which I took two shots, no booster yet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is unsafe. What do you say to people that say that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: They should not fear something like that. It's completely wrong. There is no medical product

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in the history of humanity that have been tested as much as this vaccine has been administered to

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: hundreds of millions of people. And because of the importance of COVID, they have been scrutinized

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: those people constantly. Right now, healthcare authorities are looking for every single signal

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: around the world of people that they got the vaccine and try to see if it is vaccine related

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: or not. There are electronic medical records that will tell us when and what happened to a person

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: when he did got the vaccine. And we know now, we have so high certainty that it is so safe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: exactly as the data sheet says about this vaccine, more than any other product. They should not be

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: afraid of something like that. And they should not listen to information, but it is misinformation

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that it is spread on purpose. Well, I don't like the word misinformation because,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: you know, again, back to the Soviet Union, anyone who opposes the state is spreading misinformation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So you can basically call anything misinformation. That's the unfortunate times we live in. You can

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: call anyone, you can basically call anybody a liar and say, I'm the sole possessor of the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And just no offense to me, just because you wear a tie doesn't mean you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: any more likely to be in the possession of the truth than anyone else. So-

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I wouldn't disagree with that at all. I don't think that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: As somebody who's not wearing a tie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And as you can, people can see that I'm not wearing a tie in Europe. But it's not about

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: being able, those that they have the power to impose on the others, the stigma that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: what you're saying is misinformation. But there are a few things that the society

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: we have accomplished and science is one of them. And analytics of data is another one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And to say that something which is highly scientific by people that they're not scientists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think that it is not what you're describing what used to happen in the Soviet Union or in any other

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: autocratic regime in the world right now. But I definitely do think that the scientists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: the public science communicators I've listened to over COVID have really disappointed me

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: because they have not spoken with empathy. They haven't sufficiently, in my view,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: have put their ego aside and really listened to people. Yes, people that don't have a PhD,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: people who have not really, maybe you've not even taken a biology course in college or something

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: like that. But still, they have children, they worry, they fear, they don't know who to trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: They don't know if they should listen to the CEO of Pfizer who might have other incentives in mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: who might just care about money and nothing else. And so they just use common sense and they ask

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: questions. And I think to them, talking down to them as if they're not intelligent and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is something scientists have done, almost like rolled their eyes. And that disappoints me because

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I think that's kind of what is the source of division. Look, humility is a virtue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Yes. And the fact that you're educated doesn't mean that you are having either humility or empathy

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: or you have good human qualities. This was never and will never be a metric of judging

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: this type of virtues. Those that they do this, they're wrong. And actually, they are not doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: good service to the public health because they are undermining. People are not stupid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: They see if you're not respecting them and if you're not respecting their need to learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: because that affects their health, the health of the mother, of the kids. So I fully agree with you

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that we should be very patient to explain again and again and again what is happening. And the

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: vast majority of the people that they don't get vaccinations right now is because they're afraid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's not for any other reason. It's not that they have an agenda. What I'm saying is there is a small

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: number of people that they have made business for them to profit from this anxiety. I'll give you

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: an example. I have been arrested by FBI. This is what someone wrote. I read it. I laughed. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: okay, this is where they take it. There was a reason why they wrote it that. The

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Pfizer CEO was arrested by FBI because they want to create doubts in the minds of the people that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: they're afraid and say, look, if the FBI arrested him, likely I will not do the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: But I laughed. A week later, the wife of the Pfizer CEO died. There is a picture in this website of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: my wife. Someone sends to me, now I'm pissed. I'm not laughing. I try to find my kids to tell them

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: if you read something, mom is fine. Don't worry. Then I remember that she has very old parents

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: back in Greece. We start calling them to making sure because we know that that will be picked up

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: by Greek newspapers and they will publish it. Those people that wrote these things, they know

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: very well that my wife didn't die and died because she was vaccinated. So this is the narratives

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that they are on purpose forming to profit from the stress and the anxiety of good people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And that's something I have to kind of, people that listen to this, that kind of doubt institutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I do also want to say that there's quite a few folks who realize they can make money

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: from saying the man is lying to you. The government is lying to you. It's all corrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: It's all a scam. Big pharma is lying to you. They're manipulating you. I'm surprised at how

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: much money can be made with that. And it's sad. So you have to, just as people use their common

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: sense to be skeptical when listening to politicians and powerful figures, they should be skeptical

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: to also when listening to sort of the conspiracy theorists or not even the conspiracy theorists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but people who raise questions about institutions. Think on your own, think critically with an open

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: mind that everyone can be manipulating you, but also everybody has the capacity to do good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And I think science in its pure form, not when entangled with institutions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is a beautiful thing. And in the hands of many companies, it is a beautiful thing at scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: Still, you have a lot of incentive as having created the vaccine at Pfizer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: this incredible technology to sing it praises.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So there's a kind of, you know, people are skeptical, like how much do we trust?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: How excited Albert is about this vaccine? So for example, I mean, not to do a Shakespearean

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: analysis of your Twitter, but I think you tweeted something about a study with 100% efficacy of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: vaccine or in stopping a transmission or something like that. But I think you tweeted something about

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: it. Do you regret sort of being like over-representing the effectiveness of the vaccine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: technically saying correct things, but just kind of like highlighting the super positive things

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that may be misinterpreted, you know, saying a hundred percent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: No, I never said something 100% that every time I speak, if a number is 100%, I rush to say that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: in biology there is nothing 100% because always there will be when you go to the millions, okay?

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: There were in the study things that were 100%, for example, deaths or in South Africa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: When we tried, there was 100% efficacy. Clearly, it's more numbers. When the numbers will become

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: much bigger, the 100% will not hold, but will be 95, 96. So still, the direction of this is the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: So I'm very, very careful what I tweet. And in addition to how careful I am, I have people

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: that they are looking at and they are having second or third opinions to make sure that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: don't put. Why? Because I know that people are listening to me right now, everything I say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And I want to make sure that they continue not only being clear as to what I want to say so

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: there are no misunderstandings, but also I maintain the trust of the people. I don't think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: someone who only cherry picks information and only emphasizes positive things, it's someone that it

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is the one to be trusted. And I want me and Pfizer to be trusted. So many felt the vaccine was

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: presented as a cure that wouldn't require regular booster shots. Was that something you believed

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: early on? Did you always believe that many regular shots would be required? And maybe in a bigger

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: picture, how many, do you think this will, for the Pfizer vaccine, is it something you see that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: taking a booster shot regularly, like annually? Yes. In the beginning, when we had the first

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: months of the vaccine, people would ask me, do we need another one? And I said, we don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: I was very clear about it. Then around April, May, I start seeing the first data and I made

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: statements that I think we will need a booster around eight to 12 months after the second dose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: And then after that, annually vaccinations, this is what I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: believe is one of the most likely scenarios. And it was based on the data that I had,

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: but then Delta came. And because I always making the caveat that with

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: absent a new variant, with everything we know. With Delta, it was proven that we need the booster

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: to move to the six months. And this is what happened. And I still said, I think the booster

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: is a six months and then I think it will be an annual revaccination, likely. We have to monitor

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: to see the data, but this is the likely scenario. Now we have Omicron. And Omicron says that two

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: doses might be challenging. We don't know exactly yet, but three doses work. So clearly a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Albert Bourla: Pfizer CEO | Lex Fridman Podcast #249

body.input: countries already started moving now the third dose, not from six months to three. So that they

body.input: The following is a conversation with Yeonmi Park, a North Korean defector, human rights activist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and author of the book, In Order to Live. Quick mention of our sponsors, Balcampo,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Gala Games, BetterHelp, and 8 Sleep. Check them out in the description to support this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Let me say a few words about North Korea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: From 1994 to 1998, North Korea went through a famine, mass starvation, caused primarily

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: by King Jong-il, who at the time was the new leader of North Korea after his father's death

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: in 1994. Somewhere between 600,000 and 3 million people died due to starvation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: From all the stories of famine in history, including my own family history, I've come to

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: understand that hunger tortures the human mind in a way that can break everything we stand for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: In North Korea, during the 90s famine, many were driven to cannibalism. Imagine more than

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: 10 million people suffering starvation for months and years, always on the brink of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: We don't know the exact numbers of people who died because the suffering was done in silence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: in darkness. Very little information in or out. Most people had to survive without electricity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: without clean water, medical supplies, sanitation, and food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: The North Korean propaganda machine called this the arduous march or the march of suffering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and words such as famine and hunger were banned because they implied government failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: And once again, now in 2021, Kim Jong-un, the current leader of North Korea, is calling for

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: his country to prepare for another arduous march or march of suffering. Another period of mass

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: starvation as the country closes its borders. Looking at atrocities of the past decades and

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: the encroaching atrocity there now, I think about the quiet suffering of millions of North Koreans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I think about the torture of the human spirit. I think about a North Korean child who could be a

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: scientist, an artist, a writer, but who instead grows impossibly thin without food, their bodies

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: slowly rotting away as their parents watch helplessly. I got emotional in this conversation

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: with you and me, in part because I remembered my grandmother who survived Haldimor, the famine in

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Ukraine, intentionally created by Stalin, where four to 10 million people died and many, many more

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: suffered. Imagine knowing that if you don't engage in cannibalism, you will die before your children

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: did, and then they will be eaten. Imagine, because of this, deciding to murder and eat your own

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: children, as many people did. Imagine the kind of desperation, torture that leads up to a decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: like that. I'm not smart enough to know what evil is, nowhere to draw the line between good and evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: But Stalin, King Jung Il, Kim Jong Un are men who in the name of power are willing to make millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: of people, of children, suffer and die from starvation. I rarely have hate in my heart,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: but I hate these men. I hate that such men exist in this world. I hate that the beauty I love

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: about this life exists amidst such unimaginable cruelty. I have been haunted by this conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: by memories of my grandmother's pain, but I've also been warmed by memories of her love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Love gives me hope, hope for the perseverance of the human spirit, even in the face of evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Can you tell your story from North Korea to today as you describe in your 2015 book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and with the extra perspective on life, love, and freedom you've gained since then?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Wow, that's a long story. I was born in the northern part of North Korea initially,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and my father was a party member, and my mom was housewife. I had one older sister,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and I remember born in that country. I never thought I was in an unusual country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Now I'm thinking about it, it's like literally called the Hermit Kingdom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: but I thought I believed that I was living in the best country on earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: It was a socialist paradise, and everybody in the rest of the world worshiped my dear leader,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and there was nothing to envy for me. So I had this enormous pride in my heart,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: and grateful to be in that country. So was love for the leader not fear?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: For me at least, it was love. Yeah, it was admiration and gratitude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: It changed lately, but for me it was pure, pure like love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Was there any, like looking back with the perspective you have now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: would you describe some of those moments growing up as full of happiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: in this 21st century has no internet, and they don't even know the existence of internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: keep telling me that they were our source of meaning and happiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: laughing with my family and my friends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I'm going to accept that fully. So what? Instead of me keep asking the impossible question, why I'm here, I'm going to let you do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Let the science do that, right? You guys go out in the space and look for the evidence. I'm content.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: You accept that you're here and you're just going to enjoy it. You're here for love, as you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I think I'm here for the process of pursuing something bigger than me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: The process of doing something. It's not like a model. It's not a virtual signaling thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: It just makes me happy that I fight for something bigger. Like that me, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: How boring is it? Every day you get up like, oh my God, I'm going to buy myself this. I'm going to get this for myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: It's so boring, isn't it? So in a way, I think that's what it is. I'm grateful that I'm in a state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I don't have to fight for myself anymore. But more new people have to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: And that's sometimes more than enough they have to do. And I salute them. They are doing fighting, saving themselves every day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: But now I'm not there. I'm very blessed. That's why I'm very grateful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: So fighting for something much bigger than you. But do you still believe that you can change the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: That you can be a thing that at least in part helps North Korea or even broader helps alleviate some suffering in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: So that's the thing. I was reading this book, Fooled by Randomness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: They were like, oh my God, you're so courageous. You're amazing. I was like, no, I'm not. I'm horrible. I know myself. You don't want to tell me that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: It's random why I ended up here. Why did I pick up English so quickly? Why do I love books? I don't know why. It's random.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Don't ask why. Just enjoy it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I think I don't know how the history will remember me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I think the only thing I have to at this point to make sure is that the people after consulting a lot of security teams, like now North Korea became a lot smarter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Like you said, they make it more disguised as a suicide and I call it accident. So when I die, they don't even know I got killed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I think that's a higher chance. So I think that's a thing like people are suffering. Take it or not. It's your choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: And at least it's my responsibility for them to know what's going on. I think if you do not know and didn't do anything, you're not even guilty of a thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: But once you know, then you are not doing it. Then you something's like not right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: So that's what I'm doing. I want people to know. And then what they want to do is not my problem afterwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: So my role is very small in that regard. And I just hope that we're humanized North Koreans for the first time because we have been so dehumanized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Like we are like looking like robots. If you look at us marching and cry like when D.O. later dies, it almost seems like we don't even have the same emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: People cannot connect us in the same level. And I think that's something media have done to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: And you're you're shining a small light on this dark part of the world that I think you make it. You're so modest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: But I think I think you will have that little light just might be a big thing that changes that incredible amount of suffering that's happening on that part of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: You're you're an amazing person. I'm so fortunate to get a chance to talk with you. I can't wait. We do in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I hope you write many more books. I do hope you continue making videos, continue having conversations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: You're an inspiration to me and millions of others. I really appreciate you talk with me today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: I'm so honored. Thank you. Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Thank you for listening to this conversation with you on me, Park. And thank you to Balcampo Gala Games, Better Help and Eight Sleep.

body.input: Check them out in the description to support this podcast. And now let me leave you some words from Bob Marley.

body.input: Better to die fighting for freedom and be a prisoner all the days of your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yeonmi Park: North Korea | Lex Fridman Podcast #196

body.input: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: But I think it's also bad from an innovation perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: because, like, I have infinite amounts of faith

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: give folks powerful tools,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: they will go do interesting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: And it's more than just a few tens of thousands of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: with the interesting tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: It should be millions of people with the tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: So it's sort of like, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: for human labor that we've built like a machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: when these things are getting deployed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: And like, they built factories around them and businesses,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: and the experts who knew how to build and maintain them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: like they're like little engines, you know, sort of everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: They're just a component in how we build the modern world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: like AI needs to get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: Yeah, so that's a really powerful way to think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30

body.input: If we think of AI as a platform versus a tool

metadata.title: Podcast: Kevin Scott: Microsoft CTO | Lex Fridman Podcast #30
