metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: very strong promises. And I first saw the definition in much earlier days, and my first

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: reaction was like, well, my worry about this definition would be that it's a great definition

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of privacy, but that it'll be so restrictive that we won't really be able to use it. We

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: won't be able to compute many things in a differentially private way. So, that's one of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the great successes of the field, I think, is in showing that the opposite is true and that most

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: things that we know how to compute, absent any privacy considerations, can be computed in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: differentially private way. So, for example, pretty much all of statistics and machine learning can

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: be done differentially privately. So, pick your favorite machine learning algorithm, back

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: propagation and neural networks, cart for decision trees, support vector machines, boosting, you name

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: it, as well as classic hypothesis testing and the like in statistics. None of those algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: are differentially private in their original form. All of them have modifications that add

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: noise to the computation in different places in different ways that achieve differential privacy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: So, this really means that to the extent that we've become a scientific community very dependent

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: on the use of machine learning and statistical modeling and data analysis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: we really do have a path to provide privacy guarantees to those methods. And so, we can still

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: enjoy the benefits of the data science era while providing rather robust privacy guarantees to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: individuals. So, perhaps a slightly crazy question, but if we take the ideas of differential privacy

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and take it to the nature of truth that's being explored currently, so what's your most favorite

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and least favorite food? I'm not a real foodie, so I'm a big fan of spaghetti. Spaghetti? Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: What do you really don't like? I really don't like cauliflower.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Wow, I love cauliflower. Okay. But is one way to protect your preference for spaghetti by having

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: an information campaign, bloggers and so on of bots saying that you like cauliflower? So, like this

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: kind of the same kind of noise ideas. I mean, if you think of in our politics today, there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: this idea of Russia hacking our elections. What's meant there, I believe, is bots

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: spreading different kinds of information. Is that a kind of privacy or is that too much of a stretch?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: No, it's not a stretch. I've not seen those ideas. That is not a technique that to my knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: will provide differential privacy. But to give an example, one very specific example about what

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you're discussing is there was a very interesting project at NYU, I think led by Helen Nissenbaum

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: there, in which they basically built a browser plugin that tried to essentially obfuscate your

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Google searches. So, to the extent that you're worried that Google is using your searches to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: build predictive models about you, to decide what ads to show you, which they might very reasonably

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: want to do. But if you object to that, they built this widget you could plug in. And basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: whenever you put in a query into Google, it would send that query to Google. But in the background,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: all of the time from your browser, it would just be sending this torrent of irrelevant queries

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to the search engine. So, it's like a weed and chaff thing. So, out of every thousand queries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: let's say that Google was receiving from your browser, one of them was one that you put in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but the other 999 were not. So, it's the same kind of idea, kind of privacy by obfuscation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: So, I think that's an interesting idea. It doesn't give you differential privacy. It's also,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I was actually talking to somebody at one of the large tech companies recently about the fact that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you know, just this kind of thing that there are some times when the response to my data

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: needs to be very specific to my data, right? Like I type mountain biking into Google, I want results

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: on mountain biking and I really want Google to know that I typed in mountain biking. I don't want

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: noise added to that. And so, I think there's sort of maybe even a little bit of a difference

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: between the two. I think there's sort of maybe even interesting technical questions around notions

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of privacy that are appropriate where, you know, it's not that my data is part of some aggregate

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: like medical records and that we're trying to discover important correlations and facts about

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the world at large, but rather, you know, there's a service that I really want to, you know, pay

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: attention to my specific data, yet I still want some kind of privacy guarantee. And I think these

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: kind of obfuscation ideas are sort of one way of getting at that, but maybe there are others as

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: well. So where do you think we'll land in this algorithm driven society in terms of privacy? So,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: sort of China, like Kai-Fu Lee describes, you know, it's collecting a lot of data on its citizens,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but in the best form, it's actually able to provide a lot of sort of protect human rights

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and provide a lot of amazing services and it's worst forms that can violate those human rights and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and limit services. So where do you think we'll land? So algorithms are powerful when they use

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: data. So as a society, do you think we'll give over more data? Is it possible to protect the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: privacy of that data? So I'm optimistic about the possibility of, you know, balancing the desire for

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: individual privacy and individual control of privacy with kind of societally and commercially

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: beneficial uses of data, not unrelated to differential privacy or suggestions that say like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: well, individuals should have control of their data. They should be able to limit the uses of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that data. They should even, you know, there's, you know, fledgling discussions going on in

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: research circles about allowing people selective use of their data and being compensated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And then you get to sort of very interesting economic questions like pricing, right? And one

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: interesting idea is that maybe differential privacy would also, you know, be a conceptual

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: framework in which you could talk about the relative value of different people's data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: like, you know, to demystify this a little bit. If I'm trying to build a predictive model for some

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: rare disease and I'm trying to use, I'm going to use machine learning to do it, it's easy to get

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: negative examples because the disease is rare, right? But I really want to have lots of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: with the disease in my data set, okay? And so somehow those people's data with respect to this

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: application is much more valuable to me than just like the background population. And so maybe they

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: should be compensated more for it. And so, you know, I think these are kind of very, very fledgling

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: conceptual questions that maybe we'll have kind of technical thought on them sometime in the coming

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: years. But I do think we'll, you know, to kind of get more directly answer your question, I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I'm optimistic at this point from what I've seen that we will land at some, you know, better

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: compromise than we're at right now, where again, you know, privacy guarantees are few, far between

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and weak and users have very, very little control. And I'm optimistic that we'll land in something

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that, you know, provides better privacy overall and more individual control of data and privacy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: But, you know, I think to get there, it's again, just like fairness, it's not going to be enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to propose algorithmic solutions, there's going to have to be a whole kind of regulatory legal

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: process that prods companies and other parties to kind of adopt solutions. And so I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: solutions. And I think you've mentioned the word control a lot. And I think giving people control,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that's something that people don't quite have in a lot of these algorithms. And that's a really

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: interesting idea of giving them control. Some of that is actually literally an interface design

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: question, sort of just enabling because I think it's good for everybody to give users control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: It's not it's not it's almost not a trade off, except that you have to hire people that are good

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: at interface design. Yeah, I mean, the other thing that has to be said, right, is that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: it's a cliche, but you know, we, as the users of many systems, platforms, and apps, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: we are the product, we are not the customer, the customer are advertisers, and our data is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: product. Okay. So it's one thing to kind of suggest more individual control of data and privacy and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: uses. But this, you know, if this happens in sufficient degree, it will upend the entire

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: economic model that has supported the internet to date. And so some other economic model will have

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to be, you know, we'll have to replace it. So the idea of markets, you mentioned, by exposing

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the economic model to the people, they will then become a market, they can be participants in

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: participants. And, you know, this isn't, you know, this is not a weird idea, right? Because

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: there are markets for data already, it's just that consumers are not participants in them. There's

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: like, you know, there's sort of, you know, publishers and content providers on one side that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: have inventory, and then they're advertisers on the others. And, you know, you know, Google and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Facebook are running, you know, they're pretty much their entire revenue stream is by running

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: two sided markets between those parties, right? And so it's not a crazy idea that there would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: like a three sided market or that, you know, that on one side of the market or the other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: we would have proxies representing our interest. It's not, you know, it's not a crazy idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but it would, it's not a crazy technical idea, but it would have pretty extreme

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: economic consequences. Speaking of markets, a lot of fascinating aspects of this world arise

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: not from individual humans, but from the interaction of human beings. You've done a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: lot of work in game theory. First, can you say what is game theory and how does it help us model

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and study? Yeah, game theory, of course, let us give credit where it's due. They don't, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: comes from the economist first and foremost, but as I've mentioned before, like, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: computer scientists never hesitate to wander into other people's turf. And so there is now this

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: 20 year old field called algorithmic game theory, but, you know, game theory, first and foremost,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: is a mathematical framework for reasoning about collective outcomes in systems of interacting

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: individuals. Yeah. You know, so you need at least two people to get started in game theory. And many

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: people are probably familiar with prisoner's dilemma as kind of a classic example of game

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: theory and a classic example where everybody looking out for their own individual interests

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: leads to a collective outcome that's kind of worse for everybody than what might be possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: if they cooperated, for example. But cooperation is not an equilibrium in prisoner's dilemma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And so my work in the field of algorithmic game theory more generally in these areas kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: looks at settings in which the number of actors is potentially extraordinarily large and their

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: incentives might be quite complicated and kind of hard to model directly, but you still want kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: algorithmic ways of kind of predicting what will happen or influencing what will happen in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: design of platforms. So what to you is the most beautiful idea that you've encountered in game

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: theory? There's a lot of them. I'm a big fan of the field. I mean, you know, I mean, technical

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: answers to that, of course, would include Nash's work just establishing that, you know, there's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: competitive equilibrium under very, very general circumstances, which in many ways kind of put the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: field on a firm conceptual footing, because if you don't have equilibrium, it's kind of hard to ever

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: ever reason about what might happen since, you know, there's just no stability. So just the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that stability can emerge when there's multiple... Or that, I mean, not that it will necessarily

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: emerge, just that it's possible, right? It's possible. Like the existence of equilibrium

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: doesn't mean that sort of natural iterative behavior will necessarily lead to it. In the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: real world, yes. Yeah. Maybe answering a slightly less personally than you asked the question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I think within the field of algorithmic game theory, perhaps the single most important kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of technical contribution that's been made is the realization between close connections between

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: machine learning and game theory, and in particular between game theory and the branch of machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: learning that's known as no regret learning. And this sort of provides a very general framework

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: in which a bunch of players interacting in a game or a system, each one kind of doing something

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that's in their self-interest will actually kind of reach an equilibrium and actually reach an

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: equilibrium in a pretty, you know, a rather, you know, short amount of steps. So you kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: mentioned acting greedily can somehow end up pretty good for everybody. Or pretty bad. Or pretty bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: It will end up stable. Yeah, right. And, you know, stability or equilibrium by itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: is not necessarily either a good thing or a bad thing. So what's the connection between machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: learning and the ideas? Well, I mean, I think we kind of talked about these ideas already in kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of a non-technical way, which is maybe the more interesting way of understanding them first,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: which is, you know, we have many systems, platforms, and apps these days that work really

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: hard to use our data and the data of everybody else on the platform to selfishly optimize on

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: behalf of each user. Okay? So, you know, let me give, I think, the cleanest example, which is just

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: driving apps, navigation apps like, you know, Google Maps and Waze, where, you know, miraculously

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: compared to when I was growing up at least, you know, the objective would be the same when you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: wanted to drive from point A to point B, spend the least time driving. Not necessarily minimize

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the distance, but minimize the time, right? And when I was growing up, like the only resources

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you had to do that were like maps in the car, which literally just told you what roads were

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: available. And then you might have like half-hourly traffic reports, just about the major freeways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but not about side roads. So, you were pretty much on your own. And now we've got these apps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: You pull it out and you say, I want to go from point A to point B. And in response kind of to what

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: everybody else is doing, if you like what all the other players in this game are doing right now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: here's the, you know, the route that minimizes your driving time. So, it is really kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: computing a selfish best response for each of us in response to what all of the rest of us are doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: at any given moment. And so, you know, I think it's quite fair to think of these apps as driving or

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: nudging us all towards the competitive or Nash equilibrium of that game. Now you might ask like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: well, that sounds great. Why is that a bad thing? Well, you know, it's known both in theory and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: with some limited studies from actual like traffic data that all of us being in this competitive

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: equilibrium might cause our collective driving time to be higher, maybe significantly higher,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: than it would be under other solutions. And then you have to talk about what those other solutions

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: might be and what the algorithms to implement them are, which we do discuss in the kind of game

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: theory chapter of the book. But similarly, you know, on social media platforms or on Amazon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you know, all these algorithms that are essentially trying to optimize our behalf,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: they're driving us in a colloquial sense towards some kind of competitive equilibrium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And, you know, one of the most important lessons of game theory is that just because we're at

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: equilibrium doesn't mean that there's not a solution in which some or maybe even all of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: might be better off. And then the connection to machine learning, of course, is that in all these

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: platforms I've mentioned, the optimization that they're doing on our behalf is driven by machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: learning, you know, like predicting where the traffic will be, predicting what products I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: going to like, predicting what would make me happy in my newsfeed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Now, in terms of the stability and the promise of that, I have to ask just out of curiosity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: how stable are these mechanisms that you game theory is just, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: game theory is just the economists came up with, and we all know that economists don't live in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: real world. Just kidding. Sort of what's, do you think when we look at the fact that we haven't

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: blown ourselves up from a game theoretic concept of mutually shared destruction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: what are the odds that we destroy ourselves with nuclear weapons as one example of a stable game

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: theoretic system? Just to prime your viewers a little bit, I mean, I think you're referring

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to the fact that game theory was taken quite seriously back in the 60s as a tool for reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: about kind of Soviet US nuclear armament, disarmative, detente, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I'll be honest, as huge of a fan as I am of game theory and its kind of rich history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: it still surprises me that you had people at the RAND Corporation back in those days kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: drawing up two by two tables and one, the row player is the US and the column player is Russia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and that they were taking seriously. I'm sure if I was there, maybe it wouldn't have seemed as

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: naive as it does at the time. It seems to have worked, which is why it seems naive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Well, we're still here. We're still here in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Yeah. Even though I kind of laugh at those efforts, they were more sensible then than

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: they would be now, right? Because there were sort of only two nuclear powers at the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and you didn't have to worry about deterring new entrants and who was developing the capacity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And so we have many... It's definitely a game with more players now and more potential entrants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I'm not in general somebody who advocates using kind of simple mathematical models when the stakes

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: are as high as things like that, and the complexities are very political and social,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but we are still here. So you've worn many hats, one of which,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the one that first caused me to become a big fan of your work many years ago is algorithmic trading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: So I have to just ask a question about this because you have so much fascinating work there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: In the 21st century, what role do you think algorithms have in the space of trading,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: investment in the financial sector? Yeah. It's a good question. I mean, in the time I've spent

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: on Wall Street and in finance, I've seen a clear progression, and I think it's a progression that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: kind of models the use of algorithms and automation more generally in society, which is the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that kind of get taken over by the algos first are sort of the things that computers are obviously

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: better at than people. So first of all, there needed to be this era of automation where just

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: financial exchanges became largely electronic, which then enabled the possibility of trading

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: becoming more algorithmic because once the exchanges are electronic, an algorithm can

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: submit an order through an API just as well as a human can do at a monitor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Can do it really quickly, can read all the data so-

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Yeah. And so I think the places where algorithmic trading have had the greatest inroads and had the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: first inroads were in kind of execution problems, kind of optimized execution problems. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: what I mean by that is at a large brokerage firm, for example, one of the lines of business might be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: on behalf of large institutional clients taking what we might consider difficult trade. So it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: not like a mom and pop investor saying, I want to buy a hundred shares of Microsoft. It's a large

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: hedge fund saying, I want to buy a very, very large stake in Apple and I want to do it over the span

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of a day. And it's such a large volume that if you're not clever about how you break that trade up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: not just over time, but over perhaps multiple different electronic exchanges that all let you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: trade Apple on their platform, you will move, you'll push prices around in a way that hurts

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: your execution. So this is an optimization problem. This is a control problem. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: machines are better. We know how to design algorithms that are better at that kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: thing than a person is going to be able to do because we can take volumes of historical

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and real-time data to kind of optimize the schedule with which we trade. And similarly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: high-frequency trading, which is closely related, but not the same as optimized execution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: where you're just trying to spot very, very temporary mispricings between exchanges or

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: within an asset itself, or just predict directional movement of a stock because of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the kind of very, very low level granular buying and selling data in the exchange.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Machines are good at this kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: It's kind of like the mechanics of trading. What about the... Can machines do long-term

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: sort of prediction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Yeah. So I think we are in an era where clearly there have been some very successful

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: quant hedge funds that are in what we would traditionally call still in the stat arb regime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: What's that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Stat arb, referring to statistical arbitrage. But for the purposes of this conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: what it really means is making directional predictions in asset price movement or returns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Your prediction about that directional movement is good for... You have a view that it's valid for

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: some period of time between a few seconds and a few days. And that's the amount of time that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you're going to kind of get into the position, hold it, and then hopefully be right about the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: directional movement and buy low and sell high as the cliche goes. So that is kind of a sweet spot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I think, for quant trading and investing right now and has been for some time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: When you really get to kind of more Warren Buffett style time scales, like my cartoon

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of Warren Buffett is that Warren Buffett sits and thinks what the long-term value of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Apple really should be. And he doesn't even look at what Apple is doing today. He just decides,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I think that this is what its long-term value is and it's far from that right now. And so I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: going to buy some Apple or short some Apple and I'm going to sit on that for 10 or 20 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: So when you're at that kind of time scale or even more than just a few days,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: all kinds of other sources of risk and information. So now you're talking about holding things through

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: recessions and economic cycles. Wars can break out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: So there you have to understand the human nature at a level that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Yeah, and you need to just be able to ingest many, many more sources of data that are on

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: wildly different time scales. So if I'm an HFT, I'm a high-frequency trader, like I don't...

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Like I don't... I really... My main source of data is just the data from the exchanges themselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: about the activity in the exchanges. And maybe I need to keep an eye on the news,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: because that can cause sudden... The CEO gets caught in a scandal or gets run over by a bus

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: or something that can cause very sudden changes. But I don't need to understand economic cycles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I don't need to understand recessions. I don't need to worry about the political situation

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: or war breaking out in this part of the world, because all I need to know is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: as long as that's not gonna happen in the next 500 milliseconds, then my model's good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: When you get to these longer time scales, you really have to worry about that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And people in the machine learning community are starting to think about this. We jointly sponsored

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: a workshop at Penn with the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia a little more than a year ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: on... I think the title is something like Machine Learning for Macroeconomic Prediction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: macroeconomic referring specifically to these longer time scales. And it was an interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: conference, but it left me with greater confidence that we have a long way to go to... And so I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that people that... In the grand scheme of things, if somebody asked me like, well, whose job on

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Wall Street is safe from the bots? I think people that are at that longer time scale and have that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: appetite for all the risks involved in long-term investing and that really need kind of not just

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: algorithms that can optimize from data, but they need views on stuff. They need views on

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: the political landscape, economic cycles and the like. And I think they're pretty safe for a while

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: as far as I can tell. So Warren Buffett's job is safe for a little while. Yeah, I'm not seeing

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: a robo Warren Buffett anytime soon. Should give him comfort. Last question, if you could go back to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: If there's a day in your life you could relive because it made you truly happy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: happy. Maybe outside family. Yeah, otherwise... What day would it be? Can you look back,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: you remember just being profoundly transformed in some way or blissful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I'll answer a slightly different question, which is like, what's a day in my life or my career that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: was kind of a watershed moment? I went straight from undergrad to doctoral studies and that's not

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: at all atypical. And I'm also from an academic family. My dad was a professor, my uncle on his

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: side is a professor. Both my grandfathers were professors. All kinds of majors too, philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I saw all over the map. Yeah. And I was a grad student here just up the river at Harvard and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: then came to study with Les Valiant, which was a wonderful experience. But I remember my first year

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of graduate school, I was generally pretty unhappy. And I was unhappy because at Berkeley as an

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: undergraduate, yeah, I studied a lot of math and computer science, but it was a huge school,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: first of all. And I took a lot of other courses. As we've discussed, I started as an English major

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: and took history courses and art history classes and had friends that did all kinds of different

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: things. And Harvard's a much smaller institution than Berkeley and its computer science department,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: especially at that time, was a much smaller place than it is now. And I suddenly just felt very

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: like I'd gone from this very big world to this highly specialized world. And now all of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: classes I was taking were computer science classes and I was only in classes with math and computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: science people. And so I thought often in that first year of grad school about whether I really

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: wanted to stick with it or not. And I thought like, oh, I could stop with a master's, I could go back

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to the Bay Area and to California. And this was in one of the early periods where there was...

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Like you could definitely get a relatively good job paying job at one of the tech companies back,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that were the big tech companies back then. And so I distinctly remember a late spring day when

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I was sitting in Boston Common and really just chewing over what I wanted to do with my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: And then I realized, okay, and I think this is where my academic background helped me a great

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: deal. I sort of realized, yeah, you're not having a great time right now. This feels really narrowing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: but you know that you're here for research eventually and to do something original and to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: try to carve out a career where you kind of choose what you want to think about and have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: great deal of independence. And so at that point, I really didn't have any real research experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: yet. I mean, it was trying to think about some problems with very little success, but I knew

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: that I hadn't really tried to do the thing that I knew I'd come to do. And so I thought, I'm gonna

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: stick through it for the summer. And that was very formative because I went from kind of contemplating

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: quitting to a year later, it being very clear to me I was gonna finish because I still had a ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: to go, but I kind of started doing research. It was going well. It was really interesting. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: it was sort of a complete transformation. And it's just that transition that I think every

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: doctoral student makes at some point, which is to sort of go from being like a student

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: of what's been done before to doing your own thing and figure out what makes you interested

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: in what your strengths and weaknesses are as a researcher. And once I kind of made that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: decision on that particular day at that particular moment in Boston Common,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: I'm glad I made that decision. And also just accepting the painful nature of that journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Yeah, exactly. In that moment said, I'm gonna stick it out. Yeah, I'm gonna stick around for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Well, Michael, I've looked off to your work for a long time. It's really nice to talk to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: Thank you so much. It's great to get back in touch with you too and see how great you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Kearns: Algorithmic Fairness, Privacy & Ethics | Lex Fridman Podcast #50

body.input: doing as well. Thanks a lot. Appreciate it.
