body.input: The following is a conversation with Pamela McCordick. She's an author who has written on

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the history and the philosophical significance of artificial intelligence. Her books include

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Machines Who Think in 1979, The Fifth Generation in 1983 with Ed Fagenbaum, who's considered to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the father of expert systems, The Edge of Chaos that features women, and many more books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I came across her work in an unusual way by stumbling in a quote from Machines Who Think

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that is something like, artificial intelligence began with the ancient wish to forge the gods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: That was a beautiful way to draw a connecting line between our societal relationship with AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: from the grounded day-to-day science, math, and engineering to popular stories and science fiction

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and myths of automatons that go back for centuries. Through her literary work, she has spent a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: time with the seminal figures of artificial intelligence, including the founding fathers of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: AI from the 1956 Dartmouth summer workshop where the field was launched. I reached out to Pamela

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: for a conversation in hopes of getting a sense of what those early days were like and how their

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: dreams continued to reverberate through the work of our community today. I often don't know where

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the conversation may take us, but I jump in and see. Having no constraints, rules, or goals is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: wonderful way to discover new ideas. This is the Artificial Intelligence Podcast. If you enjoy it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: subscribe on YouTube, give it five stars on iTunes, support it on Patreon, or simply connect with me

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: on Twitter at Lex Friedman, spelled F-R-I-D-M-A-N. And now here's my conversation with Pamela McCordick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: In 1979, your book Machines Who Think was published. In it, you interviewed some of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the early AI pioneers and explored the idea that AI was born not out of maybe math and computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: science, but out of myth and legend. So tell me if you could the story of how you first arrived at

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the book, the journey of beginning to write it. I had been a novelist. I'd published two novels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And I was sitting under the portal at Stanford one day in the house we were renting for the summer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And I thought, I should write a novel about these weird people in AI I know. And then I thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: ah, don't write a novel, write a history. Simple, just go around, interview them, splice it together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: voila, instant book. Ha, ha, ha. It was much harder than that. But nobody else was doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And so I thought, well, this is a great opportunity. And there were people who, John McCarthy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: for example, thought it was a nutty idea. The field had not evolved yet, so on. And he had some

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: mathematical thing he thought I should write instead. And I said, no, John, I am not a woman

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in search of a project. This is what I want to do. I hope you'll cooperate. And he said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: oh, mutter, mutter, well, OK, it's your time. What was the pitch for the, I mean, such a young

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: field at that point. How do you write a personal history of a field that's so young? I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: this is wonderful. The founders of the field are alive and kicking and able to talk about what

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: they're doing. Did they sound or feel like founders at the time? Did they know that they

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: know that they have founded something? Oh, yeah. They knew what they were doing was very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What I now see in retrospect is that they were at the height of their research careers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And it's humbling to me that they took time out from all the things that they had to do as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: consequence of being there and to talk to this woman who said, I think I'm going to write a book

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: about you. No, it was amazing. Just amazing. So who stands out to you? Maybe looking 63 years ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the Dartmouth Conference. So Marvin Minsky was there. McCarthy was there. Claude Shannon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Alan Newell, Herb Simon, some of the folks you've mentioned. Then there's other characters, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: One of your co-authors. He wasn't at Dartmouth. He wasn't at Dartmouth. No. But I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: he was I think an undergraduate then. And of course, Joe Traub. I mean, all of these are players,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: not at Dartmouth, but in that era. Right. CMU and so on. So who are the characters,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: if you could paint a picture that stand out to you from memory? Those people you've interviewed

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and maybe not people that were just in the atmosphere. Of course, the four founding fathers

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: were extraordinary guys. They really were. Who are the founding fathers? Alan Newell, Herbert Simon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Marvin Minsky, John McCarthy. They were the four who were not only at the Dartmouth Conference,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but Newell and Simon arrived there with a working program called the Logic Theorist. Everybody else

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: had great ideas about how they might do it, but they weren't going to do it yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And you mentioned Joe Traub, my husband. I was immersed in AI before I met Joe

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: because I had been Ed Feigenbaum's assistant at Stanford. And before that, I had worked on a book

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: edited by Feigenbaum and Julian Feldman called Computers and Thought. It was the first textbook

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: of readings of AI. And they only did it because they were trying to teach AI to people at Berkeley.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And you'd have to send them to this journal and that journal. This was not the internet where you

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: could go look at an article. So I was fascinated from the get-go by AI. I was an English major.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What did I know? And yet I was fascinated. And that's why you saw that historical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that literary background, which I think is very much a part of the continuum of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: That AI grew out of that same impulse. That traditional, what drew you to AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: How did you even think of it back then? What was the possibilities, the dreams? What was interesting to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The idea of intelligence outside the human cranium, this was a phenomenal idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And even when I finished Machines Who Think, I didn't know if they were going to succeed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: In fact, the final chapter is very wishy-washy, frankly. I'll succeed the field did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah. So was there the idea that AI began with the wish to forge the gods? So the spiritual

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: component that we crave to create this other thing greater than ourselves?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: For those guys, I don't think so. Newell and Simon were cognitive psychologists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What they wanted was to simulate aspects of human intelligence and they found they could do it on the computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Minsky just thought it was a really cool thing to do. Likewise, McCarthy. McCarthy had got the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in 1949 when he was a Caltech student. And he listened to somebody's lecture. It's in my book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I forget who it was. And he thought, oh, that would be fun to do. How do we do that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And he took a very mathematical approach. Minsky was hybrid and Newell and Simon were very much

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: cognitive psychology. How can we simulate various things about human cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What happened over the many years is, of course, our definition of intelligence expanded tremendously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: These days, biologists are comfortable talking about the intelligence of a cell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the intelligence of the brain, not just human brain, but the intelligence of any kind of brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Cephalopause, an octopus is really intelligent by any... We wouldn't have thought of that

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in the 60s, even the 70s. So all these things have worked in. And I did hear one behavioral

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: primatologist, Franz de Waal, say AI taught us the questions to ask.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah, this is what happens, right? When you try to build it is when you start to actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: ask questions, it puts a mirror to ourselves. Yeah, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So you were there in the middle of it. It seems like not many people were asking the questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that you were, just trying to look at this field the way you were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I was solo. When I went to get funding for this because I needed somebody to transcribe the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: interviews and I needed travel expenses, I went to everything you could think of, the NSA,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: NSF, DARPA. There was an Air Force place that doled out money. And each of them said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: well, that was very interesting. That's a very interesting idea, but we'll think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And the National Science Foundation actually said to me in plain English, hey, you're only a writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: You're not a historian of science. And I said, yeah, that's true. But the historians of science

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: will be crawling all over this field. I'm writing for the general audience, so I thought. And they

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: still wouldn't budge. I finally got a private grant without knowing who it was from, from Ed

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Fredkin at MIT. He was a wealthy man and he liked what he called crackpot ideas. And he considered-

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: This a crackpot idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: This a crackpot idea and he was willing to support it. I am ever grateful. Let me say that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Some would say that a history of science approach to AI or even just a history or anything like the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: book that you've written hasn't been written since. Maybe I'm not familiar, but it's certainly not

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: many. If we think about bigger than just these couple of decades, few decades, what are the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: roots of AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Oh, they go back so far. Yes, of course, there's all the legendary stuff, the Golem and

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the early robots of the 20th century. But they go back much further than that. If you read Homer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Homer has robots in the Iliad. And a classical scholar was pointing out to me just a few months

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: ago, well, you said you just read the Odyssey. The Odyssey is full of robots. It is, I said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah. How do you think Odysseus' ship gets from one place to another? He doesn't have the crew

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: people to do that, the crew men. Yeah, it's magic, it's robots. Oh, I thought. How interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So we've had this notion of AI for a long time. And then toward the end of the 19th century,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the beginning of the 20th century, there were scientists who actually tried to make this happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: some way or another, not successfully. They didn't have the technology for it. And of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Babbage in the 1850s and 60s, he saw that what he was building was capable of intelligent behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And when he ran out of funding, the British government finally said, that's enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: He and Lady Lovelace decided, oh, well, why don't we play the ponies with this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: He had other ideas for raising money too. But if we actually reach back once again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I think people don't actually really know that robots do appear or ideas of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: You talk about the Hellenic and the Hebraic points of view. Oh, yes. Can you tell me about each?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Tell me about each. I defined it this way. The Hellenic point of view is robots are great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: They are party help. They help this guy Hephaestus, this God Hephaestus in his forge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I presume he made them to help him and so on and so forth. And they welcome the whole idea of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The Hebraic view has to do with, I think it's the second commandment, thou shalt not make

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: any graven image. In other words, you better not start imitating humans because that's just

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: forbidden. It's the second commandment. And a lot of the reaction to artificial intelligence has been

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in a sense that this is somehow wicked. This is somehow blasphemous. We shouldn't be going there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Now, you can say, yeah, but there are going to be some downsides. And I say, yes, there are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but blasphemy is not one of them. There is a kind of fear that feels to be almost primal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Is there religious roots to that? Because so much of our society has religious roots. And so there

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is a feeling of, like you said, blasphemy, of creating the other, of creating something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: It doesn't have to be artificial intelligence. It's creating life in general. It's the Frankenstein

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: idea. It was the annotated Frankenstein on my coffee table. It's a tremendous novel. It really

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is just beautifully perceptive. Yes, we do fear this and we have good reason to fear it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: because it can get out of hand. Maybe you can speak to that fear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the psychology, if you've thought about it. There's a practical set of fears, concerns in

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the short term. If we actually think about artificial intelligence systems, you can think

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: about bias of discrimination in algorithms. You can think about their social networks have

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: algorithms that recommend the content you see. Thereby, these algorithms control the behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: of the masses. There's these concerns. But to me, it feels like the fear that people have

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is deeper than that. So have you thought about the psychology of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I think in a superficial way, I have. There is this notion that if we

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: produce a machine that can think, it will outthink us and therefore replace us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I guess that's a primal fear of almost kind of a kind of mortality. So around the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: you said you work with Stanford, with Ed Fagenbaum. So let's look at that one person

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: throughout his history. Clearly a key person, one of the many in the history of AI. How has he

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: changed in general around him? How has Stanford changed in the last, how many years are we talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: about here? Oh, since 65. 65. So maybe it doesn't have to be about him. It could be bigger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but because he was a key person in expert systems, for example, how is that? How are these folks who

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: you've interviewed in the 70s, 79 changed through the decades? In Ed's case, I know him well. We are

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: dear friends. We see each other every month or so. He told me that when Machines Who Think first

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: came out, he really thought all the front matter was kind of baloney. He said, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: all the front matter was kind of baloney. And 10 years later, he said, no, I see what you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: getting at. Yes, this has been a human impulse for thousands of years to create something outside

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the human cranium that has intelligence. I think it's very hard when you're down

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: at the algorithmic level and you're just trying to make something work, which is hard enough,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: just step back and think of the big picture. It reminds me of when I was in Santa Fe, I knew a

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: lot of archeologists, which was a hobby of mine. And I would say, yeah, yeah, well, you can look

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: at the shards and say, oh, this came from this tribe and this came from this trade route and so

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: on. But what about the big picture? And a very distinguished archeologist said to me, they don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: think that way. No, they're trying to match the shard to where it came from. Where did this corn,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: remainder of this corn come from? Was it grown here? Was it grown elsewhere? And I think this

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is part of the AI, any scientific field. You're so busy doing the hard work, and it is hard work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that you don't step back and say, oh, well, now let's talk about the general meaning of all this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah. So none of the, even Minsky and McCarthy, they-

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Oh, those guys did. Yeah, the founding fathers did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Early on or-

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Pretty early on. But in a different way from how I looked at it, the two cognitive psychologists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Newell and Simon, they wanted to imagine reforming cognitive psychology so that we would really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: really understand the brain. Minsky was more speculative, and John McCarthy saw it as,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I think I'm doing him right by this, he really saw it as a great boon for human beings to have this

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: technology, and that was reason enough to do it. And he had wonderful, wonderful fables about how,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: if you do the mathematics, you will see that these things are really good for human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And if you had a technological objection, he had an answer, a technological answer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but here's how we could get over that, and then blah, blah, blah, blah. And one of his favorite

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: things was what he called the literary problem, which of course he presented to me several times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: That is, everything in literature, there are conventions in literature. One of the conventions

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is that you have a villain and a hero, and the hero in most literature is human, and the villain

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in most literature is a machine. And he said, no, that's just not the way it's going to be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but that's the way we're used to it. So when we tell stories about AI, it's always with this

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: paradigm. I thought, yeah, he's right. Looking back, the classics, RUR is certainly the machines

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: trying to overthrow the humans. Frankenstein is different. Frankenstein is a creature. He never

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: has a name. Frankenstein, of course, is the guy who created him, the human, Dr. Frankenstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: This creature wants to be loved, wants to be accepted, and it is only when Frankenstein

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: turns his head, in fact, runs the other way, and the creature is without love

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that he becomes the monster that he later becomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So who's the villain in Frankenstein? It's unclear, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Oh, it is unclear, yeah. It's really the people who drive him. By driving him away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: they bring out the worst. That's right. They give him no human solace, and he is driven away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: You're right. He becomes, at one point, the friend of a blind man, and he serves this blind man,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and they become very friendly. But when the sighted people of the blind man's family come in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: ah, you've got a monster here. So it's very didactic in its way. What I didn't know is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Mary Shelley and Percy Shelley were great readers of the literature surrounding abolition in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: United States, the abolition of slavery, and they picked that up wholesale. You know, you are making

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: monsters of these people because you won't give them the respect and love that they deserve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Do you have, if we get philosophical for a second, do you worry that once we create machines that

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: are a little bit more intelligent, let's look at Roomba, the vacuum cleaner, that this darker

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: part of human nature where we abuse the other, the somebody who's different, will come out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I don't worry about it. I could imagine it happening. But I think that what AI has to offer

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the human race will be so attractive that people will be won over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So you have looked deep into these people, have deep conversations, and it's interesting to get a

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: sense of stories of the way they were thinking and the way it was changed, the way your own

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: thinking about AI has changed. So you mentioned McCarthy. What about the years at CMU, Carnegie

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Mellon with Joe? Sure. Joe was not in AI. He was in algorithmic complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Was there always a line between AI and computer science, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Is AI its own place of outcasts? Was that the feeling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: There was a kind of outcast period for AI. For instance, in 1974,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the new field was hardly 10 years old. The new field of computer science was asked by the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: National Science Foundation, I believe, but it may have been the National Academies, I can't remember,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: to tell your fellow scientists where computer science is and what it means. And they wanted

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: to leave out AI. And they only agreed to put it in because Don Knuth said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: hey, this is important. You can't just leave that out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Really? Don Knuth? Don Knuth, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I talked to him recently too. Out of all the people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yes. But you see, an AI person couldn't have made that argument. He wouldn't have been believed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but Knuth was believed. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So Joe Traub worked on the real stuff. Joe was working on algorithmic complexity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but he would say in plain English again and again, the smartest people I know are in AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Really? Oh, yes. No question. Anyway, Joe loved these guys. What happened was that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I guess it was as I started to write Machines Who Think, Herb Simon and I both wrote it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Herb Simon and I became very close friends. He would walk past our house on Northumberland Street

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: every day after work. And I would just be putting my cover on my typewriter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And I would lean out the door and say, Herb, would you like a sherry?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And Herb almost always would like a sherry. So he'd stop in and we'd talk for an hour,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: two hours. My journal says we talked this afternoon for three hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What was on his mind at the time in terms of on the AI side of things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Oh, we didn't talk too much about AI. We talked about other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Just life. We both love literature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And Herb had read Proust in the original French twice all the way through. I can't, I've read it

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in English in translation. So we talked about literature. We talked about languages. We talked

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: about music because he loved music. We talked about art because he was actually enough of a painter

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that he had to give it up because he was afraid it was interfering with his research

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and so on. So no, it was really just chat chat, but it was very warm. So one summer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I said to Herb, you know, my students have all the really interesting conversations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I was teaching at the University of Pittsburgh then in the English department.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: They get to talk about the meaning of life and that kind of thing. And what do I have? I have

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: university meetings where we talk about the photocopying budget and whether the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: course on romantic poetry should be one semester or two. So Herb laughed. He said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: yes, I know what you mean. He said, but you could do something about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Dot, that was his wife, Dot and I used to have a salon at the University of Chicago every Sunday

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: night. And we would have essentially an open house and people knew it wasn't for a small talk. It was

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: really for some topic of depth. He said, but my advice would be that you choose the topic ahead

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: of time. Fine. I said, so the following, we exchanged mail over the summer. That was US post

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in those days because you didn't have personal email. And I decided I would organize it and there

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: would be eight of us, Alan Null and his wife, Herb Simon and his wife, Dorothea. There was a novelist

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: in town, a man named Mark Harris. He had just arrived and his wife, Josephine. Mark was most

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: famous then for a novel called Bang the Drum Slowly, which was about baseball and Joe and me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: so eight people. And we met monthly and we just sank our teeth into really hard topics. And it

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: was great fun. How have your own views around artificial intelligence changed through the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: process of writing Machines Who Think and afterwards the ripple effects? I was a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: skeptical that this whole thing would work out. It didn't matter to me. It was so audacious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: This whole thing being AI. AI generally, yeah. And in some ways, it hasn't worked out the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I expected so far. That is to say there's this wonderful lot of apps thanks to deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and so on, but those are algorithmic. And in the part of symbolic processing, there is very little

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: yet. And that's a field that lies waiting for industrious graduate students. Maybe you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: tell me some figures that popped up in your life in the 80s with expert systems where there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the symbolic AI possibilities of what most people think of as AI. If you dream of the possibilities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: AI is really expert systems. And those hit a few walls and there were challenges there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And I think, yes, they will reemerge again with some new breakthroughs and so on. But what did

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: that feel like, both the possibility and the winter that followed, the slowdown and research?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Ah, you know, this whole thing about AI winter is to me a crock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: It's no winters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Because I look at the basic research that was being done in the 80s, which is supposed to be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: my God, it was really important. It was laying down things that nobody had thought about before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but it was basic research. You couldn't monetize it, hence the winter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Hence the winter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: You know, research, scientific research goes and fits and starts. It isn't this nice, smooth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: oh, this follows this, follows this. No, it just doesn't work that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The interesting thing, the way winters happen, it's never the fault of the researchers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: It's the some source of hype over promising. Well, no, let me take that back. Sometimes it

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: is the fault of the researchers. Sometimes certain researchers might over promise the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: possibilities. They themselves believe that we're just a few years away, sort of just recently talked

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: to Elon Musk and he believes he'll have an autonomous vehicle. We'll have autonomous

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: vehicles in a year. And he believes it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: A year?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: A year, yeah. We'll have mass deployment of our time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: For the record, this is 2019 right now. So he's talking 2020.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: To do the impossible, you really have to believe it. And I think what's going to happen when you

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: believe it, because there's a lot of really brilliant people around him, is some good stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: will come out of it. Some unexpected, brilliant breakthroughs will come out of it when you really

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: believe it, when you work that hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah, I believe that. And I believe autonomous vehicles will come. I just don't believe it'll

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: be in a year. I wish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: But nevertheless, autonomous vehicles is a good example. There's a feeling many companies have

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: promised by 2021, by 2022, Ford, GM, basically every single automotive company has promised

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: they'll have autonomous vehicles. So that kind of over promise is what leads to the winter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Because we'll come to those dates. There won't be autonomous vehicles. And there'll be a feeling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: well, wait a minute, if we took your word at that time, that means we just spent billions of dollars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: had made no money, and there's a counter response to where everybody gives up on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Sort of intellectually, at every level, the hope just dies. And all that's left is a few basic

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: researchers. So you're uncomfortable with some aspects of this idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Well, it's the difference between science and commerce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So you think science goes on the way it does?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Science can really be killed by not getting proper funding or timely funding. I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Great Britain was a perfect example of that. The Lighthill report in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I don't remember the year, essentially said, there's no use Great Britain putting any money

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: into this. It's going nowhere. And this was all about social factions in Great Britain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Edinburgh hated Cambridge and Cambridge hated Manchester. Somebody else can write that story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: But it really did have a hard effect on research there. Now, they've come roaring back with deep

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: mind, but that's one guy and his visionaries around him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: But just to push on that, it's kind of interesting. You have this dislike of the idea of an AI winter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Where's that coming from? Where were you? Oh, because I just don't think it's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: There was a particular periods of time. It's a romantic notion, certainly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah, well, I admire science, perhaps more than I admire commerce. Commerce is fine. Hey, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: we all got to live. But science has a much longer view than commerce and continues almost regardless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: It can't continue totally regardless, but it's almost regardless of what's saleable and what's

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: not, what's monetizable and what's not. So the winter is just something that happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: on the commerce side and the science marches. That's a beautifully optimistic, inspiring message.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I agree with you. I think if we look at the key people that work in AI, they work in key scientists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: most disciplines, they continue working out of the box. They continue working out of the box.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: They work in key scientists, most disciplines, they continue working out of the love for science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: No matter the, you can always scrape up some funding to stay alive and they continue working

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: diligently, but there certainly is a huge amount of funding now and there's a concern on the AI side

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and deep learning. There's a concern that we might with over-promising hit another slowdown in funding,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: which does affect the number of students, that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah, it does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So the kind of ideas you had in Michigan to think, did you continue that curiosity through

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the decades that followed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yes, I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: What was your view, historical view of how AI community evolved, the conversations about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the work? Has it persisted the same way from its birth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: No, of course not. It's just, as we were just talking, the symbolic AI really kind of dried up

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and it all became algorithmic. I remember a young AI student telling me what he was doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: and I had been away from the field long enough. I'd gotten involved with complexity at the Santa

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Fe Institute. I thought, algorithms, yeah, they're in the service of, but they're not the main event.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: No, they became the main event. That surprised me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And we all know the downside of this. We all know that if you're using an algorithm to make decisions

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: based on a gazillion human decisions, baked into it are all the mistakes that humans make, the bigotries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the short-sightedness, so on and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: So you mentioned Santa Fe Institute. So you've written the novel Edge of Chaos,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: but it's inspired by the ideas of complexity, a lot of which have been extensively explored

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: at the Santa Fe Institute. It's another fascinating topic of just sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: emergent complexity from chaos. Nobody knows how it happens really, but it seems to wear all the

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: interesting stuff that does happen. So how did first, not your novel, but just complexity in

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: general in the work at Santa Fe fit into the bigger puzzle of the history of AI, or maybe even

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: your personal journey through that? One of the last projects I did

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: concerning AI in particular was looking at the work of Harold Cohen, the painter. And Harold was

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: deeply involved with AI. He was a painter first, and what his project, Aran, which was a lifelong

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: project, did was reflect his own cognitive processes. Harold and I, even though I wrote

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: a book about it, we had a lot of friction between us. And I went, I thought, this is it, the book

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: died, it was published and fell into a ditch. This is it, I'm finished, it's time for me to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: something different. By chance, this was a sabbatical year for my husband, and we spent two months at

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: the Santa Fe Institute and two months at Caltech, and then the spring semester in Munich, Germany.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Okay, those two months at the Santa Fe Institute were so restorative for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The institute was very small then. It was in some kind of office complex on old Santa Fe Trail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Everybody kept their door open. So you could crack your head on a problem, and if you finally

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: didn't get it, you could walk in to see Stuart Kaufman or any number of people and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I don't get this, can you explain? And one of the people that I was talking to about complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: adaptive systems was Murray Gell-Mann. And I told Murray what Harold Cohen had done. And I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: you know, this sounds to me like a complex adaptive system. And he said, yeah, it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Well, what do you know? Harold's errand had all these kissin' cousins all over the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: In science and in economics and so on and so forth. I was so relieved. I thought, okay,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: your instincts are okay. You're doing the right thing. I didn't have the vocabulary. And that

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: was one of the things that the Santa Fe Institute gave me. If I could have rewritten that book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: no, it had just come out. I couldn't rewrite it. I would have had a vocabulary to explain

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: what Aaron was doing. Okay. So I got really interested in what was going on at the Institute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The people were, again, bright and funny and willing to explain anything to this amateur.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: George Cowan, who was then the head of the Institute, said he thought it might be a nice

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: idea if I wrote a book about the Institute. And I thought about it. And I had a book called

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: The

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: God Knows What. And I said, I'm sorry, George. Yeah, I'd really love to do it, but, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: just not going to work for me at this moment. And he said, oh, too bad. I think it would make an

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: interesting book. Well, he was right and I was wrong. I wish I'd done it. But that's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: I hadn't thought about that. That that was a road not taken that I wish I'd taken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Well, you know what? That's just on that point. It's quite brave for you as a writer, as sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: of coming from a world of literature, the literary thinking and historical thinking. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: just from that world and bravely talking to quite, I assume, large egos in AI or in complexity and

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: so on. How'd you do it? Like, where did you? I mean, I suppose they could be intimidated of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: you as well, because it's two different worlds. I don't think I never picked up that anybody was

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: intimidated by me. But how were you brave enough? Where did you find the guts? God, just dumb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: dumb luck. I mean, this is an interesting rock to turn over. I'm going to write a book about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: And, you know, people have enough patience with writers if they think they're going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: end up in a book that they let you flail around and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Well, but they also look if the writer has, there's like, if there's a sparkle in their eye,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: if they get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Yeah, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34

body.input: Right. When were you at the Santa Fe Institute?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pamela McCorduck: Machines Who Think and the Early Days of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #34
